item.content:encoded: B y Dapo Akinrefon An Executive Director (Projects Implementation) of the Federal Housing Authority (FHA), Oluremi Omowaiye, has criticised former President Olusegun Obasanjo over his remarks on President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, alleging that the former president was uncomfortable with the achievements of the current administration. Omowaiye, who defended Tinubu’s economic policies, said Obasanjo was unhappy because the President had achieved what he failed to accomplish during his eight years in office. Obasanjo had criticised the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, arguing that they had pushed many Nigerians deeper into poverty. However, reacting to the former president’s position in a statement on Friday, Omowaiye, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), said Obasanjo should be ashamed of his comments, insisting that Tinubu had surpassed his achievements. “Obasanjo should cover his face in shame. He is unhappy because we have Yoruba man who has done what he failed to do as president. He is uncomfortable because President Tinubu has surpassed his achievements,” he said. The FHA director further alleged that Obasanjo was uncomfortable with Tinubu’s performance because the President was delivering on his promises and could secure another four-year term in 2027. “Obasanjo is unhappy because President Tinubu is delivering on his promises and he knows he is going to achieve much more when he gets reelected for another four years. That is why he is doing everything to stop it but he won’t succeed. “Nigerians are happy with the President’s Renewed Hope agenda and they want him to continue,” Omowaiye said. Questioning Obasanjo’s claim that Tinubu’s reforms had made Nigerians 300 per cent poorer, Omowaiye argued that the former president’s business interests continued to operate despite the economic difficulties he had highlighted. He specifically cited Bells University and Obasanjo Farms, asking whether the former president had shut down either business because of the financial challenges facing Nigerians. “Did he close down Bells University because students are unable to pay? No. Has he closed down Obasanjo Farms because the economy is so bad?” he asked. Omowaiye also cited Next Cash and Carry supermarket, which he described as Nigeria’s biggest single supermarket, arguing that its continued operation after a fire incident demonstrated that businesses could still thrive despite economic challenges. “Peter Obi that Obasanjo is supporting has the biggest single supermarket in Nigeria. It got burnt sometimes ago. He rebuilt it and it is doing fine today. If the economy is so bad, will Next Supermarket be doing fine?” he queried. He also faulted Obasanjo over the state of infrastructure during his presidency, particularly the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, which he described as the country’s most economically viable road. According to him, Obasanjo failed to rehabilitate the road throughout his eight years in office, while the APC administration eventually undertook its reconstruction. “The most economically viable road in Nigeria today is the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. He never fixed that road throughout his eight years. It was the APC government that fixed it,” he said. The FHA director also praised the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway project embarked upon by the Tinubu administration, describing it as the fulfilment of a vision associated with the late nationalist and former Premier of the Western Region, Chief Obafemi Awolowo. “Look at the Coastal road built by the Tinubu administration. It is something that the late sage Obafemi Awolowo envisaged and had a vision for,” he added. On education, Omowaiye contrasted the industrial disputes involving the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) during Obasanjo’s presidency with what he described as industrial stability under Tinubu. He recalled that ASUU embarked on a strike lasting about 10 months in 2001, arguing that such disruptions had become a thing of the past under the current administration. “ASUU strike is a regular thing during the Obasanjo presidency. In 2001, ASUU went on strike for about 10 months. Under President Tinubu, ASUU strike has become a thing of the past,” he said. Defending the economic reforms, Omowaiye acknowledged that the policies had caused hardship but maintained that they were necessary to reposition Nigeria for sustainable growth and prosperity. He expressed confidence that the current difficulties would ease, insisting that the country was already beginning to experience the benefits of the reforms. “These reforms by President Tinubu are painful but they are needed for Nigeria to be productive and prosperous. Today, we are already seeing the results and the pains will soon be a thing of the past,” he said. Citing what he described as improvements in key economic indicators, Omowaiye claimed that inflation had declined from above 20 per cent to 14 per cent, while the price of a bag of rice had dropped from more than N100,000 to between N50,000 and N57,000. He also defended the government’s decision to float the naira, saying predictions that the dollar would exchange for as much as N10,000 had not materialised. “Today, the inflation rate has dropped from over 20 percent to 14 percent now. For agriculture, a bag of rice that was over N100,000 is now N50,000. “When President Tinubu floated the naira, some economists predicted that the naira will exchange for N10,000 but today a dollar is N1,300. Today, our economy is improving and investors are coming into the country,” he said. Omowaiye urged Nigerians to support the Tinubu administration, maintaining that its Renewed Hope agenda was beginning to yield positive results. item.title: 2027: ‘Embrace Senator Orji Kalu’s adoption as consensus candidate’, Cleric tells Abia North aspirants
item.description: Bishop Silas Eke of the Kingly People’s Assembly has commended the people of Abia State, particularly political and community stakeholders in Abia North Senatorial District, for the remarkable demonstration of unity in adopting Senator Orji Uzor Kalu as their consensus candidate for the 2027 senatorial election. The cleric urged other aspirants seeking to represent Abia North in the Senate to accept the adoption of the former governor in good faith, congratulate him and join hands with other stakeholders in advancing the collective interests of the senatorial district. Eke noted that the development of Abia North should take precedence over individual political ambitions, stressing that unity among stakeholders was essential to attracting greater federal presence and accelerating the socioeconomic development of the district. “I sincerely appreciate the people of Abia State, particularly Abia North, for the unity they have demonstrated. Our collective development must remain paramount. Those aspiring to represent the district should embrace the adoption of Senator Orji Uzor Kalu in good faith and congratulate him,” Eke said. The bishop expressed optimism that Kalu’s return to the Senate would yield greater developmental benefits for Abia North and the Igbo nation, identifying the establishment of federal universities, healthcare institutions, reconstruction of quality roads, housing development and attraction of business investments as areas deserving further attention. Eke also expressed support for the vision concerning Kalu attributed to the Leader of INRI Evangelical Spiritual Church, Primate Elijah Ayodele, maintaining that Abia North stood to benefit from the opportunities envisaged by the prominent cleric. He emphasised that the ultimate measure of political leadership should be its impact on the lives of ordinary citizens and the opportunities it creates for future generations. Speaking on Kalu’s ongoing ward-to-ward tour of Abia North, Bishop Eke disclosed that he had been closely following the senator’s engagements across the various communities, describing the exercise as an exemplary approach to grassroots representation and public accountability. “I have followed his ward-to-ward engagements with keen interest. Returning to the people to render an account of stewardship, listen to their concerns and identify their priorities is an important aspect of effective representation,” he stated. Today, citizens are demanding more from their representatives because they have seen what is possible,” he said. Beyond infrastructural development, Bishop Eke highlighted Kalu’s investment in education and human capital development, stating that more than 60 beneficiaries had received opportunities for overseas scholarships and professional training through the senator’s initiatives. He also cited the construction of school buildings, distribution of educational materials, installation of solar-powered streetlights and other community-based interventions as significant aspects of Kalu’s stewardship. “From road construction to education and human capital development, we have witnessed interventions that deserve recognition. Investing in people is equally as important as building physical infrastructure,” the bishop added. Eke maintained that political cooperation should translate into tangible benefits for the people, including improved access to healthcare, quality education, employment opportunities, infrastructure and an enabling environment for businesses to thrive. The cleric thanked traditional rulers, community leaders, political stakeholders, women and youths across Abia North for their commitment to peaceful political engagement. He urged stakeholders to sustain the prevailing spirit of unity, accommodate differing political views and place the long-term development of Abia North above personal and partisan considerations. item.title: Rohit Sharma back as MI captain for IPL 2027: Inside story of how Mumbai Indians convinced 'Hitman' to take over from Hardik Pandya
item.description: Rohit Sharma back as MI captain for IPL 2027: Inside story of how Mumbai Indians convinced 'Hitman' to take over from Hardik Pandya originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Mumbai Indians have officially named Rohit Sharma captain for IPL 2027. Rohit first suggested Tilak Varma, but the franchise asked him to lead again. Kieron Pollard’s new support staff includes Uthappa, McClenaghan, Dilip and Kulkarni, all reportedly close to Rohit. MI captain for IPL 2027: Rohit Sharma officially takes over captaincy from Hardik Pandya Rohit Sharma is the Mumbai Indians captain again. The franchise confirmed the appointment on Friday evening, ending three seasons under Hardik Pandya and handing the job back to the man who won them all five of their titles. Mumbai announced it on their social channels with the line “Smile, everybody smile 💙 #MumbaiIndians #CaptainRo”, at 5:45 p.m. IST in a nod to the number 45 Rohit wore through his years at the club. Smile, everybody smile 💙 #MumbaiIndians #CaptainRo pic.twitter.com/YUqYZTQxu9 — Mumbai Indians (@mipaltan) November 27, 2026 The Indian Express had reported earlier in the month that the five-time champions were likely to make the change, and that Rohit had agreed to it after the franchise approached him. The decision did not come as a surprise, particularly because Mumbai have carried out a complete overhaul of their support staff over the past fortnight. A change at the top of the dressing room was widely expected to follow, and the franchise has settled on the most familiar name available to it. It is understood that Mumbai wanted Rohit to take over from Pandya midway through the last IPL, at a time when the team was in dire straits. The change is now formal, with the mini-auction in Goa on December 16. Why Mumbai Indians decided to replace Hardik Pandya as captain The results under Pandya’s leadership gave the franchise little reason to wait. Mumbai lost 10 of their 14 games last season, finished ninth in the table and stretched their wait for a title to six years, which is a long drought by their own standards. Across the three seasons he led them, Pandya captained Mumbai in 39 matches and won 15 of them. Rohit’s own record in the job reads 87 wins from 158 matches, with five titles and five wins from five finals, three of those against Chennai Super Kings. According to Express, Suryakumar Yadav and Jasprit Bumrah have been part of the setup for a long time, so a fresh face was certainly possible. The franchise instead went back to Rohit, as they allegedly believe that the 39-year-old is the best person to lead in the next edition, with a mega auction soon to follow in 2028. item.content:encoded: Rohit Sharma back as MI captain for IPL 2027: Inside story of how Mumbai Indians convinced 'Hitman' to take over from Hardik Pandya originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Mumbai Indians have officially named Rohit Sharma captain for IPL 2027. Rohit first suggested Tilak Varma, but the franchise asked him to lead again. Kieron Pollard’s new support staff includes Uthappa, McClenaghan, Dilip and Kulkarni, all reportedly close to Rohit. MI captain for IPL 2027: Rohit Sharma officially takes over captaincy from Hardik Pandya Rohit Sharma is the Mumbai Indians captain again. The franchise confirmed the appointment on Friday evening, ending three seasons under Hardik Pandya and handing the job back to the man who won them all five of their titles. Mumbai announced it on their social channels with the line “Smile, everybody smile 💙 #MumbaiIndians #CaptainRo”, at 5:45 p.m. IST in a nod to the number 45 Rohit wore through his years at the club. Smile, everybody smile 💙 #MumbaiIndians #CaptainRo pic.twitter.com/YUqYZTQxu9 — Mumbai Indians (@mipaltan) November 27, 2026 The Indian Express had reported earlier in the month that the five-time champions were likely to make the change, and that Rohit had agreed to it after the franchise approached him. The decision did not come as a surprise, particularly because Mumbai have carried out a complete overhaul of their support staff over the past fortnight. A change at the top of the dressing room was widely expected to follow, and the franchise has settled on the most familiar name available to it. It is understood that Mumbai wanted Rohit to take over from Pandya midway through the last IPL, at a time when the team was in dire straits. The change is now formal, with the mini-auction in Goa on December 16. Why Mumbai Indians decided to replace Hardik Pandya as captain The results under Pandya’s leadership gave the franchise little reason to wait. Mumbai lost 10 of their 14 games last season, finished ninth in the table and stretched their wait for a title to six years, which is a long drought by their own standards. Across the three seasons he led them, Pandya captained Mumbai in 39 matches and won 15 of them. Rohit’s own record in the job reads 87 wins from 158 matches, with five titles and five wins from five finals, three of those against Chennai Super Kings. According to Express, Suryakumar Yadav and Jasprit Bumrah have been part of the setup for a long time, so a fresh face was certainly possible. Tilak Varma, who is regarded as a future leader, was a natural choice as well if the team wanted to look ahead of 2027. The franchise instead went back to Rohit, as they allegedly believe that the 39-year-old is the best person to lead in the next edition, with a mega auction soon to follow in 2028. How Mumbai Indians convinced Rohit Sharma to take the captaincy again Rohit, it seems, did not push for the job himself, and he first named Tilak as the person who should lead the side. “Rohit initially had suggested Tilak Varma’s name but the franchise has requested him to take over captaincy which he has now agreed,” the source told Express. The source also described the extent to which the former captain was involved in the planning. “There were a series of talks that had happened before he flew to New Zealand and Rohit’s suggestions were sought during appointment of new coaches as well,” he added. Tilak is expected to be named his deputy, although Mumbai have not confirmed the vice-captaincy alongside the captaincy announcement. Hardik Pandya has left Mumbai Indians for Punjab Kings in the Arshdeep Singh trade The question of what Pandya would do under a new captain has already been settled. He has been traded to Punjab Kings in a straight swap for Arshdeep Singh, with both players valued at INR 18 crore and nobody else involved in the deal. RevSportz reported that Mumbai held talks with Pandya in June, August and September, and that four options were on the table. Kolkata Knight Riders offered Cameron Green and a fast bowler, Rajasthan Royals offered Yashasvi Jaiswal, Punjab offered Arshdeep, and the fourth was for Pandya to stay one more season before the mega auction. The franchise attracted heavy criticism when it appointed Pandya as captain after an all-cash trade from Gujarat Titans before the 2024 season, and the crowd at the Wankhede Stadium booed him repeatedly during home games. His exit removes the awkwardness of a replaced captain sharing a dressing room with his successor. Why Rohit Sharma is the right captain for Mumbai Indians in IPL 2027 The decision to turn back to Rohit Sharma looks sensible, because it matches both the team’s recent results and the changes made behind the scenes. A ninth-place finish and 10 defeats in 14 games left the franchise with little room to continue as before, and the dressing room needed a leader who commands instant respect. Rohit’s record speaks for itself, and the fact that he had to be persuaded rather than the other way around is a pleasing detail. His early suggestion of Tilak Varma shows that he is thinking about the team’s future, and a season or two under his guidance could be the ideal preparation phase for the youngster. The reunion with Kieron Pollard and the arrival of Robin Uthappa, Mitchell McClenaghan, T Dilip and Dhawal Kulkarni also give the setup a familiar flavour, which could help the squad settle quickly after a disappointing campaign. The challenge now is the squad rather than the dressing room. Mumbai go to the auction with nine places to fill, Arshdeep Singh replacing Pandya as the headline name, and a side that has not reached a final since 2020. Mumbai will still need results to back up the story, but the plan makes sense. item.description: Manchester United are error-prone, leaky at the back, and desperately short of confidence as they face the growing nightmare of a Premier League relegation battle. Talk of the Red Devils going down still appears fanciful, but analysts at Opta say they have a 27 percent chance of dropping into the Championship as they prepare to host impressive Brentford. At the top end of the table, Manchester City’s match at Arsenal appears to be a must-win for Enzo Maresca’s team, who have fallen off the pace after a barren spell. Manchester United’s Dutch forward #11 Joshua Zirkzee (C) and teammates react to their defeat on the pitch after the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Manchester United on November 22, 2026. Following their 2-2 draw, United had conceded the most goals (36), the most penalties (five), and had received the most red cards (five) of any Premier League team this season across all competitions. Chelsea’s Wobbly Defence Manchester United’s Argentinian head coach Mauricio Pochettino (L) speaks with Manchester United’s Spanish goalkeeping coach Toni Jimenez (R) on the pitch after the English Premier League football match(Photo by PAUL ELLIS / AFP) | PAUL ELLIS / AFP Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea started the season as the swashbuckling entertainers of the Premier League, but defensive problems are threatening to derail them. He won five IPL titles in 11 seasons before Hardik Pandya replaced him in 2024. Full timeline of how Rohit lost the MI captaincy and won it back. MI have brought in Kieron Pollard and Robin Uthappa, both of whom played alongside Rohit at the franchise, as part of a wider coaching overhaul. MORE: The Hardik-Arshdeep trade: Who stands to gain? MI or PBKS? Timeline of how Rohit Sharma lost the Mumbai Indians captaincy and won it back Rohit's two spells either side of the Pandya years cover 14 seasons of MI cricket. Here is how the captaincy changed hands and what pushed it back in his direction. 2013: Rohit Sharma replaces Ricky Ponting and wins Mumbai Indians their first IPL title Rohit was handed the captaincy midway through the 2013 season after Ricky Ponting, who had won three and lost three of his six matches in charge, dropped himself from the side and gave up the role. MI went on a run under their new captain and reached the final in Kolkata, where they beat Chennai Super Kings by 23 runs for the franchise's first title. Kieron Pollard's 60 not out off 32 balls won him the player of the match award. MORE: New MI coach calls themselves 'underdogs' ahead of IPL 2027 season 2015 to 2020: Four more IPL trophies make Rohit Sharma the most successful captain Rohit added titles in 2015, 2017, 2019, and 2020, two of them by a single run. MI beat CSK by 41 runs in the 2015 final, edged Rising Pune Supergiant by one run in 2017, beat CSK by one run in 2019, and saw off Delhi Capitals by five wickets in Dubai in 2020. Those five trophies are the most by any IPL captain. By the end of the 2020 campaign, MI had become the first side to win back-to-back titles in nine years, and Rohit's standing at the franchise looked permanent. IPL 2021 to 2023: Rohit Sharma's returns dry up and the Mumbai Indians slip The run of trophies stopped abruptly. MI finished fifth in 2021 and missed the playoffs on net run rate, then came last in 2022 with four wins from 14 matches after losing their first eight games of the season. Rohit's own form fell away at the same time. He made 381 runs at 29.30 in 2021, 268 runs at 19.14 in 2022 and 332 runs at 20.75 in 2023, with a single fifty across the first two of those seasons. The 2023 campaign brought a fourth-place finish and a run to Qualifier 2, which papered over the batting numbers. It turned out to be his last season in charge. MORE: MI retention list for IPL 2027: Retained and released players March 2024: Mumbai Indians sack Rohit Sharma and appoint Hardik Pandya as captain MI brought Pandya back from Gujarat Titans in the trade window and then took the decision that shaped the next three years, removing Rohit as captain and handing the role to the all-rounder. The call drew an immediate backlash from supporters, who objected both to the sacking of a five-time champion and to the manner of it. Pandya was booed by MI's own fans at the Wankhede Stadium during the season that followed. IPL 2024 to 2026: Hardik Pandya's three seasons brought only one playoff finish MI finished last in 2024 with four wins from 14 matches. They recovered to finish fourth in 2025 and reach the playoffs, which suggested the arrangement was settling down. The 2026 season undid that. MI won four of 14 and finished ninth, where the second side was eliminated, and suffered their heaviest IPL defeat by runs when CSK beat them by 103. Pandya missed games through unavailability, with Suryakumar Yadav and Jasprit Bumrah standing in. Reports of a breakdown between Pandya and the senior players ran through the campaign. Rohit, restricted to nine matches, made 283 runs at 35.38 with a strike rate of 157.22, having passed 400 in each of the previous two seasons. MORE: SKY targets IPL 2027 title with MI after ‘lucky’ meeting with PM Modi November 2026: Hardik Pandya's exit to Punjab Kings clears the way for Rohit Sharma MI traded Pandya to Punjab Kings for Arshdeep Singh, a straight swap with both players valued at INR 18 crore and nobody else involved in the deal. RevSportz's Boria Majumdar reported that MI had held talks with Pandya in June, August, and September, leaving four routes open to them. Kolkata Knight Riders offered Cameron Green and a fast bowler, Rajasthan Royals offered Yashasvi Jaiswal, Punjab offered Arshdeep, and the fourth option was for Pandya to stay one more season before the mega-auction. With Punjab's offer accepted, the captaincy slot became vacant. And now, after a few weeks, MI appointed Sharma as their skipper again. Rohit returns as MI skipper. item.title: NFL playoff picture: What does the Bills’ win over the Chiefs mean for AFC standings?
item.description: (Photo by Ryan Kang/Getty Images) | Getty Images Update: Buffalo’s dramatic win over Kansas City on Thanksgiving night kept the Bills atop the AFC standings, and Buffalo is now two games ahead of No. 2 seed Denver for the moment. Kansas City remains in the No. 5 spot, and the Chiefs are one game behind the Broncos in the loss column for the moment. Two AFC titans renew their rivalry on Thanksgiving night, when Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. With both teams near the top of the AFC standings, this game has serious playoff implications for both teams and the AFC as a whole. Let’s dive into the playoff scenarios for both the Bills and the Chiefs ahead of this game. AFC playoff standings Here is the AFC standings ahead of Week 12: 1. Buffalo Bills (9-1) 2. Denver Broncos (8-2) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) 4. Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) 5. Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) 6. Cleveland Browns (6-4) 7. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4) 8. New England Patriots (5-5) 9. Houston Texans (4-6) 10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-7) 11. Baltimore Ravens (4-7) 12. New York Jets (3-8) 13. Indianapolis Colts (3-8) 14. Los Angeles Chargers (1-9) 15. Miami Dolphins (1-9) 16. Tennessee Titans (1-9) Buffalo Bills playoff picture With a 9-1 record, the Bills sit atop the AFC standings and in position for the No. 1 seed in the conference, as well as the lone bye week. Buffalo also has a comfortable four-game lead over the New England Patriots in the AFC East, but New England won their meeting earlier this season. Should Buffalo win on Thursday night, the Bills would improve to 10-1 and maintain control of the top spot in the conference. A loss, however, would drop Buffalo down to the No. 2 line, and put Kansas City in control of the top seed, at least for the moment. Kansas City Chiefs playoff picture If the NFL playoffs began today, the Kansas City Chiefs would be in, but as the No. 5 seed in the AFC. Why? That comes down to tiebreakers. The Chiefs are tied with the Denver Broncos with an 8-2 record, and those two teams have already split their season series. Since both teams are 3-1 in AFC West games, under the league’s tiebreaking procedures, the next step is win-loss-tied percentage in common games. Both teams have defeated the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Chiefs lost to the Seattle Seahawks, a team the Broncos beat. So for the moment, the Broncos are ahead in the AFC West, and they take the No. 2 spot. However, the Chiefs would not only take control of the top spot in the division, but they would move to the top spot in the AFC overall with a win on Thursday night. That would pull Kansas City level with Buffalo, and the Chiefs would have a head-to-head tiebreaker advantage over the Bills with the victory. With a loss, the Chiefs would remain in the No. 5 spot. They would not be in danger of sliding down further, as both the Cleveland Browns and the Pittsburgh Steelers — the teams at No. 6 and No. 7 right now — are 6-4. But the Chiefs would be

Buffalo also has a comfortable four-game lead over the New England Patriots in the AFC East, but New England won their meeting earlier this season. Should Buffalo win on Thursday night, the Bills would improve to 10-1 and maintain control of the top spot in the conference. A loss, however, would drop Buffalo down to the No. 2 line, and put Kansas City in control of the top seed, at least for the moment. Kansas City Chiefs playoff picture If the NFL playoffs began today, the Kansas City Chiefs would be in, but as the No. 5 seed in the AFC. Why? That comes down to tiebreakers. The Chiefs are tied with the Denver Broncos with an 8-2 record, and those two teams have already split their season series. Since both teams are 3-1 in AFC West games, under the league’s tiebreaking procedures, the next step is win-loss-tied percentage in common games. Both teams have defeated the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Chiefs lost to the Seattle Seahawks, a team the Broncos beat. So for the moment, the Broncos are ahead in the AFC West, and they take the No. 2 spot. However, the Chiefs would not only take control of the top spot in the division, but they would move to the top spot in the AFC overall with a win on Thursday night. That would pull Kansas City level with Buffalo, and the Chiefs would have a head-to-head tiebreaker advantage over the Bills with the victory. With a loss, the Chiefs would remain in the No. 5 spot. They would not be in danger of sliding down further, as both the Cleveland Browns and the Pittsburgh Steelers — the teams at No. 6 and No. 7 right now — are 6-4. But the Chiefs would be on the wrong end of the head-to-head tiebreaker with Buffalo. Tiebreaker implications The winner of this game will have a head-to-head tiebreaker advantage, which is the first step in deciding tiebreakers between division winners when it comes to seeding.

item.description: Celtics Face Fascinating Three-Day Stretch That Could Reveal Plenty About Their Progress originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics return from their Thanksgiving break Friday evening with an interesting stretch of basketball awaiting them. Boston will host the Atlanta Hawks before traveling to San Antonio for a Sunday afternoon game against the Spurs. The two contests provide head coach Joe Mazzulla with opportunities to evaluate his team against considerably different opponents. Boston entered the holiday following Tuesday's 131-116 victory over the Washington Wizards. While that result provided some much-needed momentum, the upcoming weekend could offer a more meaningful indication of where the Celtics stand as November concludes. Atlanta Offers Boston An Opportunity To Establish Consistency The Celtics' first assignment involves taking advantage of a home game against Atlanta. Boston has experienced some inconsistent performances during the opening portion of the season, making Friday an important opportunity to establish a more dependable foundation. Superstar 🌟 https://t.co/nyv08X3W4q — Boston Celtics (@celtics) November 25, 2026 One of the most important objectives involves maintaining offensive organization throughout four quarters. The Celtics possess enough individual talent to create significant scoring runs, but consistently generating quality opportunities becomes particularly valuable against opponents capable of responding with runs of their own. Friday's NBA Cup game also introduces additional competitive significance. The Celtics have an opportunity to finish their group-stage responsibilities while building momentum before another challenging road stretch. Boston's ability to create opportunities without relying exclusively on difficult individual scoring possessions could become particularly important. The Celtics will have limited preparation time before Sunday's afternoon contest, making their ability to adjust particularly interesting. item.title: McInnes tempers 'anxiety' as Rangers seek top spot
item.description: Ryan Naderi has netted some crucial goals for Derek McInnes this term [SNS] Derek McInnes says Rangers should not experience any anxiety about the prospect of going top of the Scottish Premiership as the Ibrox side look to extend their four-match winning run. Rangers host in-form Falkirk on Saturday (15:00 GMT), who have won six on the bounce in the league, and victory would move McInnes' team top before leaders Celtic travel to face Hearts on Sunday. "I don't think there should be anxiety when you're trying to go top of the league at all," McInnes said. "Obviously, you want to be top of the league come the end of the season. "If you've got an opportunity to go there, it's important you try and take it." Ryan Naderi netted an early second-half equaliser then set up Djeidi Gassama as Rangers turned a 1-0 deficit into a 3-1 lead before Aberdeen scored a consolation in Tuesday's Premiership match at Ibrox. It was Naderi's 11th goal of the season and McInnes spoke of his awareness of the now Czech Republic international last season while managing Hearts, who have used a data analytics firm for much of their recent recruitment. "Last January, obviously, when we first saw that Rangers were linked with Naderi, like everything else, I would say to [Hearts sporting director] Graeme Jones, 'how do they rate him?' "Because you're always curious, it's just the way it is. It's brilliant when you see other teams round about you signing a player that's not rated! "He was someone that I think was well known to them. Brugge had an interest in Ryan, I think, and I think USG potentially had an interest in him as well but the kind of money, the fee, it just went away from them. "The feeling was that he could help Rangers and make them better. "I had a good conversation with Ryan when I first came in the door and what we felt this season could look like for him. "He's stood up brilliantly to the injuries to Youssef [Chermiti] and Lawrence [Shankland] and he's had to be the guy. He's led the line brilliantly and I love the goals he scores. All top strikers have intelligence to be in the right place at the right time." "These conversations that I have with Jim [Gillespie, chief executive] on a regular basis about players that we should be speaking to and trying to address and secure and give them a wee bit more security and a wee bit more comfort for us, these conversations, I think, have been ongoing," McInnes said. "The club's well aware of what needs to be done and what we shouldn't be doing and Ryan's been part of that conversation." item.title: Ducks’ Dylan Raiola issues warning about Washington’s motives ahead of Saturday’s rivalry game
item.description: In October, the Oregon Ducks started former walk-on Brock Thomas over Dylan Raiola against the Nebraska Cornhuskers, the program Raiola left after two seasons as its starter. On Wednesday at the Hatfield-Dowlin Complex, Raiola met reporters as Oregon’s starting quarterback heading into his first game against the Washington Huskies, with the Ducks riding a four-game winning streak. Raiola entered that Oct. 17 game at the start of the fourth quarter with Oregon down 14-6 and threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Jamari Johnson with 28 seconds left for a 17-14 win. June 2, 2022; Tempe, Arizona; USA; Chandler quarterback Dylan Raiola throws during a 7-on-7 tournament, an ASU High School Football Showcase. High School Football Asu High School Football Showcase No. 24 Washington comes to Autzen Stadium on Saturday night at 7-4 overall and 4-4 in the Big Ten. The No. 12 Ducks are 8-3 and 6-2, and a win keeps their Big Ten title game hopes alive. “I promise you Washington wants nothing more to come in here and throw a dent in what we got going on. So, we gotta come with it. I know my guys will, and honestly, they’ll probably throw some punches, too. So, we gotta be ready for a heavyweight fight,” Raiola told reporters . He said the Huskies had been sending the “no love lost” message all week, and that Oregon acknowledged it early before turning to preparation. He also said Oregon still regards Washington as a strong team despite the rivalry, and he expects the noise to fall away once the ball is kicked off. “All the emotion, all the hate, everything’s just like ‘All right, it’s football now,'” Raiola said , according to Oregon Ducks On SI’s Chris Wuensch. item.title: Big 12 Conference Championship Game: How Texas Tech clinched a berth
item.description: (Photo by Jocelyn Rafidi/Baylor Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) Update: With a win over TCU on Thanksgiving night, Texas. Tech clinched a spot in the Big 12 Championship Game against Utah. Rivalry Week is upon us. While some teams are already looking ahead to the College Football Playoff, others are hoping to play spoiler during Rivalry Week. But that proposition has taken on greater importance this year, with the impending move to a 24-team playoff next season. That means these are the last round of Conference Championship Games, so denying a rival a spot in the title game might mean even more this year. In the Big 12, unbeaten Utah has already clinched a spot in the title game. But who will the Utes face: No. 11 Texas Tech, or No. 10 BYU? How Texas Tech can clinch a spot The Red Raiders have the inside track to a spot in the Big 12 title game, and a date with Utah. With a win over TCU on Thanksgiving night, then Texas Tech will clinch the second spot in the Big 12 Championship Game. However, the Red Raiders can still get in if they lose to TCU, provided BYU loses to Cincinnati on Saturday afternoon. How BYU can clinch a spot BYU hosts Cincinnati on Saturday afternoon, but the Cougars might already be eliminated before kickoff. To advance to the Big 12 title game, BYU needs Texas Tech to lose to TCU on Thursday night, and then a win over Cincinnati on Saturday.

item.title: Florida State loses only 2027 running back commit as Jayden Miles flips to Missouri
item.description: The Florida State Seminoles played last Saturday’s 28-10 loss to the NC State Wolfpack with former walk-on Zay Parks taking every running back snap. On Thanksgiving, their 2027 recruiting class lost its only running back commitment as well. Four-star back Jayden Miles of Baton Rouge (La.) Catholic flipped his pledge from Florida State to the Missouri Tigers, Kolby Crawford reported for 247Sports on Thursday. The 6-foot-2, 203-pound Miles had been committed to the Seminoles since June, when he picked them over the Ohio State Buckeyes. His recruitment reopened Nov. 1, the day Florida State fired Mike Norvell and handed the program to interim coach Rick Stockstill. The LSU Tigers, his hometown school, moved first, hosting Miles for an unofficial visit Nov. 7 and an official visit the following weekend. Missouri extended its offer later in November and brought him to Columbia for an official visit last weekend. NEWS: Four-star RB Jayden Miles has flipped his commitment from Florida State to Missouri, @247Sports has learned. Story: https://t.co/yX7jB1QzaU https://t.co/AmrIOX3M5C — Kolby Crawford (@kolby_crawford) November 26, 2026 Sep 21, 2024; Tallahassee, Florida, USA; Florida State Seminoles head coach Mike Norvell and associate head coach Odell Haggins high-five after winning against the California Golden Bears at Doak S. Campbell Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Melina Myers-Imagn Images Both of Missouri’s moves landed while Florida State was still searching for a permanent head coach. The Seminoles hired Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann on Nov. 23, after Missouri’s official visit had already taken place. By then, the program that had held his commitment for five months had gone 22 days without a full-time head coach to make its case. 247Sports ranks Miles as the No. 17 running back nationally and the No. 13 prospect in Louisiana, while the 247Sports Composite, which blends the major recruiting services, places him No. 27 at the position. His commitment arrived less than a week before the early signing period opens on Dec. 2. Florida State’s running back problem now stretches into 2027 Schumann’s first 2027 class holds 13 commitments, none at running back, and sits No. 70 in the 247Sports team rankings with the signing window about to open. Florida State has also played this season without its top five preseason running backs, which is how Parks ended up carrying the full load against NC State. Schumann now needs help at the position on the current depth chart and on the recruiting board at the same time, and the board just lost the one back it had. Missouri, meanwhile, comes away with its first flip of the 2027 cycle. Miles becomes the Tigers’ second running back commitment in the class, joining four-star Kingston Miles, which gives Missouri two four-star backs who share a last name heading into signing week. LSU had Miles on campus twice in November, including an official visit one weekend before Missouri’s, and he still picked a program

item.title: What DJ Jacobs’ family said about Ohio State visits before five-star EDGE’s decommitment
item.description: The highest-rated player in the Ohio State Buckeyes’ 2027 recruiting class backed off his commitment on Thanksgiving, two days before the Buckeyes host the Michigan Wolverines and six days before the early signing period opens. Five-star edge rusher David “DJ” Jacobs of Blessed Trinity Catholic in Roswell, Georgia, confirmed the decision Thursday to Rivals’ Hayes Fawcett , who lists him as the No. 1 recruit in the class. Jacobs had been committed since Dec. 29, 2025, when he picked Ohio State live on CBS Sports HQ over finalists the Miami Hurricanes and Texas A&M Aggies. When DJ showed up at a Georgia Bulldogs home game against Western Kentucky in September, his father, former Georgia defensive lineman David Jacobs, described the trip as a visit for younger brother Dawson, a 2028 defensive line prospect, and drew a firm line around DJ’s own travel. item.title: Chelsea’s chances of landing £100m dream midfield target in January rated by the Athletic
item.description: Chelsea’s chances of landing £100m dream midfield target in January rated by the Athletic Chelsea’s interest in Alex Scott is well reported – but how likely are they to actually be able to land him in January? If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. The Athletic’s “Deal Sheet” summary of Chelsea’s potential transfer business says that the Blues could sign players in a number of positions. But there’s nowhere with more need than central midfield, and there’s no player more heavily linked than Alex Scott of Bournemouth. Fans shouldn’t get too excited, however. The article claims that Chelsea are “wary they could face competition” for the midfielder and “believe they may have to wait until the summer.” Chelsea face tough battle to land in-demand central midfielder Alex Scott (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Earlier in the year it felt like the fact that Bournemouth had made a slow start made it possible they would want to hold on to their key player until the summer to ensure they stayed clear of relegation. Now the opposite is true – they’re on a superb run and may instead want to keep him to see just how high in the table they can finish. The Blues also aren’t offering a very tempting destination right now. There’s bound to be competition from other teams, and another year of chaos at Chelsea might not be what a player pushing to get into the England team wants to sign up for. In other news… Emmanuel Emegha is in the mix for tonight’s game and we expect him to start. Xabi Alonso had some words about what he can offer the team. The injury report for tonight’s game has one vital starter confirmed as back – but two regulars will still be missing.

item.title: Fashola says election riggers deserve jail, not death
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has said people who manipulate election results should face imprisonment rather than execution, urging Nigerians to reject violent rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. Fashola made the remarks during a television interview on Friday while reacting to the “rig and die” statement attributed to Ovie Omo-Agege, a Delta Central senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress. The former Minister of Works and Housing said electoral offences must be punished under the law, arguing that even where an offence attracts capital punishment, the accused must first be charged, tried and given an opportunity to defend themselves. “Absolutely not. I mean, come on. I think we must move away from what I think are extreme narratives and rhetoric,” Fashola said when asked whether election riggers should be killed. He stressed that the Electoral Act does not prescribe death as punishment for election rigging. “The punishment under the Electoral Act is not death. And even if it were death, which I will not support, there’s a process before you take human life; a charge, a trial, an opportunity to defend yourself,” he said. Fashola, however, maintained that election manipulation should attract serious punishment and urged politicians to seek votes through legitimate campaigns. “The penalty for rigging is not death. But don’t rig. Go and campaign for your party,” he added. He advised political parties to concentrate on mobilising voters in areas where they enjoy support rather than attempting to manipulate results in places where they have little electoral influence. The former governor also advocated stiffer prison sentences for serious electoral offences, suggesting that some violations should carry custodial penalties without the option of a fine. “I think maybe there might be stiffer sentences without the option of a fine, maybe a defined custodial sentence that is deterrent in nature,” he said. Fashola further called for greater public education on electoral conduct, noting that Nigeria had repeatedly amended its electoral laws without giving sufficient attention to educating citizens about the principles of democracy. He said sustained nationwide enlightenment would help reduce desperation during elections and encourage politicians and voters to understand that electoral contests could produce either winners or losers. The post Fashola says election riggers deserve jail, not death appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Texas Tech follows 2025 blueprint into final Big 12 championship game against unbeaten Utah
item.description: The Texas Tech Red Raiders opened 2025 with six straight wins, dropped their seventh game on the road and did not lose again on the way to the program’s first Big 12 title. The 2026 team has followed that route almost step for step, and it now ends at the Big 12 Championship Game against the No. 2 Utah Utes on Dec. 4. Tech locked up its spot Thursday night in Lubbock with a 48-27 win over the TCU Horned Frogs, a result that also ended the BYU Cougars’ hopes of returning to Arlington. Thomas Castellanos completed 20 of 25 passes for a career-high 374 yards and three touchdowns, two of them in a four-play span late in the first half. Oct 11, 2025; Lubbock, Texas, USA; A general view of Texas Tech Red Raiders helmets in the second half on the bench during the game against the Kansas Jayhawks at Jones AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Michael C. Johnson-Imagn Images TCU, playing its first game since firing Sonny Dykes on Sunday, led 10-0 after one quarter while Tech went three-and-out on its first two possessions. The Red Raiders outscored the Frogs 48-17 from there, turning two second-quarter turnovers into 10 points and scoring touchdowns on their first three drives of the second half. After a 6-0 start this fall, Tech lost 37-24 at the Cincinnati Bearcats on Oct. 24. The 2025 team took its only regular-season loss in the same spot, 26-22 at the Arizona State Sun Devils in game seven, and answered by winning its last five regular-season games before beating BYU for the conference crown. This group has now won five straight since Cincinnati, finishing 11-1 overall and 8-1 in league play. Texas Tech gets one shot at the last Big 12 title game The Big 12 announced that this year’s game will be the final edition, with the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams in 2027 and the league’s automatic bid moving to its regular-season champion. Whoever wins in Arlington will be the last team to lift that trophy. Utah is unbeaten in Morgan Scalley’s first season as head coach at his alma mater. The Utes clinched their spot with a win at TCU on Nov. 21 and entered that game riding a 16-game winning streak, the longest active run in FBS. They also beat BYU in their rivalry game on Nov. 7, and the Cougars entered this week as the only team besides Tech still alive for the second spot, needing a win over Cincinnati and a Tech loss. A win would make Tech the first team to win consecutive Big 12 title games since the Oklahoma Sooners won four straight from 2017 to 2020. It would also make Joey McGuire’s program the final champion of a game the league first played in 1996, in what will be its 25th and last edition. item.title: Gaming The System: IU Indy's hot start
item.description: If you're unfamiliar with IU Indy (formerly and forever in my heart known as IUPUI), Ben Howlett and The System, let me introduce you. The System means running. A lot. Howlett presses the entire game, sprints out in transition, and frequently runs full hockey-style five-player line changes to keep his guys fresh. I recommend this piece by Sam Federman from last summer for a deeper dive, but the ten-second version above should get the point across. The System debuted at the D-I level last year, but it doesn't come from Howlett. He played and then coached at West Liberty University under the brains behind the operation, the legendary Jim Crutchfield. Howlett, though, was the first to workshop it at the top level of the college game. In year one, there were signs of life, but they were relatively few and far between. The Jaguars went 7-25 (3-17 Horizon League), a three-win decrease from the one and only season under Paul Corsaro. They finished 317th at KenPom, an improvement over their 354th spot in preseason projections but nevertheless a mild drop from 312th under Corsaro. So far this year, it's been a different story. The Jags have four wins in seven games and have jumped from 316th preseason in KenPom to 275th in the season's first month. They led Penn State for nearly 25 minutes before ultimately losing by seven. They've won three of four against the four D-I teams within 100 spots of them at KenPom, either way, including a win over UT-Martin, an OVC favorite. And Howlett has accomplished it by doing something he may have never thought he'd do: slow down. Not all the way, but enough. The changes by the numbers Don't get me wrong, this team still runs. If you saw the Jags last season and you've watched them this November, it probably looks nearly indiscernible play by play. They still press full court for 40 minutes. The hockey subs still come into play. Their games are still track meets: in seven contests, neither IU Indy nor their opponent has scored below 70 points even once. But a look at the underlying numbers shows some distinct changes, most of which have had a positive effect early on. First and foremost is the pace. The 25-26 iteration of the Jaguars played 74.6 possessions per game, the highest in the country. This season, they're at 70.6 possessions, an unremarkable number that has them in the 67th %ile for pace. But if they're not backing off the press, what's causing it? First of all, the Jags have made strides on the offensive glass. They get three more misses back per game, despite taking almost two fewer shots. That's boosted their offense while slowing the game down possession-wise. The stat that jumps out most, though, and that points directly to the slower pace, is how much of IU Indy's games are played in transition. Last year, it allowed a stunning 17% of opponent FGA to come in transition while taking 17.5% of its shots on the run. item.content:encoded: If you're unfamiliar with IU Indy (formerly and forever in my heart known as IUPUI), Ben Howlett and The System, let me introduce you. The System means running. A lot. Howlett presses the entire game, sprints out in transition, and frequently runs full hockey-style five-player line changes to keep his guys fresh. I recommend this piece by Sam Federman from last summer for a deeper dive, but the ten-second version above should get the point across. The System debuted at the D-I level last year, but it doesn't come from Howlett. He played and then coached at West Liberty University under the brains behind the operation, the legendary Jim Crutchfield. Howlett, though, was the first to workshop it at the top level of the college game. In year one, there were signs of life, but they were relatively few and far between. The Jaguars went 7-25 (3-17 Horizon League), a three-win decrease from the one and only season under Paul Corsaro. They finished 317th at KenPom, an improvement over their 354th spot in preseason projections but nevertheless a mild drop from 312th under Corsaro. So far this year, it's been a different story. The Jags have four wins in seven games and have jumped from 316th preseason in KenPom to 275th in the season's first month. They led Penn State for nearly 25 minutes before ultimately losing by seven. They've won three of four against the four D-I teams within 100 spots of them at KenPom, either way, including a win over UT-Martin, an OVC favorite. And Howlett has accomplished it by doing something he may have never thought he'd do: slow down. Not all the way, but enough. The changes by the numbers Don't get me wrong, this team still runs. If you saw the Jags last season and you've watched them this November, it probably looks nearly indiscernible play by play. They still press full court for 40 minutes. The hockey subs still come into play. Their games are still track meets: in seven contests, neither IU Indy nor their opponent has scored below 70 points even once. But a look at the underlying numbers shows some distinct changes, most of which have had a positive effect early on. First and foremost is the pace. The 25-26 iteration of the Jaguars played 74.6 possessions per game, the highest in the country. This season, they're at 70.6 possessions, an unremarkable number that has them in the 67th %ile for pace. But if they're not backing off the press, what's causing it? First of all, the Jags have made strides on the offensive glass. They get three more misses back per game, despite taking almost two fewer shots. That's boosted their offense while slowing the game down possession-wise. The stat that jumps out most, though, and that points directly to the slower pace, is how much of IU Indy's games are played in transition. Last year, it allowed a stunning 17% of opponent FGA to come in transition while taking 17.5% of its shots on the run. This year, offensive transition sits at 14.6%, while transition FGA defense sits at 14.3%, up from 11.9% before its most recent game against William & Mary. In transition efficiency, the numbers have gotten worse on offense but improved defensively. Last year, the Jags allowed an NCAA-worst 69.2% on transition FGA. This year, it's 67.8% but was 65.2% before the W&M game, still bad but survivably so. Overall, the defense has been much stiffer inside. Year-over-year, Jags opponents are shooting 8.5% worse at the rim and taking 3% more mid-range FGA than a year ago, when they forced the fewest of any team in the country. The 3-point defense has also been significantly better, but that may be attributable to variance. IU Indy defensive heat maps, 25-26 left and 26-27 right IU Indy's improvement is more noticeable on the defensive end, but it's been better offensively too. The change is attributable to a strategic alteration of the shot diet. The Cats are taking threes at a rate about 10% higher than last year's already-above-median 42.7%. Their 52.6% 3Pr so far is in the top 20 nationally. While that creates variance that could bug them game-to-game, it has paid off impressively so far, putting the math more in their favor while opening up opportunities to offensive rebound and forcing at least one defender back to prevent so many transition opportunities. The other change has come at the free throw line. No team took fewer free throws last year than the Jaguars, whose 21.1% FTA rate was more than 3% lower than anyone else. That number has risen to 33.3%, around the 36th percentile nationally. They're not overpowering, but it's a marked improvement over a year ago. All told, the Jaguars have posted a 9.3 net rating so far, per CBB Analytics, compared to -6.3 a year ago. Now let's look at who's driving the strong start. The players behind the numbers As you may expect in The System, there isn't really a star. Because of how much running this team does, they have 11 guys who have played 60+ minutes in the first seven games. All told, the Jags run out 98 bench minutes a night, or 49% of total minutes, a top 15 mark in the country. The production mirrors it, with 40 points per game (right around 49%) coming from the reserves, similarly a top 15 ranking. If you're looking for a place to start, Billy Smith is as good as any. The fifth-year transfer from Chattanooga leads the team in scoring at 14.3 PPG, and he's doing it by simply not missing. Billy Smith shooting splits This is what the shooting chart spits out for Smith. He's making 67% of his twos (and he's made 12 of 13 at the rim thus far) and a ridiculous 46.9% from three despite nearly three of every four shot attempts coming from beyond the arc. In the second half of games, he's rocking a cool 80/50 split from the floor. Oh yeah, he's also come off the bench in all seven games. The two returners are Kameron Tinsley and Reece Hagy. Tinsley is the third-leading scorer and second-best three-point shooter behind Smith, making 39% of his six attempts per game. Hagy, meanwhile, is scoring just 1.7 points per game in under 12 minutes a night, but has a nearly 3:1 A:TO ratio and is swiping away a 2.1% steal rate, which ranks in the 65th percentile. If you're into on/off splits, Peyton Heiss is your guy. When Heiss is on the floor, the offense may not shoot as many free throws, but they make more shots, take more threes, and pass the ball much better without turning it over more. Defensively, they're nearly 13 points better when the 6'4" guard is out there defending versus riding pine. Peyton Heiss on/off splits Part of what makes this team so great is that anyone can beat you on any night. But if Coach Howlett can keep leaning on his vets and returners, this team will continue to shine. What this start means At the top of the article, you may remember I mentioned that IU Indy was up to 275th in KenPom and thought that sounded unimpressive. In comparison to the rest of the country, it largely is. However, it's important to contextualize where this program is. A 275th-place finish in KenPom would be the best since 2021 and just the second time this side of COVID finishing inside the top 300, a stretch that includes four different coaches. Within the Horizon League, the Jaguars sit 10th out of 12 teams right now by KenPom rank. However, there are a ridiculous SIX teams in a 20-team range from the Horizon, with IU Indy sitting last of those six. If it can filter its way to the top of this group, that would put the Jags 5th in the league, an achievement IU Indy has not completed since making the move from the Summit League in 2017-18. Its best finish was 6th place in a 10-team Horizon in its first year. Even if IU Indy gets to, say, 8th in the league, that would be its second-best finish ever as a Horizon member. The Jaguars haven't played a .500 season or better in conference play since 2015-16, in the Summit. There's a real path to do so here and Ben Howlett will have his boys ready and running in pursuit of it.

item.title: He's back! Rodri is training with Barça and has Riazor in his sights 🔙
item.description: He's back! Rodri is training with Barça and has Riazor in his sights 🔙 The Madrid-born midfielder trained as normal alongside the rest of his teammates at the Ciutat Esportiva on Friday. Having recovered from his hamstring injury, he will be available for Hansi Flick for Sunday's trip to Riazor. Good news for Barça's midfield. Rodri Hernández completed Friday's training session with the squad, confirming that his recovery is on track. The Spanish holding midfielder has shaken off the right hamstring injury he suffered earlier this month against Aston Villa in the Champions League. A key piece in Hansi Flick's plans The Spain captain's return is a huge relief for Hansi Flick, who gets his midfield orchestrator back just as the fixture list becomes congested. Although the coaching staff remain extremely cautious to avoid a setback, all signs point to the Madrid native being included in the squad travelling to A Coruña. The aim is clear: to give him valuable minutes against Deportivo at Riazor this Sunday (16:15) to build match sharpness ahead of next week's demanding clash with Atlético de Madrid. Barça's injury update The morning session in Sant Joan Despí also brought other important team news. Lamine Yamal also returned to group training after overcoming minor ankle discomfort. Meanwhile, Andreas Christensen and Marc Bernal trained separately from the group, while Fermín López is ruled out of the trip to Riazor through suspension. item.title: Jamie Overton tears through Australia as England claim emphatic win in third T20
item.description: Jamie Overton bullied Australia into submission at the Gabba, taking five for 12 as England claimed another T20 walkover against their biggest rivals. Having squared the series 1-1 with a dominant showing on the Gold Coast, Overton carried the tourists to a seven-wicket DLS victory to complete a Queensland double in Brisbane. The 6ft 5in quick gave Australia the runaround with his pace and bounce, gutting their batting line-up with a four-over spell that contained just seven scoring shots and a solitary boundary. All out for 108 in less than 17 overs, they were all but beaten at the halfway stage. There were three separate rain delays in a disjointed chase, but the result was never in doubt as Aneurin Donald’s 31 and an unbeaten 33 from Jordan Cox eased England to a recalculated target of 93 with 43 balls remaining. The evening was Overton’s, though, as he claimed the best ever bowling figures in a T20 between the sides, England’s previous best of four for 24 set by Jon Lewis in their first ever meeting in the format 21 years ago. There was no sign of an Australian implosion at the start of their innings, with six sixes sailing over the ropes as they passed 50 inside five overs. Sam Curran was hit for easily the biggest by Jake Fraser-McGurk as his first visit went for 16. England leaned on Liam Dawson to exert some control and he obliged, hustling through two tidy powerplay overs and persuading both Mitch Marsh and Sam Harper to pick out mid-on. Overton was the catcher on both occasions, but his evening was only just getting started. The score was 64 for two when the Surrey man entered the attack for the seventh over and 97 for seven when he took his cap at the end of the 13th. He took care of Fraser-McGurk with his second ball, failing to clear Tom Banton at long on, and then went after the power-hitter Tim David. Liam Dawson (second right) made the first breakthroughs for England (Tertius Pickard/AP). Having rapped him on the forearm with a sharp bouncer, Overton bided his time as David received treatment then dismissed him via a top-edged pull off the next delivery. He should have had two in two when Joel Davies was juggled by Adil Rashid at backward point, but a short ball soon accounted for the outmatched all-rounder. Australia were increasingly unsure of how to play Overton, unsettled by his zippy bounce and too keen to step away to leg, and he finished his spell with an emphatic double-wicket maiden. Back to his task after putting down a return catch that rattled his thumb and needed the attention of the physio, he had Nikhil Chaudhary caught in the deep attempting a shot requiring more muscle than he could muster and signed off by taking Ben Dwarshuis’ outside edge. Australia’s tail barely threatened a fightback. Dawson took a third, while Rashid breezed through four overs, Mitch Owen was ran out messily and Curran blew through last man Billy Stanlake. The score was 64 for two when the Surrey man entered the attack for the seventh over and 97 for seven when he took his cap at the end of the 13th. He took care of Fraser-McGurk with his second ball, failing to clear Tom Banton at long on, and then went after the power-hitter Tim David. Liam Dawson (second right) made the first breakthroughs for England (Tertius Pickard/AP). Having rapped him on the forearm with a sharp bouncer, Overton bided his time as David received treatment then dismissed him via a top-edged pull off the next delivery. He should have had two in two when Joel Davies was juggled by Adil Rashid at backward point, but a short ball soon accounted for the outmatched all-rounder. Australia were increasingly unsure of how to play Overton, unsettled by his zippy bounce and too keen to step away to leg, and he finished his spell with an emphatic double-wicket maiden. Back to his task after putting down a return catch that rattled his thumb and needed the attention of the physio, he had Nikhil Chaudhary caught in the deep attempting a shot requiring more muscle than he could muster and signed off by taking Ben Dwarshuis’ outside edge. Australia’s tail barely threatened a fightback. Dawson took a third, while Rashid breezed through four overs, Mitch Owen was ran out messily and Curran blew through last man Billy Stanlake. A slender chase of 109 would not have worried England’s all-Welsh opening pair, having put on 151 in the previous match, but Phil Salt was an early casualty when he failed to get hold of Riley Meredith and popped a soft catch to cover. Donald was soon back in the swing of things, though, taking a like to Stanlake on the latter’s first T20 outing in seven years. At one stage he took 22 off a five-ball sequence from the tall seamer, pulling and cutting with gusto. Harry Brook hammered his fourth ball for a flat six over cover, suggesting England were in a hurry to get things done, before rain intervened. Aneurin Donald hit 32 off 13 balls (Tertius Pickard/AP). Meredith did his best to make a game of it after the restart, dismissing Brook and Donald in the space of three balls before another interruption. The winning line was revised down to 98 in 17 overs, then 93 in 16 as the weather made for a frustrating finish. Cox made hay, hitting five fours and a six in just 14 balls to end it for good off just 8.5 overs.

item.title: Fury cleared to fight Joshua after medical checks
item.description: Tyson Fury has won 36 of his 39 fights as a professional [Getty Images] Tyson Fury has been medically cleared to fight Anthony Joshua in December after the bout was put in jeopardy by claims of a schizophrenia diagnosis. Fury, 38, spoke of his mental health struggles in a Netflix documentary which was released on Friday, with his wife, Paris, saying he had been diagnosed with schizophrenia. But Paris has since retracted that statement, saying he "doesn't have this condition" and Netflix have edited the remarks out of their film. The British Boxing Board of Control told BBC Sport: "Tyson Fury has been cleared to box on 11 December." Fury faces Joshua in a long overdue all-British heavyweight contest at Cardiff's Principality Stadium in the early hours of 12 December. More to follow. item.title: Nico Paz’s stance on potential Man Utd move and Real Madrid return revealed
item.description: Nico Paz’s stance on potential Man Utd move and Real Madrid return revealed According to The Athletic , Como star Nico Paz does not currently favour rejoining Real Madrid this summer, and Manchester United may not be his first choice, especially if the Red Devils don’t qualify for the Champions League. Como star Nico Paz inevitably continues to grab headlines worldwide thanks to his fantastic performances under Cesc Fabregas. MILAN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 08: Nico Paz of Como 1907 runs with the ball during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and Como 1907 at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on November 08, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) Paz has six goals and eight assists in 16 appearances across all competitions this season, and Real Madrid have an option to re-sign him for €80m in the summer. According to The Athletic, however, the Argentine currently does not favour a return to the Spanish capital. “This stance might alter if he is assured of a prominent role — that has not been the case,” The Athletic clarifies. According to the report, Manchester United see the Argentine as a potential replacement for Bruno Fernandes, whose contract expires at the end of the season. ITALY – OCTOBER 21: Nico Paz of Como 1907 is challenged by Andrey Santos of Manchester United during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The Athletic explains that the Red Devils “may not be Nico Paz’s first-choice destination, and Champions League qualification is a major factor.” Manchester United saw Nico Paz’s quality firsthand in October, when the Argentine scored two goals and provided one assist in Como’s 4-1 victory in a Champions League match at the Stadio Sinigaglia. This is Nico Paz’s third season in Como. The Azzurri re-signed him from Real Madrid last summer for €60m.

item.title: Patriots Have Another Reason To Be Concerned About Buffalo Following Thanksgiving
item.description: Patriots Have Another Reason To Be Concerned About Buffalo Following Thanksgiving originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots received another reminder Thursday night of just how difficult it could be to challenge the Buffalo Bills for AFC East supremacy. Buffalo defeated the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 on Thanksgiving, improving to 10-1 and extending its winning streak to seven games. Tyler Bass delivered the decisive points with a 57-yard field goal as time expired. What made Buffalo's victory particularly interesting from New England's perspective wasn't necessarily the final score. The Bills managed to defeat one of the AFC's most dangerous teams despite receiving relatively little production from their most recognizable offensive player. That should concern every team hoping to challenge Buffalo during the remainder of the season. Buffalo Doesn't Always Need Josh Allen To Be Spectacular Allen completed just 10 of 21 passes for 81 yards and threw two interceptions against Kansas City. Those aren't the numbers football fans ordinarily associate with one of the NFL's premier quarterbacks, particularly during his games against Patrick Mahomes. Nevertheless, Buffalo found another way to win. BILLS WIN!!!!!!!!!!!!! @MandT_Bank | #KCvsBUF https://t.co/y23fz9iBod — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 27, 2026 James Cook rushed for 117 yards and a touchdown, while Buffalo's defense prevented Kansas City from establishing consistent offensive momentum. Bass eventually converted two field goals from beyond 50 yards in the fourth quarter. The ability to win games without exceptional quarterback production represents an important characteristic of championship contenders. Buffalo demonstrated Thursday that it doesn't necessarily need Allen to produce several spectacular plays to defeat quality opposition. MORE: Patriots’ Final Seven Games Leave Little Room For A Slow Start New England Can Learn Something From Buffalo's Victory The Patriots have their own challenges to navigate as the season enters its final stretch. Establishing a dependable running game, generating defensive stops and receiving consistent special teams contributions become particularly important when quarterback production is uncertain. Buffalo's Thanksgiving performance offered an interesting example of how those elements can work together. The Bills didn't need to win an offensive shootout against Mahomes, and they didn't allow Allen's turnovers to determine the outcome. New England's long-term objective involves building a roster capable of competing with Buffalo on a regular basis. Thursday's result demonstrated that accomplishing that requires considerably more than simply finding a franchise quarterback. The Bills have become a difficult team to defeat even when their biggest star struggles. That's an important standard for Mike Vrabel and the Patriots to pursue as they continue developing their own championship aspirati

item.title: Ipswich Women sign Ademiluyi for record fee
item.description: Ademiluyi had been on loan at the Tractor Girls from NWSL side Gotham FC since February [Getty Images] Ipswich Town Women have confirmed the permanent signing of England youth international Princess Ademiluyi for an undisclosed club record fee. The 20-year-old forward has been on loan at the Tractor Girls from NWSL side Gotham FC since February and has agreed a three-and-a-half year deal at the WSL2 side. Ademiluyi has been capped by England at under-19 and under-20 level, and has been called up for the under-23 side for the first time ahead of their internationals against Belgium and Portugal next week. "I have really made a home for myself in Suffolk and I am so excited to continue building what has been a positive start to the season for us as a group," she told the club's website. "The players, staff and supporters have all been brilliant with me since I arrived and I can't wait to see where this club can go and to continue making more memories together." Ipswich Town chairman Mark Ashton said: "Signing Princess on a permanent basis has been a real priority for us and completing such a significant deal as this highlights the club's ongoing commitment to reach the top level of the game. "This is a statement signing for the club, with further announcements to come in due course as we reaffirm our commitment to our women's set-up in both the short and long-term." Ademiluyi started her career at WSL side West Ham in 2023 before moving to US-based Gotham and is Ipswich's top scorer so far in 2026-27, with four goals. The Tractor Girls finished ninth in WSL2 last season following promotion to the second tier in 2025, and were in the fourth tier as recently as 2021. Under the management of former men's team player David Wright, appointed to the role in April, the Blues are third after eight games this season, three points behind leaders Newcastle United. Ipswich on 'inevitable' path to WSL - Boswell A statement of intent - analysis Ademiluyi has played an important role in helping the Tractor Girls transform from relegation candidates to title contenders. She made an immediate impact on joining in February, scoring goals against Durham and Birmingham City to help secure the team's survival in WSL2. The forward has continued to find the net this season, and won the WSL2 player of the month award for October. There is a growing feeling within the women's game that the Blues will be playing at the highest level in the not too distant future and securing a proven goalscorer whose stock is also rising on the international stage will only strengthen that train of thought. item.title: ‘FIRE THE ENTIRE STAFF!’ NFL Pundits and Famous Fans Erupt After Cowboys’ Epic Thanksgiving Implosion
item.description: (Screengrab via Fox) Stephen A. Smith was reduced to tears of laughter and Skip Bayless declared himself finished with the Dallas Cowboys as the Philadelphia Eagles pulled off the biggest comeback in NFL Thanksgiving history on Thursday. The sports world erupted after Philadelphia overturned a staggering 21-point deficit to beat its bitter NFC East rival 39-38, with kicker Jake Elliott drilling a 59-yard field goal with just seconds on the clock. The architect of Dallas’s humiliation was Eagles backup quarterback Joe Milton III , who was cut from the Cowboys in August but returned to haunt his old team with a sensational second-half comeback. Smith, a longtime tormentor of Cowboys fans, could barely contain himself in a video posted to X, wheezing with laughter as he mocked Dallas for losing to its former third-string quarterback. “Just when you think it can’t get worse!!” he wrote. Just when you think it can’t get worse!! pic.twitter.com/qMt8Owqnd0 — Stephen A Smith (@stephenasmith) November 27, 2026 CNN anchor Jake Tapper also delighted in the win: (Pokes head up) pic.twitter.com/JKJ03U5CCT — Jake Tapper (@jaketapper) November 27, 2026 Long-suffering Cowboys supporter Bayless responded with an enormous, all-caps “NOOOOOO” stretching hundreds of characters across X before posting a lengthy video lamenting the defeat. “The Cowboys are DONE and so am I,” he declared. NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO — Skip Bayless (@RealSkipBayless) November 27, 2026 The Cowboys are DONE and so am I. pic.twitter.com/YZIIJKVcwT — Skip Bayless (@RealSkipBayless) November 27, 2026 Fellow Cowboys fan and Fox & Friends co-host Lawrence Jones demanded an immediate clearout, posting: “FIRE THE ENTIRE STAFF TONIGHT.” FIRE THE ENTIRE STAFF TONIGHT — Lawrence Jones III (@LawrenceBJones3) November 27, 2026 The fury followed an extraordinary collapse by Dallas, which had appeared to have the Thanksgiving showdown wrapped up after building a commanding 31-10 lead in the third quarter. But Milton, filling in for the injured Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts , torched his former team for 331 passing yards and three touchdowns as Philadelphia mounted a ferocious fightback. The Eagles’ turnaround gathered pace in a frantic fourth quarter when Ty Robinson blocked a Dallas punt and Kenny Moore II returned it for a touchdown. Dallas briefly restored its two-touchdown cushion through a Dak Prescott rushing score, but Milton answered with a 15-yard touchdown run before finding WR Makai Lemon for another score to bring Philadelphia within two points.
