NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO — Skip Bayless (@RealSkipBayless) November 27, 2026 The Cowboys are DONE and so am I. pic.twitter.com/YZIIJKVcwT — Skip Bayless (@RealSkipBayless) November 27, 2026 Fellow Cowboys fan and Fox & Friends co-host Lawrence Jones demanded an immediate clearout, posting: “FIRE THE ENTIRE STAFF TONIGHT.” FIRE THE ENTIRE STAFF TONIGHT — Lawrence Jones III (@LawrenceBJones3) November 27, 2026 The fury followed an extraordinary collapse by Dallas, which had appeared to have the Thanksgiving showdown wrapped up after building a commanding 31-10 lead in the third quarter. But Milton, filling in for the injured Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts , torched his former team for 331 passing yards and three touchdowns as Philadelphia mounted a ferocious fightback. The Eagles’ turnaround gathered pace in a frantic fourth quarter when Ty Robinson blocked a Dallas punt and Kenny Moore II returned it for a touchdown. Dallas briefly restored its two-touchdown cushion through a Dak Prescott rushing score, but Milton answered with a 15-yard touchdown run before finding WR Makai Lemon for another score to bring Philadelphia within two points. The Cowboys then squandered a chance to put the contest beyond reach when Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal. With less than a minute remaining, Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer gambled on fourth-and-one rather than punt. Prescott was promptly sacked for a nine-yard loss, handing Philadelphia possession near midfield. A costly pass interference penalty against Dallas safety Markquese Bell then helped set up Elliott’s improbable 59-yard winner. Former Eagles stars were celebrating. Terrell Owens seized the opportunity to taunt Cowboys owner Jerry Jones while ex-Philadelphia center Jason Kelce branded Milton “Bazooka Joe”: Fly Eagles Fly!!!! @Eagles Happy Thanksgiving Jerry Jones!!! My cereal I cooked for Thanksgiving tastes so much better!!! @Gttppod — Terrell Owens (@terrellowens) November 27, 2026 Bazooka Joe, my goodness, hell of a performance. Man that was an electric freakin game baby. Just uncle Rico’d us to a win over the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. I’ll remember this game forever, thank you guys! — Jason Kelce (@JasonKelce) November 27, 2026 Clay Travis was joined by other pundits were utterly stunned by the final score: I watched the entire game and I legit can’t believe the Cowboys lost this game. — Clay Travis (@ClayTravis) November 27, 2026 This is the most Cowboys game possible. — Clay Travis (@ClayTravis) November 27, 2026 What exactly were the cowboys doing there — Caitlin Clark (@CaitlinClark22) November 27, 2026 Joe Milton outplaying Dak on Thanksgiving was not on my bingo card — Ben DiNucci (@B_DiNucci6) November 27, 2026 Cowboy fans. Ya’ll told me last week Titans scoring 30 was a fluke. What about 39 2 the Eagles with a bck up Qb. That out played your MVP candidate Qb? Eagles haven’t scored more than 24 pts in gm this yr. Your defensive personnel isn’t good. That’s the issue not the DC. — shannon sharpe (@ShannonSharpe) November 27, 2026 Joe Milton — Field Yates (@FieldYates) November 26, 2026 Joe Milton reminds me of blend of Tom Brady and Dan Marino — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) November 27, 2026 It was ESPN analyst Mina Kimes , however, who delivered perhaps the most cutting verdict on Dallas’s Thanksgiving disaster: “The 2026 Cowboys are performance art.” The 2026 Cowboys are performance art — Mina Kimes (@minakimes) November 27, 2026 The victory improves Philadelphia to 4-7, while Dallas slipped to 5-7. The post ‘FIRE THE ENTIRE STAFF!’ NFL Pundits and Famous Fans Erupt After Cowboys’ Epic Thanksgiving Implosion first appeared on Mediaite .

item.title: Tyson Fury ‘cleared’ to fight Anthony Joshua after clarification on schizophrenia diagnosis
item.description: Tyson Fury has reportedly been medically cleared to box Anthony Joshua , after confusion around a possible schizophrenia diagnosis. Fury is scheduled to face his fellow British heavyweight on 11 December , as the pair headline at Cardiff’s Principallity stadium in a fight years in the making. However, the bout appeared to be under threat this week, as quotes from Tyson Fury – a new Netflix documentary – did the rounds. The quotes saw Fury’s wife Paris suggesting that the boxer was once diagnosed with schizophrenia. Tyson Fury in 2026 (PA) That prompted Robert Smith, general secretary of the British Boxing Board of Control (BBBofC), to tell the BBC: “We are in the process of dealing with the matter, but if there are any medical issues we wouldn’t let anyone box. It doesn’t matter if it’s Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody. I’m fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We’re dealing with it now and we’ll have an answer very shortly.” Paris soon released a statement that read : “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.” Meanwhile, Netflix said: “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.” The film was released on Friday, and the scene in question had been reported on earlier this week, following preview screenings earlier in November . Friday also brought an update from journalist Gareth A Davies, who tweeted: “Tyson Fury’s medicals were all cleared by the Boxing Board on Thursday evening. His promoter was informed Friday morning. The notion that Fury vs Anthony Joshua would have been cancelled on mental health grounds is extremely unlikely.” The Independent has contacted the BBBofC for comment. Fury will finally face Anthony Joshua on 11 December (PA Wire) Fury vs Joshua is a fight that has been discussed for the best part of a decade. The pair even signed to fight each other during Covid, only for Deontay Wilder to threaten legal action and force a trilogy bout with Fury instead. At the time, Fury and Joshua held all the major heavyweight belts between them, but Joshua would lose the unified titles in his next fight. The 37-year-old has not held a world title since. Meanwhile, Fury, 38, retained the WBC belt until 2024, but he will similarly enter his clash with “AJ” without a world title. The vacant WBA Super belt will be on the line, however, when the heavyweights collide. This week brought confirmation that the fight will actually begin at 1.30am on 12 December, with increased stewarding, police presence, and travel options around the Welsh capital.

item.title: Mike Tomlin explains how Steelers owner will handle Mike McCarthy
item.description: Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images, Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images, Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have epitomised dysfunction this week. After Aaron Rodgers was benched and made inactive, the four-time NFL MVP called into The Pat McAfee Show and went scorched earth on head coach Mike McCarthy. The Steelers promptly released Rodgers, and on Thanksgiving night, the man who helmed McCarthy’s job as Pittsburgh’s coach for 19 seasons weighed in. Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin, who now serves as an analyst for NBC’s Football Night in America, didn’t mince words on Thursday night, calling the situation “a dumpster fire” and admitting that he was upset and saddened by the whole saga. “Art is a guy that’s not a hedge fund guy” Tomlin also explained how Steelers owner Art Rooney II will handle the situation and how his process is different than most of the modern team owners around the league. “Art is a guy that’s not a hedge fund guy that bought a football team. He’s not a, you know, artificial intelligence guy that bought a football team,” Tomlin said. ” This is a family business. It’s generational. Any advice or thought process in that way, I imagine he just says, ‘What would my dad do?’ or, ‘What would my grandfather do?’ Their mode of operation is time-tested. It’s generational. And so I doubt very, very seriously that he called anyone for outside advice.” “He was beloved” Interestingly, Tomlin also said that while coaching Rodgers in 2025, the veteran quarterback was a wonderful presence in the locker room. “He was beloved, and I’m not over-exaggerating that,” Tomlin said. “He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture, to be engaged with teammates.” “And particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, et cetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real natural way,” Tomlin continued. All in all, Tomlin is saddened by the way things ended. “Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career in the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, and just on the macro level, whether it’s organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum, those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football.” The post Mike Tomlin explains how Steelers owner will handle Mike McCarthy appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Confirmed: Brahim Diaz signs new contract with Real Madrid until 2031
item.description: Confirmed: Brahim Diaz signs new contract with Real Madrid until 2031 The series of contract renewals continues at Real Madrid as the club have now announced that Brahim Diaz has penned a new long-term deal until 2031. “Real Madrid CF and Brahim Diaz have agreed to extend the contract of our player, who is now tied to the club until June 30, 2031,” the club statement read. Signed from Manchester City in the January transfer window of 2019, Brahim has grown into a valuable squad player at Real Madrid. After initially finding it hard to break into the team, the Moroccan star spent three seasons away on loan at AC Milan, before returning in 2023. Since then, he has become a key player under different managers even though he has been unable to establish himself as a regular starter in the team. So far in his Real Madrid career, Brahim has made 173 appearances, scoring 22 and assisting 34 goals. In the process, the versatile attacker has won won seven titles at the club – 1 Champions League, 1 Club World Cup, 1 UEFA Super Cup, 2 La Liga titles, and 2 Spanish Super Cups. While minutes have been hard to come by this season as well, Brahim remains committed to Real Madrid and has renewed for five more years until 2031. Brahim’s renewal follows after Real Madrid also secured the futures of Arda Guler, Aurelien Tchouameni, and Thibaut Courtois over the last week. Jude Bellingham and Federico Valverde are expected to be next in line to sign long-term renewals.

item.title: Sam Roush: Bears Rookie Tight End Earns Bigger Role After Career-Best Game
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 27: Sam Roush of the Stanford Cardinal participates in a drill during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 27, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty S am Roush: Bears rookie tight end and 2026 third-round pick out of Stanford, did not dominate the Thanksgiving Day highlight reels in Detroit, yet he quietly delivered the most impactful performance of his young NFL career. Catching all five of his targets for 31 yards in Chicago Bears ’s thrilling 39-35 comeback victory over the Detroit Lions , the 6-foot-6, 267-pound tight end stepped directly into an emergency workload and helped keep the Bears’ offense moving. While 31 receiving yards looks modest on a box score that featured 74 total points, it marked a major step forward for a rookie who had never logged more than two receptions in a single contest prior to Week 12. A Reliable Option When the Bears Needed One Chicago’s tight end depth chart faced an immediate crisis early in Thursday’s contest when starter Colston Loveland went down with a knee injury after a Lions defender rolled into his lower left leg on a run-blocking snap. With veteran Cole Kmet already out for the remainder of the season following a Week 7 knee injury against New England, the Bears suddenly had to lean heavily on Roush and fellow reserve Stephen Carlson. Roush answered the call without hesitation. Converting every single pass thrown his way , the No. 69 overall draft pick became one of quarterback Caleb Williams’ most dependable underneath outlets, showcasing the physicality and sure hands that drew Chicago’s front office to him in April. One sequence in particular captured why the coaching staff trusts him in heavy traffic. On an 11-yard reception, Roush lowered his shoulder and powered straight through a would-be Lions tackler for extra yardage—the exact brand of tough, after-the-catch finishing that defined his college tape at Stanford. Drafted primarily for his inline blocking chops and physical edge, Thursday proved he can handle real passing-game volume when injuries strike. Trust Building at a Critical Spot Head coach Ben Johnson has steadily praised Roush’s weekly growth throughout his rookie campaign, noting how quickly the young tight end has grasped the nuances of Chicago’s offense. Thursday’s Thanksgiving showcase offered the clearest on-field proof yet that the staff’s long-term vision for him is taking hold. Roush is not suddenly going to morph into a high-volume vertical receiving threat, nor does Chicago’s scheme ask him to fill that role. What he can provide is a trustworthy security blanket over the middle of the field paired with rugged perimeter and inline blocking—precisely the kind of multi-purpose complementary piece Johnson’s offense thrives on. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty S am Roush: Bears rookie tight end and 2026 third-round pick out of Stanford, did not dominate the Thanksgiving Day highlight reels in Detroit, yet he quietly delivered the most impactful performance of his young NFL career. With veteran Cole Kmet already out for the remainder of the season following a Week 7 knee injury against New England, the Bears suddenly had to lean heavily on Roush and fellow reserve Stephen Carlson. Roush answered the call without hesitation. Converting every single pass thrown his way , the No. 69 overall draft pick became one of quarterback Caleb Williams’ most dependable underneath outlets, showcasing the physicality and sure hands that drew Chicago’s front office to him in April. One sequence in particular captured why the coaching staff trusts him in heavy traffic. On an 11-yard reception, Roush lowered his shoulder and powered straight through a would-be Lions tackler for extra yardage—the exact brand of tough, after-the-catch finishing that defined his college tape at Stanford. Drafted primarily for his inline blocking chops and physical edge, Thursday proved he can handle real passing-game volume when injuries strike. Trust Building at a Critical Spot Head coach Ben Johnson has steadily praised Roush’s weekly growth throughout his rookie campaign, noting how quickly the young tight end has grasped the nuances of Chicago’s offense. Thursday’s Thanksgiving showcase offered the clearest on-field proof yet that the staff’s long-term vision for him is taking hold. Roush is not suddenly going to morph into a high-volume vertical receiving threat, nor does Chicago’s scheme ask him to fill that role. What he can provide is a trustworthy security blanket over the middle of the field paired with rugged perimeter and inline blocking—precisely the kind of multi-purpose complementary piece Johnson’s offense thrives on. Roush ready to handle starter-level snaps Loveland’s availability remains uncertain heading into next week’s matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars, though the mini-bye created by Thursday’s holiday kickoff gives Chicago’s medical staff a few extra days to evaluate his knee. If the second-year starter is limited or forced to sit out Week 13, Roush is squarely positioned to handle starter-level snaps. Carlson also chipped in with two catches for 30 yards against Detroit to give Williams another viable option, yet Roush’s combination of size, blocking reliability, and crisp execution makes him the natural choice to anchor the position group. For a first-year player who spent the opening two months of the season working largely in supporting packages, catching all five targets in a high-stakes divisional shootout carries real weight inside Halas Hall. The Bears now sit at 9-2 and stand alone atop the NFC North—and disciplined, unheralded performances like the one Sam Roush, Bears rookie tight end, delivered in Detroit are a big reason why. item.title: Former WWE star Braun Strowman’s in-ring return match announced
item.description: Former WWE star Braun Strowman’s in-ring return match announced appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Earlier last year, former WWE Universal Champion Braun Strowman parted ways with the promotion. Shortly after, it was reported that Strowman was released from the promotion due to higher salary demands. Later, it was also noted that WWE wanted to have him back as a part-timer. However, that never advanced. While Strowman almost stopped pursuing his in-ring career after WWE, he started his own TV show, Everything on the Menu with Braun Strowman. The first season was a major success and the show was later renewed for a second season. Now, a few months after his first in-ring return, Strowman is set to lace his boots again . Recently, Great Lakes Championship Wrestling announced on social media that Strowman will team up with Erick Redbeard, aka, Erick Rowan, against The Good Brothers (Doc Gallows and Karl Anderson) at Blizzard Brawl 21. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The above-mentioned event will take place on Dec. 5, 2026, at Potawatomi Hotel & Casino (Ballroom) in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Strowman and Redbeard share a long history and have teamed up several times in the past during their time together in WWE. Earlier this year, Strowman also underwent surgery to drain excess fluid from his knee after an infection. In Jul. 2026, Strowman wrestled his first match at GLCW The Return of the Titan. It marked his return since his last WWE SmackDown match in 2025. On the other hand, Redbeard was released from WWE in Apr. 2026, along with the other members of Wyatt Sicks. He has now competed across several independent promotions and events, including AWF, ACW, MLP Sacred Ground, TMW and ECPW Autumn Aggression. Redbeard is currently an active part of the Syx faction in TNA. Just announced for Blizzard Brawl 21… @Adamscherr99 & @ErickRedBeard take on the Good Brothers, @MachineGunKA & @The_BigLG Tickets on sale now at https://t.co/V1DONAuRR9 pic.twitter.com/9YzxxcJhks — Great Lakes Championship Wrestling (@BlizzardBrawl) November 25, 2026

item.title: Week 13 college football upset watch includes Baylor, Nebraska, UCLA top rivalry picks
item.description: Rivalry week puts title berths and playoff hopes on the line across this Week 13 college football upset watch, with Baylor catching 4.5 points at No. 18 Houston and No. 25 Nebraska chasing the Heroes Trophy at No. 13 Iowa. Quarterback health hangs over the slate again. Houston’s Conner Weigman and UCLA’s Ty Dieffenbach are both listed as questionable, and Clemson is handing former walk-on Trent Pearman a second straight start against South Carolina. MORE: Week 13 college football prediction market picks: UCLA, Ohio State lead Kalshi, Polymarket No. 25 Nebraska (+3.5) at No. 13 Iowa: Upset watch 8 Nebraska Cornhuskers quarterback Anthony Colandrea (10) and offensive lineman Gunnar Gottula (77) celebrate after a touchdown against the Ohio State Buckeyes | Dylan Widger-Imagn Images Kickoff: Friday, Nov. 27, noon ET (CBS) Nebraska brings a 7-4 record and its first College Football Playoff ranking since 2016 into Kinnick Stadium after last week’s 31-28 win over Ohio State. Iowa has won 10 of the last 11 meetings and is on a four-game winning streak, with an outside shot at the playoff still alive. “There’s no one that runs the ball and stops the run better ,” Nebraska coach Matt Rhule said of Iowa this week. The Hawkeyes allow just 3.51 yards per rush, so the Huskers will need to move the ball through the air. Nebraska has the better offense for that. The Huskers rank 24th in ESPN’s offensive efficiency ratings, while Iowa ranks 45th, and they have a 47% passing success rate against FBS opponents. They’re also 2-0 under new offensive coordinator Glenn Thomas since Rhule fired Dana Holgorsen earlier this month. Iowa’s defense ranks eighth in those same ratings, and the total is 40.5, so one sustained touchdown drive could decide this. I trust Nebraska’s passing game to put that drive together and take the Heroes Trophy back to Lincoln. Picks: Nebraska 20-17, Nebraska +3.5, Under 40.5 Air Force (+6.5) at New Mexico: Upset watch 7 Air Force Falcons quarterback Evan Medders (5) runs with the ball in the second quarter against the UTEP Miners | Isaiah J. A New Mexico win guarantees the Lobos host the championship game and knocks Air Force out of contention. A Falcons win keeps their title hopes alive. Air Force leads the nation at 351.7 rushing yards per game, and New Mexico allows just 73.5. The Lobos won last year’s meeting 20-3 and held the Falcons to 110 rushing yards. This year’s Air Force offense still averages 5.66 yards per carry and runs successfully on 53.4% of its carries against FBS opponents. The bigger question is whether New Mexico can score enough. Houston’s Conner Weigman and UCLA’s Ty Dieffenbach are both listed as questionable, and Clemson is handing former walk-on Trent Pearman a second straight start against South Carolina. MORE: Week 13 college football prediction market picks: UCLA, Ohio State lead Kalshi, Polymarket No. 25 Nebraska (+3.5) at No. 13 Iowa: Upset watch 8 Nebraska Cornhuskers quarterback Anthony Colandrea (10) and offensive lineman Gunnar Gottula (77) celebrate after a touchdown against the Ohio State Buckeyes | Dylan Widger-Imagn Images Kickoff: Friday, Nov. 27, noon ET (CBS) Nebraska brings a 7-4 record and its first College Football Playoff ranking since 2016 into Kinnick Stadium after last week’s 31-28 win over Ohio State. Iowa has won 10 of the last 11 meetings and is on a four-game winning streak, with an outside shot at the playoff still alive. “There’s no one that runs the ball and stops the run better ,” Nebraska coach Matt Rhule said of Iowa this week. The Hawkeyes allow just 3.51 yards per rush, so the Huskers will need to move the ball through the air. Nebraska has the better offense for that. The Huskers rank 24th in ESPN’s offensive efficiency ratings, while Iowa ranks 45th, and they have a 47% passing success rate against FBS opponents. They’re also 2-0 under new offensive coordinator Glenn Thomas since Rhule fired Dana Holgorsen earlier this month. Iowa’s defense ranks eighth in those same ratings, and the total is 40.5, so one sustained touchdown drive could decide this. I trust Nebraska’s passing game to put that drive together and take the Heroes Trophy back to Lincoln. Picks: Nebraska 20-17, Nebraska +3.5, Under 40.5 Air Force (+6.5) at New Mexico: Upset watch 7 Air Force Falcons quarterback Evan Medders (5) runs with the ball in the second quarter against the UTEP Miners | Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Kickoff: Friday, Nov. 27, 4:30 p.m. ET (The CW) Two 9-2 teams meet in Albuquerque with a Mountain West title game spot on the line. A New Mexico win guarantees the Lobos host the championship game and knocks Air Force out of contention. A Falcons win keeps their title hopes alive. Air Force leads the nation at 351.7 rushing yards per game, and New Mexico allows just 73.5. The Lobos won last year’s meeting 20-3 and held the Falcons to 110 rushing yards. This year’s Air Force offense still averages 5.66 yards per carry and runs successfully on 53.4% of its carries against FBS opponents. The bigger question is whether New Mexico can score enough. Quarterback Luke Moga is making only his second start of the season, and running backs Scottre Humphrey and Kiefer Sibley are questionable with ankle injuries . Humphrey leads the team in rushing. Air Force is also shorthanded on defense, with inside linebacker Blake Fletcher out for a second straight game. Air Force can win by putting together a pair of long touchdown drives and making Moga answer late. I like the Falcons to steal a one-point win and keep their title hopes going. Picks: Air Force 21-20, Air Force +6.5, Under 42.5 MORE: Week 13 college fantasy football rankings: Devon Dampier, Dylan Riley lead rivalry week South Carolina at Clemson (+6.5): Upset watch 6 Clemson quarterback Trent Pearman (14), one of the Tigers’ football seniors, poses with Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney before kickoff with Georgia Tech | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Kickoff: Saturday, Nov. 28, 3 p.m. ET (ESPN2) Clemson is 7-4 after Trent Pearman won his first career start, 20-10 at Duke. He completed 17 of 27 passes for 164 yards with no interceptions and ran for a touchdown while rotating with Chris Denson , who also scored on the ground. Pearman gets the start again because Christopher Vizzina is still out with a concussion. “He is nowhere near being back ,” coach Dabo Swinney said Sunday. “I don’t think people realize just how severe that was.” Clemson’s defense makes Pearman’s job manageable. The Tigers allow only 5.65 yards per dropback and held Duke to 10 points, so South Carolina will probably have to win on the ground. The Gamecocks average 5.42 yards per rush, Clemson allows 5.05, and quarterback LaNorris Sellers gives South Carolina a second runner the Tigers have to account for. If Clemson can keep the score in the teens heading into the fourth quarter, Pearman gets a chance to win it at home on the final possession. I still give South Carolina the late field goal, but 6.5 points is too many in a game this physical. Picks: South Carolina 20-17, Clemson +6.5, Under 42.5 No. 15 USC at No. 9 UCLA (+6.5): Upset watch 7.5 UCLA Bruins defensive back Scooter Jackson (1) celebrates in the end zone after returning an interception 65-yards for a touchdown in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins | Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Kickoff: Saturday, Nov. 28, 3:30 p.m. ET (CBS) A win clinches UCLA a spot in the Big Ten championship game, but the 10-1 Bruins are coming off an 18-16 triple-overtime loss at Michigan. Quarterback Ty Dieffenbach was carted off in the first overtime with a hip injury and is listed as questionable. Coach Bob Chesney said Dieffenbach is “ nowhere near in the clear ,” and Madden Iamaleava would make his first career start if Dieffenbach can’t go. UCLA’s defense is why I’m sticking with the upset I picked in this week’s prediction market column. The Bruins allow 4.22 yards per play and 4.89 yards per dropback. They rank fifth in ESPN’s defensive efficiency ratings, and USC’s offense ranks seventh. USC’s defense is the weaker unit at 69th, and it’s thin at the back. The Trojans ruled out safeties Kendarious Reddick, Trestin Castro and Isaiah Rubin , along with linebackers Taylor Johnson and Roman Marchetti. That sets up well for a Bruins running game averaging 5.75 yards per rush, whoever plays quarterback. UCLA can lean on the run at the Rose Bowl and make USC drive the length of the field. I have the Bruins winning by a field goal and clinching their trip to Indianapolis. Picks: UCLA 24-21, UCLA +6.5, Under 46.5 MORE: Week 13 CFB DFS picks: Cole Tabb, Nate Sheppard headline DraftKings, FanDuel value Kansas (+6) at Oklahoma State: Upset watch 5.5 Jayhawks running back Dylan Edwards (1) runs the ball during the first quarter against the West Virginia Mountaineers | Ben Queen-Imagn Images Kickoff: Saturday, Nov. 28, 6:15 p.m. ET (ESPN2) Kansas is 4-7 and out of the bowl picture after a 31-29 triple-overtime loss to BYU, but coach Lance Leipold isn’t expecting a flat finish in Stillwater. “We’ve got another game. There’s no quit . We’ll keep fighting,” Leipold said after the loss. Oklahoma State is 7-4 after an overtime comeback win at Arizona State. Kansas’s biggest worry is Oklahoma State’s passing game. Oklahoma State averages 8.09 yards per dropback, and Leipold had plenty of praise for quarterback Drew Mestemaker this week. “He’s really composed. He’s very accurate, strong arm, has all the measurables that you want at the next level,” Leipold said. Kansas allows just 6.08 yards per dropback. Holding Oklahoma State close to that number would take away the Cowboys’ fastest route to a double-digit lead. The Jayhawks also average 5.39 yards per rush, which gives them a way to shorten the game. Oklahoma State has the better offense overall, ranking 12th in ESPN’s offensive efficiency ratings, and its 5.53 yards per carry keeps defenses honest. I like the Cowboys in a shootout, but Kansas has enough on both sides of the ball to stay within six. Picks: Oklahoma State 31-27, Kansas +6, Under 64.5 Baylor (+4.5) at No. 18 Houston: Upset watch 8.5 Bears wide receiver Gavin Freeman (6) runs with the ball against Kansas Jayhawks safety Corey Gordon (3) | Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Kickoff: Saturday, N

item.title: Intel faced a choice: Give Trump 10% or face the consequences
item.description: The message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your company. Right now. Or else. Do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a company call contained in a federal lawsuit. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.” Shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors. But the Trump administration official “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Tyson Fury’s wife withdraws claim that boxer has schizophrenia
item.description: Paris Fury, the wife of British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury, has withdrawn her earlier claim that her husband was diagnosed with schizophrenia, clarifying that he has never been formally diagnosed with the condition. Paris made the clarification after an earlier version of an upcoming Netflix documentary about the boxer featured her describing him as having “mild schizophrenia”. In a statement, she said she had used the term while recalling a conversation about Tyson’s mental health struggles several years ago, but acknowledged that it was not an accurate description of his medical history. “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary,” she said. “I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.” She added that mental health was complex and that finding the right words to describe someone’s experiences was not always easy. “Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love,” she said. Paris also praised her husband for speaking openly about his struggles and thanked the public for supporting their family. Netflix confirmed that it had updated the documentary following the family’s clarification about Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis. “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch,” the streaming platform said. The earlier comments had attracted attention from the British Boxing Board of Control, which indicated that it was investigating the matter. The 38 year old boxer is scheduled to face Joshua in an all British heavyweight showdown in Cardiff on December 11, with the vacant WBA title expected to be at stake. Tyson has previously spoken publicly about his mental health struggles following his victory over Ukraine’s Wladimir Klitschko in 2015, when he became world heavyweight champion. After the victory, he took a break of nearly three years from boxing, during which he battled suicidal thoughts, drug and alcohol problems, and significant weight gain. Reflecting on that period in the documentary, Tyson said he experienced severe psychological distress. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” he said. “I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 percent thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.” He later returned to boxing and regained the world heavyweight title by defeating Deontay Wilder in February 2020. Tyson suffered the first two defeats of his professional career against Oleksandr Usyk in 2024, leaving him with 39 professional fights on his record. The post Tyson Fury’s wife withdraws claim

item.title: US: Thanksgiving storms cause flooding and travel chaos
item.description: Severe storms battered the US East Coast on Thursday, bringing torrential rain, strong winds and coastal flooding. Nearly one million homes were left without power, while hundreds of flights were cancelled and thousands delayed during one of the country's busiest travel periods. The weather also forced the postponement of New York's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade until Saturday.

item.title: Black Friday: The evolution of a shopping phenomenon
item.description: Once defined by crowds queuing outside shops for one-off bargains, Black Friday has evolved into weeks of online promotions. As discounts spread throughout the year, consumers are becoming more cautious about advertised deals, increasingly turning to AI and price comparisons to find genuine bargains. Camille Knight looks at the origins of the global shopping phenomenon.

item.title: Lloyds and Bank of Scotland apps fall over on payday
item.description: Lloyds Bank and Bank of Scotland customers reported problems accessing online banking and transferring money on Friday morning. Reports on Downdetector began rising around 1000 UTC. Lloyds also acknowledged problems on its service status page . A reader who supplied the screenshot below noted the particularly awkward timing: the last Friday of the month is payday for many workers. One customer tweeted that she had "no food at home and cannot shop because I cannot transfer funds from my secondary Lloyds account to my main one. At this point I'm just going to withdraw every penny the moment I'm paid, so much for Internet banking. Never had this years ago." Bank of Scotland, another Lloyds Banking Group brand, reported similar problems on its service status page : " We're aware some customers are having issues with our app and online banking at the moment. We're sorry about this and are working hard to fix it." Earlier this year, a botched overnight software update at Lloyds Banking Group potentially exposed other customers' transaction information to almost 448,000 app users. In a letter to Parliament's Treasury Committee, consumer relationships CEO Jasjyot Singh blamed a defect in the API handling transaction data. The incident affected Lloyds, Halifax, and Bank of Scotland, and prompted goodwill payments to thousands of customers. Lloyds Banking Group said late last year that it had more than 21 million mobile app users and over 23 million digitally active customers. A spokesperson for Lloyds Banking Group told The Register : "We're aware some customers are having difficulty accessing the app this morning. We’re sorry for the inconvenience and are working to get things back to normal as quickly as possible." ®

item.title: Ross County have 102 goals and British football’s best start but is it a fairytale?
item.description: There is cynicism and jealousy but one of County’s top scorers is 39 as club try to climb leagues again after tumbling It was a vidiprinter moment worthy of a double take. Ross County 1 Cove Rangers 1 (Keir 52). Would Cove, scrapping for survival in Scottish League One, put an unlikely end last Saturday to the most emphatic run in British senior football? Don’t be silly, retorted County; four goals in the closing 17 minutes extended the Dingwall side’s goal difference to plus 45 (for 56, against 11). Played 16, won 14, drawn two. There is as much chance of Mike McCarthy settling down for Christmas dinner with Aaron Rodgers as County missing out on promotion back to Scotland’s second tier. Taking in cup competitions they have scored 102 goals this season. Assessment from the captain, Brian Graham, of a frankly irrelevant loss on penalties to Stenhousemuir in the Challenge Cup epitomises the County approach. “We should have been five- or six-nil up at half-time,” an irked Graham says. “That shows the standards we have set. We lost a dubious goal, which shouldn’t have stood.” Earlier in that competition County whacked 14 past a Hearts youth side before defeating a Celtic B team including two Chelsea loanees and a £3m midfielder. Continue reading...

item.title: The absolute best Black Friday deals we’ve found (so far)
item.description: This year’s Black Friday deals have launched in waves over the past several weeks, but now the floodgates have officially opened. You can now take advantage of the lowest prices we’ve seen in-store and online for video games, wireless earbuds, TVs, e-readers, robot vacuums, and so much more. We can’t guarantee a deal you’ve had your eye on will last through Cyber Monday; however, if prior years are any indication, most will stick around through the long holiday weekend. As usual, we sorted through thousands of deals to find the ones truly worth sharing, with an eye for the products and services we’ve tested here at The Verge . With prices up across multiple categories due to RAMageddon, some deals may not seem as big as in prior years. For example, Apple’s latest MacBook Air recently fell to its pre-price hike level for the first time since July. That’s a deal to us, and several other discounts are taking a similar shape. We’ll provide context when possible and keep this post updated throughout the day. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 The cost continues to fall on Samsung’s latest, best foldable yet. The Z Fold 8 is a passport-style phone, like the iPhone Duo, with fast performance and slick design. item.content:encoded: This year’s Black Friday deals have launched in waves over the past several weeks, but now the floodgates have officially opened. You can now take advantage of the lowest prices we’ve seen in-store and online for video games, wireless earbuds, TVs, e-readers, robot vacuums, and so much more. We can’t guarantee a deal you’ve had your eye on will last through Cyber Monday; however, if prior years are any indication, most will stick around through the long holiday weekend. As usual, we sorted through thousands of deals to find the ones truly worth sharing, with an eye for the products and services we’ve tested here at The Verge . With prices up across multiple categories due to RAMageddon, some deals may not seem as big as in prior years. For example, Apple’s latest MacBook Air recently fell to its pre-price hike level for the first time since July. That’s a deal to us, and several other discounts are taking a similar shape. item.title: Arsenic In The Water: Thailand Presses Myanmar Over Mining Pollution
item.description: As pollution mounts in its rivers, food and water, Thailand is pressing neighbouring Myanmar to tackle unregulated mining, while urging China to exert its influence in the war-ravaged nation. Tap water supplies to 14 villages in Mae Sai district near the Myanmar border were suspended earlier this month after arsenic levels were found to be nearly 30 times government limits. Bangkok this week hosted the first Thai-Myanmar working group on the issue — also attended by the Chinese ambassador — where it said tests proved rare-earth and gold mines in Myanmar were causing the pollution downstream. The two sides agreed to joint water sampling on the Kok and Sai rivers. This photo taken on June 5, 2026 shows Wan Wiriya, assistant professor from Chiang Mai University, showing the results of an arsenic level test from a water sample (C) taken from the Kok River, next to a control sample of drinking water (R) near the the northern Thai city of Chiang Rai. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP But there was no public agreement to Thailand’s request for a six-month suspension of operations, and how one could be implemented remains unclear, with Myanmar’s military not in full control. Bangkok is also looking to China, the main importer of rare-earth materials from Myanmar, to pressure private Chinese operators, as a months-long concern becomes increasingly urgent. Authorities warned residents this week against eating certain shellfish and other river species after tests in northern and northeastern Thailand found dangerous levels of arsenic and lead. Saengwaree Suvirakan, a farmer from Tha Ton in Chiang Mai province who joined a protest in Bangkok this week, said fish stocks were declining in any case. “Now with the mines the fish are all gone,” she said. ‘Not from nature’ This photo taken on June 4, 2026 shows fishermen and their boats near the confluence of the Kok River and Mekong River in Chiang Saen, northern Thailand’s Chiang Rai province. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP At the joint talks, Thai ministers said high arsenic levels in the Kok and Sai rivers could only have come from rare-earth and gold mines on the Myanmar side. “Arsenic does not come from nature, it came from mining sites. The source was from (Myanmar’s) Shan state, no-one disagrees,” Science Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat said. But how to tackle it remains an issue. Thanapon Piman, senior research fellow at the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI), welcomed the agreement on joint sampling sites. “This is going to be a first step to agree on the evidence, otherwise you cannot move to the next step, like stopping mining activity,” he told AFP. But Myanmar intervening to stop mining would be “really difficult”, he added. Multiple ethnic armed groups have been operating there for decades, while a 2021 military coup sparked an ongoing civil war. Thai officials pinpointed two gold mines just over the border from Mae Sai as the main source of high arsenic levels in the Sai River. Different group

item.content:encoded: As pollution mounts in its rivers, food and water, Thailand is pressing neighbouring Myanmar to tackle unregulated mining, while urging China to exert its influence in the war-ravaged nation. The two sides agreed to joint water sampling on the Kok and Sai rivers. This photo taken on June 5, 2026 shows Wan Wiriya, assistant professor from Chiang Mai University, showing the results of an arsenic level test from a water sample (C) taken from the Kok River, next to a control sample of drinking water (R) near the the northern Thai city of Chiang Rai. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP But there was no public agreement to Thailand’s request for a six-month suspension of operations, and how one could be implemented remains unclear, with Myanmar’s military not in full control. Bangkok is also looking to China, the main importer of rare-earth materials from Myanmar, to pressure private Chinese operators, as a months-long concern becomes increasingly urgent. Authorities warned residents this week against eating certain shellfish and other river species after tests in northern and northeastern Thailand found dangerous levels of arsenic and lead. Saengwaree Suvirakan, a farmer from Tha Ton in Chiang Mai province who joined a protest in Bangkok this week, said fish stocks were declining in any case. “Now with the mines the fish are all gone,” she said. ‘Not from nature’ This photo taken on June 4, 2026 shows fishermen and their boats near the confluence of the Kok River and Mekong River in Chiang Saen, northern Thailand’s Chiang Rai province. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP At the joint talks, Thai ministers said high arsenic levels in the Kok and Sai rivers could only have come from rare-earth and gold mines on the Myanmar side. “Arsenic does not come from nature, it came from mining sites. The source was from (Myanmar’s) Shan state, no-one disagrees,” Science Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat said. But how to tackle it remains an issue. Thanapon Piman, senior research fellow at the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI), welcomed the agreement on joint sampling sites. “This is going to be a first step to agree on the evidence, otherwise you cannot move to the next step, like stopping mining activity,” he told AFP. But Myanmar intervening to stop mining would be “really difficult”, he added. Multiple ethnic armed groups have been operating there for decades, while a 2021 military coup sparked an ongoing civil war. Thai officials pinpointed two gold mines just over the border from Mae Sai as the main source of high arsenic levels in the Sai River. Different groups control different parts of the wider area, among them Myanmar military and the United Wa State Army, an ethnic armed group with close ties to China. Mining suspension This photo taken on June 4, 2026 shows a view of the Mekong River and the Golden Triangle Special Economic Zone within Laos’ Bokeo province (R), from Chiang Saen, northern Thailand’s Chiang Rai province. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP Many mining operations in Myanmar are run by Chinese companies, and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul raised pollution with President Xi Jinping this month. “China acknowledged that they are aware of mining by private Chinese companies in Shan state,” Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said. “China made clear that they do not support activities that are improper, illegal or cause harm.” Thailand sought China’s backing for its six-month mining suspension, officials said. But China’s foreign ministry declined to comment, with a spokeswoman saying only that Beijing “pays close attention” to the pollution issue and would provide technical support. The SEI’s Thanapon said Thailand could help “slow down mining activity” by pressuring the supply chain on its side of the border. Thailand is planning to ban exports to Myanmar of two chemicals used in rare-earth mining, and restrict imports from the country of six minerals including gold and rare earths, to limit unauthorised mines’ access to buyers. For farmer Saengwaree, there is no time to waste. Even traditional customs were being hit by the pollution, she said, noting this week’s Loy Krathong festival, where residents and tourists send out small floats into waterways. “Usually it is very busy,” she said, “but right now there is nobody in Tha Ton, there are no tourists.” The post Arsenic In The Water: Thailand Presses Myanmar Over Mining Pollution appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Full list: Italy unveils 14 African countries eligible for work visas
item.description: Italy has listed 14 African countries whose citizens are eligible to apply for work visas under its 2026–2028 immigration programme, offering employment opportunities to foreign workers across several sectors of its economy. Nigeria is among the African countries on the list, alongside Ghana, Senegal, Morocco, Egypt and 10 others. The programme forms part of Italy’s broader labour migration policy, which seeks to admit foreign workers to address labour shortages and meet the country’s employment needs. Under the programme, the Italian government has reserved 25,000 work permits annually for citizens of 38 designated countries, including the 14 African nations. The African countries named are: Algeria Ivory Coast Egypt Ethiopia The Gambia Ghana Mali Morocco Mauritius Niger Nigeria Senegal Sudan Tunisia. The employment opportunities cover sectors including agriculture, forestry, fishing, food production, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail trade, hospitality, tourism, transportation, logistics, healthcare and social assistance. According to the Italian Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, the immigration programme provides for a total of 497,550 foreign workers to enter Italy between 2026 and 2028. The allocation is divided into 164,850 workers for 2026, 165,850 for 2027 and 166,850 for 2028. The figures cover seasonal and non-seasonal employment as well as self-employment. However, inclusion on the list does not automatically guarantee a work visa. Applicants must secure employment from an Italian employer, who is generally required to apply for the relevant work authorisation, known as nulla osta , before the worker proceeds with the visa application. For the 2026 allocation, applications for seasonal agricultural jobs were scheduled to open on January 12, while those for seasonal tourism jobs were scheduled for February 9. Applications for non-seasonal employment under the relevant categories were scheduled for February 16 and 18, 2026. The programme is part of Italy’s efforts to address labour shortages through regulated migration while strengthening cooperation with countries of origin. Vanguard News The post Full list: Italy unveils 14 African countries eligible for work visas appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UK Reform leader vows to scrap Graduate visa route used by 20,478 Nigerians
item.description: UK Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, has vowed to scrap the United Kingdom’s Graduate visa route if his party wins power, a move that could affect thousands of Nigerians who use the scheme to remain in the country after completing their studies. Farage announced the proposal in a post on X on Thursday, arguing that the route allows foreign graduates to stay in the UK for two years after completing their degrees, competing with British workers for entry level jobs or potentially claiming asylum. Figures published by the UK Home Office on November 26 showed that 20,478 Nigerian nationals received grants under the Graduate route in the year to September 2026, making Nigerians the third largest group of beneficiaries. Indian nationals topped the list with 66,552 grants, followed by Pakistanis with 24,768. The three nationalities accounted for about 69 per cent of all grants recorded during the period. The Graduate route allows international students who have completed eligible courses at UK universities to remain in the country and work or look for employment without needing an immediate job offer or sponsorship. Reform UK’s home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf, has described the scheme as “a scam on the British people” and proposed replacing it with a 30 day period for graduates to secure a qualifying job that meets an economic value test. The party said about 800,000 Graduate visas, including those issued to dependants, had been granted since the route was introduced in July 2021. Yusuf also cited Home Office figures showing that 5,130 asylum claims were made by people who had previously held Graduate visas in the year to June 2026, twice the number recorded in the preceding year. The pledge comes as the Labour government is already preparing to reduce the standard duration of the Graduate visa from two years to 18 months from January 1, 2027. The change will not apply to graduates from institutions that meet certain compliance and labour market outcome standards. However, Reform UK has yet to clarify how its proposed abolition would affect people who already hold Graduate visas or international students currently studying in the country. The latest Home Office figures also showed a decline in the number of Nigerian students receiving sponsored study visas. Grants to Nigerian nationals fell by 34 per cent to 19,734 in the year to September 2026, representing about six per cent of the total. The post UK Reform leader vows to scrap Graduate visa route used by 20,478 Nigerians appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
item.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®

item.title: Tyson Fury’s Wife Backtracks On Schizophrenia Claim
item.description: Paris Fury, the wife of Tyson Fury, has retracted her claim that the British heavyweight was diagnosed with schizophrenia just months after he was crowned world champion in 2015. In clips promoting a Netflix documentary, the boxer spoke about his mental health struggles following his victory over Ukraine’s Wladimir Klitschko in Germany. Paris Fury said Tyson Fury had “mild schizophrenia” in an initial version of the documentary, which will be released on Friday. Netflix said it had worked to “update” the footage in light of her clarification. Fury, 38, is due to face Anthony Joshua in a long-awaited all-British showdown in Cardiff on December 11. Britain’s boxer Anthony Joshua celebrates winning against Albania’s boxer Kristian Prenga in their heavyweight boxing fight at the Jeddah Superdome in Jeddah on July 26, 2026. (Photo by AFP) Paris Fury’s comments come after the British Boxing Board of Control indicated that it was investigating the comments, though Robert Smith, the board’s general secretary, told the BBC it was “fairly confident” he would be cleared to fight Joshua. “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary,” Paris said in a statement. “I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. “Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love. “I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.” Fury has been open about his mental health struggles since beating Klitschko, after which he took a break of nearly three years from boxing. Britain’s Tyson Fury (C) celebrates after his victory over Russia’s Arslanbek Makhmudov in their heavyweight ‘Clash of the Giants’ contest at the Tottenham Hotspur stadium in London on April 11, 2026. (Photo by Henry NICHOLLS / AFP) His weight ballooned while he battled suicidal thoughts and drug and alcohol problems. Fury admitted hearing “voices in my mind” following his win, adding: “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. “I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 percent thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.” Fury became world heavyweight champion for a second time when he beat WBC champion Deontay Wilder in February 2020. Despite losing twice to Oleksandr Usyk in 2024, the only losses in his 39-fight professional career, Fury could become a three-time world champion when he takes on Joshua with the vacant WBA title set to be on the line. item.title: Saudi Strike Kills 11 In Yemen
item.description: A Saudi strike killed 11 people on Friday in western Yemen, Houthi media said, a day after an attack by the Iran-backed movement on an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia. A Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government has been regularly bombing areas controlled by the armed group since the country’s civil war reignited over the summer. In response, Houthi forces have been targeting the oil-rich kingdom almost daily, hitting energy facilities, airports and the financial district of the capital, Riyadh. Saudi warplanes carried out a raid on a residential building in the city of Al-Turba in Taiz governorate on Friday, killing “11 citizens, most of them children,” the Houthis’ Saba news agency said, citing a local source. The agency also reported strikes targeting fuel tanks in the Saada region, the movement’s birthplace and stronghold. Smoke billows from the Yemeni capital Sanaa on November 26, 2026 after Houthi media reported a series of Saudi airstrikes against territories held by the Iran-backed group, hours after it struck Riyadh. Photo by AFP On Thursday, the Houthis targeted the Jazan refinery in southern Saudi Arabia, killing a Nepalese worker and injuring several other people, according to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA). The attack also triggered a fire that led to the shutdown of the facility, the SPA said. Yemen plunged back into war in July, after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the Middle East war. Hostilities intensified in September when the Houthis, who already controlled the most densely populated parts of Yemen, seized the western coastline overlooking the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait on the Red Sea. The Houthis are now advancing toward Aden, a major southern city where the government has taken refuge after being driven out of the capital Sanaa in 2015. Since the conflict resumed, fighting in Yemen has killed more than 2,300 people and displaced over 364,000, according to the United Nations. In Saudi Arabia, Houthi attacks have killed 27 people, according to the kingdom’s authorities. The post Saudi Strike Kills 11 In Yemen appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Books, bikes, and The Burbs: These are Ars staff’s holiday gift picks for 2026
item.description: The holiday shopping season is upon us, and as is our custom, we're here with a list of Ars staffers' favorite recent purchases that could make good gifts. (Or maybe they might be a gift you get yourself!) Rather than try to write a definitive "best gifts for your sister or brother" type of guide, we simply polled Ars staffers on stuff they've actually bought this year that they recommend. The thinking is that if we're into it, hopefully some of you or your friends or family might be. As such, there's no rhyme or reason to these selections, really; it's just a list of stuff we bought that we're happy about. It's heavy on interesting books and cycling accessories, but there are some gadgets and the like in here, too. For each gadget (or whatever else it might be), we have a brief description of how or why we’ve been using this particular thing and why we would recommend it. Our picks are ordered by price, from lowest to highest. Note, though, that the prices of these products are listed as they were when the list was written. Online retailers often adjust prices frequently, especially around Black Friday, so just a heads up: The price might be different by the time you read this. Read full article Comments

item.title: The SE 3 is the Apple Watch most people should buy on Black Friday
item.description: The SE 3 adds an always-on display to Apple’s budget-friendly wearable. | Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge During Black Friday, the Apple Watch SE 3 is on sale in the 40mm / GPS configuration at Amazon , Walmart , and Target starting around $179 ($70 off), $20 less than its previous lowest price. The 44mm variant, meanwhile, is on sale at Amazon , Walmart , and Target starting at around $209 (also $70 off), also beating its previous low by $20. Apple Watch SE 3 Where to Buy: $249 $179 at Amazon (40mm, GPS) $249 $179 at Walmart (40mm, GPS) $279 $209 at Amazon (44mm, GPS) Despite having launched over a year ago, the Apple Watch SE 3 is still the Apple Watch model we recommend for most people. It includes many of the trademark features of higher-end Apple Watch models like the Series 12, including an always-on display, double-tap and wrist flick gestures, fast-charging, and on-device Siri. The compromise is that the SE 3 lacks some of the more advanced health features found on more expensive models, like blood oxygen and EKG sensing. The battery life also isn’t quite as strong, but if you don’t need as many health-tracking sensors, it’s a much better value, especially at this price. Read our Apple Watch SE 3 review .

item.title: UN warns of worsening hunger in northern Nigeria, 15 other areas
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The United Nations has warned of worsening hunger across 16 regions of the world over the next six months, identifying northern Nigeria, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia and Yemen as areas facing the highest risk of acute food insecurity. The warning was contained in a joint report by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP), which attributed the growing food crisis to armed conflicts, climate extremes, economic shocks and declining humanitarian assistance. The report, released on Friday, covers the period from December 2026 to May 2027 and cautioned that conditions could deteriorate further in several African countries as conflict and extreme weather events continue to disrupt livelihoods and food production. It identified Sudan and South Sudan as countries where famine remains a plausible risk, particularly in parts of North Darfur. The agencies also expressed concern over rising political violence, noting that incidents had increased by more than 15 per cent compared with the same period last year. The development, according to the report, has triggered significant displacement in recent months, particularly in South Sudan and Yemen, further worsening the humanitarian situation. It also highlighted a sharp decline in humanitarian funding to the five countries facing the highest levels of concern. According to the agencies, humanitarian assistance to the countries fell by nearly two-thirds between 2022 and 2025, dropping from $5.1bn to $2bn. “While conflict, economic shocks, climate extremes and access constraints have remained the primary drivers of these crises, declining humanitarian resources have reduced the capacity to sustain gains and mitigate worsening conditions,” the report stated. The agencies warned that previous humanitarian interventions had helped prevent famine in affected areas, but the improvements were often temporary, with severe food insecurity returning within a few years. Other areas classified as facing very high concern include Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Palestine and Haiti. The report noted that gang violence in Haiti had displaced about 1.5 million people and disrupted humanitarian access, while the Democratic Republic of Congo continues to grapple with an Ebola outbreak. Chad, Uganda, Southern Africa and the Central American Dry Corridor were also added to the list of hunger hotspots. The agencies warned that the impact of El Niño could worsen food production in several of these regions, particularly through irregular rainfall, drought and flooding. item.content:encoded: By Enitan Abdultawab The United Nations has warned of worsening hunger across 16 regions of the world over the next six months, identifying northern Nigeria, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia and Yemen as areas facing the highest risk of acute food insecurity. The warning was contained in a joint report by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP), which attributed the growing food crisis to armed conflicts, climate extremes, economic shocks and declining humanitarian assistance. The report, released on Friday, covers the period from December 2026 to May 2027 and cautioned that conditions could deteriorate further in several African countries as conflict and extreme weather events continue to disrupt livelihoods and food production. It identified Sudan and South Sudan as countries where famine remains a plausible risk, particularly in parts of North Darfur. The agencies also expressed concern over rising political violence, noting that incidents had increased by more than 15 per cent compared with the same period last year. The development, according to the report, has triggered significant displacement in recent months, particularly in South Sudan and Yemen, further worsening the humanitarian situation. It also highlighted a sharp decline in humanitarian funding to the five countries facing the highest levels of concern. According to the agencies, humanitarian assistance to the countries fell by nearly two-thirds between 2022 and 2025, dropping from $5.1bn to $2bn. “While conflict, economic shocks, climate extremes and access constraints have remained the primary drivers of these crises, declining humanitarian resources have reduced the capacity to sustain gains and mitigate worsening conditions,” the report stated. The agencies warned that previous humanitarian interventions had helped prevent famine in affected areas, but the improvements were often temporary, with severe food insecurity returning within a few years. Other areas classified as facing very high concern include Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Palestine and Haiti. The report noted that gang violence in Haiti had displaced about 1.5 million people and disrupted humanitarian access, while the Democratic Republic of Congo continues to grapple with an Ebola outbreak. Chad, Uganda, Southern Africa and the Central American Dry Corridor were also added to the list of hunger hotspots. The agencies warned that the impact of El Niño could worsen food production in several of these regions, particularly through irregular rainfall, drought and flooding. They estimated that about 49 million additional people could be pushed into acute food insecurity by the end of 2027 as a result of the particularly intense El Niño conditions expected to persist into next spring. “El Niño-related rainfall deficits and elevated temperatures have already contributed to crop losses in the Central American Dry Corridor and Eastern Africa, while also threatening the upcoming agricultural season in Southern Africa,” the report said. It further warned that heavy rainfall and localised flooding could worsen conditions for displaced households in Gaza by damaging shelters and disrupting essential services. The FAO and WFP called for urgent humanitarian interventions, including the provision of adapted seeds, improved protection for livestock and water supplies, as well as timely assistance to vulnerable communities. However, they disclosed that a joint plan to address the crisis was facing a funding shortfall of $125m. “Targeted humanitarian action is urgently needed to save lives and livelihoods across all hunger hotspots,” the report stated, adding that immediate intervention was critical in areas facing the highest risk to prevent starvation and loss of life. The post UN warns of worsening hunger in northern Nigeria, 15 other areas appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
item.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. No number of testimonials replaces a written contract that states what you are paying for, what you are not paying for, and what happens if a payment is missed. None of this is complicated. item.dc:creator: Israel Toluwalope Olaleye
item.content:encoded: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. No number of testimonials replaces a written contract that states what you are paying for, what you are not paying for, and what happens if a payment is missed. None of this is complicated. It is just not taught. The irony is that my generation may need this knowledge more than any before us. We are buying earlier, often on instalment plans, often far from where we live. Many of us are buying from abroad, relying on a cousin’s video call and a WhatsApp voice note. We are also buying in places our parents may never have considered. Ogun State, for example. In the most recent quarterly report from Nigeria Property Centre, rental listings in Ogun drew roughly three times as many enquiries per listing as those in Lagos. People priced out of Lagos are already living there. Young buyers have noticed, and so have people who would happily sell them land that does not exist. I have come to believe that the most valuable thing a real estate professional can offer is not a property. It is clarity. I have seen buyers relax, visibly, when someone finally explains the difference between a Certificate of Occupancy and a survey plan, or tells them plainly which fees are coming and which are not. I have also seen people who were afraid to invest for years finally do it, not because they were persuaded, but because they understood. If you are about to buy your first piece of land, here is what I wish someone sits my generation down to say. Don’t let anyone’s confidence replace your own checks. Get your own lawyer to search the title. Get a surveyor to chart the land. Ask, in writing, what the price includes and what it does not, including any family or community fee. Ask what happens to your money if you cannot complete an instalment plan. And verify the person you are dealing with, including people like me. Our parents had communities that remembered. We have screenshots, receipts and group chats. That can work, but only if we learn to ask the questions our parents never had to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We can still teach each other. The post Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today? appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .
