item.title: AWS adds virtual iPhones to its cloud
item.description: AWS now offers two new types of cloudy computers: emulated Androids and simulated iPhones. The cloudy colossus announced both virtual offerings on Wednesday. They’re part of its Device Farm service, which previously saw AWS offer developers the chance to test their software on actual iOS and Android devices that reside in the Amazonian cloud. AWS will now also host virtual devices running Android and iOS. AWS touts the virtual mobile devices as superior to physical devices. “With virtual devices, you can shift testing left to stages that need high speed and volume, such as pull requests, code merges, and smoke tests, and keep real devices for later stages that need high fidelity, such as regression and release testing,” the cloudy business unit argues in its launch announcement. AWS also says developers can get to work faster on a virtual iPhone or Pixel. “Virtual devices running the latest device and OS typically start in seconds, and others start in around a minute,” the outfit argues. That may sound appetizing, but Amazon’s menu of virtual devices is short and bland. When The Register logged on as an AWS user, the only emulated Android phone listed was a Google Pixel 10, running Android 15, 16, or 17. An emulated Pixel tablet running Android 17 is also on the menu. At the time of writing, we could find only a virtual iPhone 16, running iOS 18.6, 23.61, and 27.0. Analyst firm Counterpoint’s list of the world’s top 10 best-selling smartphones in Q2 of 2026 does not include a single Pixel device. The iPhone 16 occupies 10 th place. iPhone 17 models occupy the first, second, third, and seventh place on the list. AWS might excite more developers if it adds emulators for the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Galaxy A07 4G, A17 5G, A17 4G, and Galaxy S26, as they occupy the fourth, fifth, sixth, eighth and ninth places on Counterpoint’s list. Amazon’s choice of a Pixel tablet is also an oddity given analyst firm IDC doesn’t list Google among its top five tablet vendors . Amazon does offer physical Galaxy A17 devices and three versions of the iPhone 17. But Device Farm doesn’t offer any foldable devices, meaning developers struggling to wrap their heads around the iPhone Duo will need either ask Apple for a loaner or shell out $2,000 to acquire one. At least developers don’t have to change behavior to access the few virtual devices AWS offers, as existing Device Farm APIs and test frameworks will work on real or notional machines. ®

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 27 – The Moon Watchers
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 27 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The Moon Watchers Explanation: On November 24 , all denizens of our fair planet could watch the Moon rise opposite the setting Sun. Easy to spot in twilight skies above fields, fences, backyards, and even stone walls, the Moon was big and bright, and at its full phase . Known to some as a Beaver Moon, November’s Full Moon was also near perigee, the closest point in its elliptical orbit around planet Earth. That made it one of the biggest and brightest Full Moons, also known as a supermoon . In fact, November’s Full Moon was the first in a series of four consecutive Full Moon’s near perigee. So your next chance to watch a supermoon rise will be when the Cold Moon rises on December 23. item.title: Shivelyuch Socked In
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Shivelyuch Socked In Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search In the same way that Shivelyuch (also called Shiveluch) frequently displays volcanic activity, it is also chronically obscured by clouds. When the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured this image on November 8, 2026, clouds encroached on the snowy mountain on Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula . But they hovered beneath the volcano’s 3,283-meter (10,771-foot) peak, leaving a clear opening over its caldera and northern upper slopes. The upper reaches of Shivelyuch feature a caldera 9 kilometers (5.6 miles) wide that is open to the south. A lava dome , formed by vents extruding viscous magma, appears as a dark area within it. Lava domes on Shivelyuch go through cycles of growth and collapse, with collapses sometimes setting off fast-moving avalanches of hot ash and rock called pyroclastic flows . In November 2026, effusive eruptions of lava and explosive activity at Shivelyuch had been ongoing for months , according to reports from the Kamchatka Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT). And despite frequent cloudiness, satellites regularly detect thermal anomalies from the volcano. On the day of this image, KVERT reported that a plume of resuspended ash drifted 120 kilometers (75 miles) to the east. That kind of activity is relatively tame for the mountain. Explosions from Shivelyuch periodically send ash several kilometers up into the atmosphere, where it can travel great distances and pose risks to aircraft . In July 2026, an ash plume rode the jet stream over the Bering Sea into Alaskan airspace, according to news reports , prompting the cancellation of multiple flights. Some of Larson’s most beloved comic strips feature animals drawn in his signature style, including dogs, chickens, and especially cows . He often gave these animals human-like intelligence and other anthropomorphic traits and depicted them in very human-like scenarios.

item.title: Free e-government platform that serves two billion people in ten countries has critical SQL injection bug
item.description: India’s free e-government platform has a critical SQL injection flaw that thousands of organizations must patch to protect up to two billion citizens. The platform is called the Digital Infrastructure for Governance (Impact and Transformation) – aka DIGIT – and is a modular suite that offers common services such as authentication and payment collection. Third party developers can also create DIGIT modules, and plenty have done so and now offer add-ons that handle tasks as diverse as managing birth and death certificates, revenue collection, and running water treatment plants. DIGIT is ubiquitous in India, where all state and union territory governments use the platform, as do over 20,000 local government entities. India also exports DIGIT under its policy of turning software created for its own needs into “digital public goods” (DPI) that it happily gives away to other nations. Nine nations have implemented DIGIT to some degree, among them Mozambique, Liberia, Senegal, Nigeria, Burundi, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Jamaica, and Sri Lanka India’s population is 1.4 billion. Indonesia’s is 280 million and Nigeria is home to 240 million. DIGIT is therefore used by governments that serve over two billion people, some of whom are now at risk thanks to CVE-2026-136706 , a 9.3-rated SQL injection flaw present in DIGIT which allows “improper neutralization of user supplied input while constructing SQL queries and execution in the affected User and Access Control Service components.” “An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted input through the affected API endpoint to the targeted system,” according to CERT-IN . “Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary SQL queries, potentially resulting in unauthorized disclosure, modification or deletion of database information on the targeted system.” eGov India, which oversees work on DIGIT, has released source code for an update that fixes the problem. While local government users of DIGIT typically access it as SaaS, through large implementations run by national or state governments, over 1,000 deployments are live across various cities and other entities. Those orgs can therefore add patching DIGIT to their urgent to-do lists, along with fixing Java , PHP , vCenter and any other widely used technologies that suddenly need an urgent security update. ®

item.title: The token factory never sleeps
item.description: Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. Conversely, enterprises are often working with small operations teams in existing datacenters that may not have been built with AI in mind. That means they need to think harder about maintenance windows, existing management tooling and predictable deployment. And they'll often be retrofitting halls whose racks rarely draw more than 30
item.dc:creator: Robin Birtstone
item.content:encoded: Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. Conversely, enterprises are often working with small operations teams in existing datacenters that may not have been built with AI in mind. That means they need to think harder about maintenance windows, existing management tooling and predictable deployment. And they'll often be retrofitting halls whose racks rarely draw more than 30 kW. In token factory terms, the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System is the core compute engine. Each system puts eight NVIDIA HGX Rubin GPUs on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, linked by sixth-generation NVLink. ASUS has designed its equipment to support the constraints above. Its customers can choose between the hybrid and fully liquid-cooled models, and they can opt for partial or full rack configurations by buying multiple trays. This enables them to match their facilities' needs. Peak performance versus sustained performance The other difference between model providers and enterprises lies in which numbers they care about. Peak performance is different from sustained performance. The first is a specification sheet number, while the second is what the GPU actually delivers hours into a heavy workload. Production inference tends to run continuously, especially when it uses agents, as opposed to training, which is a sporadic job. So the sustained figure is the one that buyers pay for. Heat becomes a real issue here because when cooling can't keep up, GPUs throttle their clocks to protect themselves. In a token factory, a throttled GPU is a slower production line. The more advanced the architecture becomes, the higher the stakes get. NVIDIA HGX Rubin GPU has raised them to their highest point, delivering up to 400 petaflops of NVFP4 inference per eight-GPU board, according to NVIDIA's sparse specification. This is screamingly fast, but the increased heat per board means less margin before throttling. ASUS designed both models to put direct-to-chip liquid cooling on every GPU. Only the 3U unit leaves the CPUs on air cooling. ASUS also says it puts every configuration through a 168-hour stress test. Power and heat set the shape of the rack As boards increase their compute density, pushing up the power and heat requirements, planning naturally has to move out of the server room and into the facility. That's the case whether you're talking about an entire NVL72 rack or a stack of eight-GPU servers like the ASUS systems. There are other things to consider beyond heat. Few datacenters run racks drawing more than 30 kilowatts, says th e Uptime Institute . Yet a single liquid-cooled tray of the ASUS systems draws up to 23.9 kilowatts, and a full rack of nine has a power budget of about 216 kilowatts. Floor loading and power distribution matter as much as cooling. NVIDIA HGX Rubin GPU raises the stakes again. The eight-GPU format enables organizations to buy their computing power in more granular steps. That's where the two ASUS systems come into their own. With few enterprises needing a training cluster at NVL72 scale, the advantage is that an HGX box lets them buy AI compute in digestible pieces. The ASUS systems also come with a 54V busbar and cable-free board-to-board design. ASUS says this simplifies assembly and improves reliability. Connectivity, storage and management So that's space, power and heat. But a GPU board won't produce many tokens if the network, storage or operational tooling can't feed it properly. Agent workloads move context and data all the time, so east-west bandwidth and local storage are key to effective utilization. Any new equipment should ideally slot straight into the enterprise's existing management and monitoring tooling. ASUS ships the whole rack, including servers, networking, power and storage, as a single blueprint. ASUS pre-validates this AI Factory reference architecture at rack scale so that organizations can plan for future growth. That includes dedicated management nodes and a management switch. Inside each tray, ASUS has sized the data paths to keep the GPUs fed. Eight OSFP ports on NVIDIA ConnectX-9 give every GPU 800Gb/s of east-west bandwidth to the rest of the cluster, and an NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPU adds two 400GbE ports. Within the board, the eight GPUs talk to each other over NVLink at 3,600GB/s, ASUS says. The 2U tray takes up to 4TB of DDR5 system memory and has eight E1.S NVMe bays for fast local data access, while the 3U model offers a choice of U.2 or E1.S drives. Built to be serviced The other issue for enterprises putting AI inference into production is service and maintenance. In a liquid-cooled box, routine fixes can mean draining a coolant loop, which is downtime, and lost token output, that most enterprises can't afford, especially when dealing with non-batch workloads such as inferencing. So ASUS set out to make components quicker to swap. On the 2U fully liquid-cooled model, ASUS did it with independent, tool-less CPU and GPU sleds, each with its own direct-to-chip cooling. On the 3U hybrid, ASUS says the air-cooled CPU sled cuts maintenance time by up to 50 percent. From loading dock to first token Services aren't just about server maintenance. They're also about decreasing the time to value for AI. Most enterprises won't have in-house rack-scale GPU integration skills, which is why pre-validation and design services are so important.

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. item.title: Black Friday hype stems from a desire 'to be part of a collective event', expert says
item.description: Once a strictly US affair, it's become a truly global phenomenon. From shoppers hunting for bargains in Louisiana, to queues forming outside stores in Venezuela, the Black Friday sales event has become the biggest day of the year for retail foot traffic. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Olaya Moldes Andres, Associate Professor in Marketing and Strategy at Cardiff Business School. She explains that, beyond the sales, the success of Black Friday may also be due to a desire by shoppers to "join the collective action. Whether it is spending money or going to the mall, shoppers feel part of a collective event, so perhaps this is where the whole hype comes from, to feel that we're being part of something, same thing as Christmas or any other social event".
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
item.content:encoded: Once a strictly US affair, it's become a truly global phenomenon. From shoppers hunting for bargains in Louisiana, to queues forming outside stores in Venezuela, the Black Friday sales event has become the biggest day of the year for retail foot traffic. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Olaya Moldes Andres, Associate Professor in Marketing and Strategy at Cardiff Business School. She explains that, beyond the sales, the success of Black Friday may also be due to a desire by shoppers to "join the collective action. Whether it is spending money or going to the mall, shoppers feel part of a collective event, so perhaps this is where the whole hype comes from, to feel that we're being part of something, same thing as Christmas or any other social event".

item.title: RN’s antisemitic past ‘coming back to haunt them’: Will Le Pen ‘distance herself’ from Bardella?
item.description: Could new allegations of antisemitism damage Jordan Bardella’s standing and the far-right National Rally’s electoral prospects? Charli James is pleased to welcome Paul Smith, Associate Professor in French and Francophone Studies at the University of Nottingham. Smith examines the far-right leader’s continued denials and considers whether Marine Le Pen might eventually distance herself from him. In the meantime, Smith suggests that Bardella needs to “make his mind up” about how to respond to these latest troubling allegations published by Le Monde and Mediapart. “It’s very difficult to deny. Le Monde and Mediapart, certainly Le Monde, wouldn’t be publishing these details if they didn’t have some pretty substantial evidence.” Could this prove to be the Achilles’ heel of a far-right party with its sights set on the second round of the presidential election?

item.title: Is Spain's snap election being rigged? Debunking viral claims
item.description: Ahead of Spain's snap election on Sunday, allegations of vote rigging - known in Spanish as "pucherazo" - are spreading widely on social media. From claims that undocumented migrants are being illegally registered to vote, to allegations that postal ballots and vote counts could be manipulated, internet users are accusing Pedro Sánchez's government of attempting to rig the election. But these claims misrepresent how Spain's electoral system works, as Vedika Bahl explains in Truth or Fake.

item.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
item.description: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser. The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Despite Yéremy Pino’s saved penalty in stoppage time and a number of other chances that were squandered, Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory and revive Palace’s Europa League campaign. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none and the Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step. Continue reading...

item.title: Éric Cantona: ‘If I regret something about the kung fu kick, it’s that I would love to kick him in another place’
item.description: Before the release of a new documentary, the unrepentant Manchester United icon reflects on his deep bond with English football and his darker instincts “I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity. I’m far from being the person who always tells the truth. I’m far from being the person who has never been hypocritical. Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.” It’s hard to know what to expect from the only written interview pinned to the release of Cantona: Flower of Evil . Joel Cantona has warned that his famous brother will walk out at any mention of the enduring crisis surrounding Manchester United , whether it’s a question about Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival or the Glazer family’s ruinous ownership of the club. Continue reading...

item.title: Slow internet? The best wifi extenders and mesh systems to boost your home network – tested
item.description: We put 11 range extenders and mesh systems to the test to find the fastest and most reliable for streaming, gaming and working from home • The best office chairs Fast fibre broadband is fantastic – if the wifi signal reaches the part of your home where you need it. Most of us use the router provided by our broadband provider, often tucked away in a hallway or corner of the lounge. Sadly, these often don’t have the range to cover every room in your home, leaving you high and dry when you’re trying to binge-watch TV or get work done in a distant home office. Wifi extenders and mesh systems can help. Extenders plug in to a mains socket between your location and the router, then pass data backwards and forwards to extend your router’s reach. Mesh systems are even smarter, pairing a secondary router with one or two satellite units, which work together to extend the wifi coverage throughout your home. The mesh system can pass your connection from unit to unit to make sure you’re always getting the best possible link from your device to the internet, wherever you are in your home. Continue reading...

item.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
item.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain. "Threat actors define scope and targets for ARTEX, which then uses AI agents to set verifiable goals, define tactical steps for each stage of the operation, use tools to attack targets, create graphs to track discovered systems and res
item.dc:creator: Connor Jones
item.content:encoded: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain. "Threat actors define scope and targets for ARTEX, which then uses AI agents to set verifiable goals, define tactical steps for each stage of the operation, use tools to attack targets, create graphs to track discovered systems and results of actions, and report back to the threat actor." Notably, ARTEX does not offer any new attack techniques. All of the tool's capabilities were previously known to the cybersecurity world, but its value lies in the automation capabilities it offers users, chaining attacks at machine speed. In the UK NCSC's warning about AOFs this week, it said the key strengths of this technology are its speed, its thoroughness in probing target systems for weaknesses, how it learns from failures instantly, and that it is inexpensive to run at scale. AOFs' speed comes at a cost, however. These tools are noisy, the NCSC said, making them easier to detect in network logs and by defensive solutions. Some examples of the attacks in which the tool has been implicated include Storm-0940's hit on ConnectWise, which enabled attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants, various financial institutions in South Korea and India , UK registrar 123 Reg , and the European Commission . ®

item.title: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
item.description: The Forerunner 265S is great for runners with small wrists. | Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks of fitness watches at the time, and the only thing that bugged me was its price. But now that it’s down to $299.99 (a $150 discount off its MSRP) at Amazon and Best Buy for Black Friday, I can easily recommend it. Garmin Forerunner 265S (42mm) Garmin’s Forerunner 265S is identical to the standard 265, only it features a slightly better battery life and a smaller 42mm build for those with more petite wrists. Where to Buy: $449.99 $299.99 at Amazon $449.99 $299.99 at Best Buy The neat thing about Garmins in general is that you really don’t need the latest models to get the most out of the company’s platform. Its watches tend to get firmware updates for several years after launch, which is how long the average Garmin user tends to hold on to theirs. This particular watch is best suited for folks who want something a bit slimmer and smaller, enjoy a pop of color, and want a little extra fitness tracking prowess — but don’t need the whole kit and caboodle that sends the price up by hundreds. There are a few other Garmin models I like that are also on sale during Black Friday. I wish that I had 10 arms to fully vet every single last one, but alas. That said, here are some others that I have tested and recommend: The Garmin Fenix 8 is $749 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , which is a 25 percent discount off its original price. Its higher price comes down to having more features than the Forerunner 265S, so it’s really best for someone who does multiple outdoor sports and could make use of its handy LED flashlight. Garmin’s Venu 4 is $449 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , an 18 percent discount. This is a great option if you’re looking for more of a smartwatch that does fitness than a fitness-y watch that looks like a smartwatch. It’s a fine line, but if you know, you know. Finally, Garmin’s Forerunner 970 is $100 off, costing $649 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI . This is what I’d recommend to marathoners who need something a bit more robust but not as heavy-duty as the flagship Fenix line. I’ve used it to train for a few races and it’s a solid upper-midrange (for Garmin!) option.

item.title: Indie web browser Ladybird enters alpha testing
item.description: The independent Ladybird web browser has reached an important milestone: an alpha test version. What's more, it works well. These may not be the criteria by which some will judge it, though. Earlier this week, the developer behind the Ladybird web browser announced that Ladybird is now in alpha . We've given it a brief test, and it performed very well. It's more stable and works better than its alpha label would suggest. There are downloads available , covering macOS on Apple Silicon, as well as for Linux on x86-64; for the latter, there's a Flatpak package, as well as native Ubuntu and Fedora packages. It's an open source project, so you can download the source code from the GitHub repository and compile it yourself, but in an unusual move, back in June the project announced that the developers would no longer accept public code contributions. We first mentioned Ladybird as part of our early 2022 look at its original parent project – SerenityOS: Remarkable project with its own JS-capable web browser . Both the name and the date are significant: the former is a nod to the Serenity prayer , recited at the end of Alcoholics Anonymous meetings. The date of the article is because it's well before the launch of ChatGPT at the end of 2022 . About a year and a half later, we reported that Serenity OS turns five and emits first offspring, Ladybird . Both the OS and the browser were still hand-coded, but now the browser could be compiled and run on other OSes. That freed it up to call upon external libraries which didn't exist for SerenityOS. Earlier this year, we wrote Ladybird flutters toward Rust with a little help from AI . At one point, developer Andreas Kling used Apple's Swift language, but this year, he changed course and adopted Rust instead, using LLM tools to convert some existing code. Some will dismiss Ladybird because of this, but as our first coverage shows, the browser and its original host OS were established projects before the current wave of AI-assisted development. Kling does use LLMs, but Ladybird is not some sloppy vibe-coded effort. The macOS download is 68.4 MB in size, which in 2026 is remarkably small. The Flatpak is larger – about 111 MB – but it also pulls in some KDE dependencies which increase its size. We tested it on Pop!_OS. It handles sites such as The Register and Hacker News and everything else we tried perfectly, and took just 6 percent of our Dell XPS13's CPU to play full-screen HD video from YouTube smoothly. In our short testing, we saw no crashes, hesitation, or any other problems at all. The developers nevertheless warn that the alpha can crash, some websites will not work, and they make no security guarantees at this stage. The use of LLMs will put some people off. However, this is not the only controversial thing about the project. As we have noted in our previous coverage, Ladybird belongs to the same political wing of the FOSS movement as Omarchy, XLibre, and other right-wing projects. If the LLM use doesn't

item.content:encoded: The independent Ladybird web browser has reached an important milestone: an alpha test version. What's more, it works well. These may not be the criteria by which some will judge it, though. Earlier this week, the developer behind the Ladybird web browser announced that Ladybird is now in alpha . We've given it a brief test, and it performed very well. It's more stable and works better than its alpha label would suggest. There are downloads available , covering macOS on Apple Silicon, as well as for Linux on x86-64; for the latter, there's a Flatpak package, as well as native Ubuntu and Fedora packages. It's an open source project, so you can download the source code from the GitHub repository and compile it yourself, but in an unusual move, back in June the project announced that the developers would no longer accept public code contributions. We first mentioned Ladybird as part of our early 2022 look at its original parent project – SerenityOS: Remarkable project with its own JS-capable web browser . Both the name and the date are significant: the former is a nod to the Serenity prayer , recited at the end of Alcoholics Anonymous meetings. The date of the article is because it's well before the launch of ChatGPT at the end of 2022 . About a year and a half later, we reported that Serenity OS turns five and emits first offspring, Ladybird . Both the OS and the browser were still hand-coded, but now the browser could be compiled and run on other OSes. That freed it up to call upon external libraries which didn't exist for SerenityOS. Earlier this year, we wrote Ladybird flutters toward Rust with a little help from AI . At one point, developer Andreas Kling used Apple's Swift language, but this year, he changed course and adopted Rust instead, using LLM tools to convert some existing code. Some will dismiss Ladybird because of this, but as our first coverage shows, the browser and its original host OS were established projects before the current wave of AI-assisted development. Kling does use LLMs, but Ladybird is not some sloppy vibe-coded effort. The macOS download is 68.4 MB in size, which in 2026 is remarkably small. The Flatpak is larger – about 111 MB – but it also pulls in some KDE dependencies which increase its size. We tested it on Pop!_OS. It handles sites such as The Register and Hacker News and everything else we tried perfectly, and took just 6 percent of our Dell XPS13's CPU to play full-screen HD video from YouTube smoothly. In our short testing, we saw no crashes, hesitation, or any other problems at all. The developers nevertheless warn that the alpha can crash, some websites will not work, and they make no security guarantees at this stage. The use of LLMs will put some people off. However, this is not the only controversial thing about the project. As we have noted in our previous coverage, Ladybird belongs to the same political wing of the FOSS movement as Omarchy, XLibre, and other right-wing projects. If the LLM use doesn't put you off, the political views may. On the other hand, as we've seen from our earlier coverage of Omarchy and XLibre, the same factors also attract others. The modern Web is an entire complex compute platform in its own right, and currently, only three tools support it – and two of those are interrelated. The dominant engines are Google's Blink, used by Chrome and other Chromium browsers; Apple's WebKit, used by Safari; and Mozilla's Gecko, used by Firefox. Blink was forked from WebKit. Some day, when the Servo project matures some more, it may be another. Even so, today, the first preliminary release of Ladybird means that there are now four competitive modern browser engines. That's a significant step. ®

item.title: Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again
item.description: Sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car. In the years since, the Blue Oval has been back to France more than a few times, with varying success. It could never replicate the GT40’s success winning overall, but it celebrated the 40th anniversary with a class win . Now it wants another shot at the really big trophy , and it debuted the car during the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears football game today: meet the GT41. “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” said Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program. “It's the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design, and development teams and an important milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead—the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high, and there are no shortcuts to success. Our focus has been on building the right foundations, bringing together the right people and making sure we learn as much as possible from every stage of development.” The video was directed by Zack Snyder and features Matt Damon’s voice-over. Like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars. LMDh cars start with one of four approved carbon fiber chassis—in this case, Ford is working with Oreca, which has also partnered with Genesis and Acura. Read full article Comments

item.title: 'Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home' at 40: 'Trek' has never been as joyous or fun as in 'the one with the whales'
item.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters. They gave him freedom to tell the story he wanted to tell, and he landed on a not obviously box-office-friendly formula of "No dying, no fighting, no shooting, no photon torpedoes, no phaser blasts, no stereotypical bad guy". It was a massive shift away from Khan and Kruge, the grandstanding villains in movies II and III. Nimoy also wanted the film to have an environmental message and appeal beyond the franchise's traditional fanbase. The film would actually be promoted with minimal "Trek" branding in some territories. (Image credit: Paramount) "I wanted to make it accessible to people who don't go to 'Star Trek' movies," Nimoy said in "The Fifty-Year Mission" by Edward Gross and Mark A. Altman. "I wanted to make it a movie-movie. It starts out like a 'Star Trek' movie and then makes a left turn. It is intentionally very different." "The Voyage Home" effectively closes the trilogy that began four years earlier with "The Wrath of Khan". The story picks up three months after Spock's regenerated body is reunited with his katra (spirit), though nobody ever explains why Kirk and the rest of the crew are all still wearing exactly the same clothes. Following the self-destruction of Enterprise over the Genesis Planet, the gang are heading back to Earth to face the music for a lengthy rap sheet that includes grand theft starship and insubordination on an epic scale. But as they voyage home (geddit?) in a reconditioned Klingon Bird-of-Prey nicknamed the Bounty — complete with a cloaking device that wil
item.dc:creator: Richard Edwards
item.content:encoded:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters. They gave him freedom to tell the story he wanted to tell, and he landed on a not obviously box-office-friendly formula of "No dying, no fighting, no shooting, no photon torpedoes, no phaser blasts, no stereotypical bad guy". It was a massive shift away from Khan and Kruge, the grandstanding villains in movies II and III. Nimoy also wanted the film to have an environmental message and appeal beyond the franchise's traditional fanbase. The film would actually be promoted with minimal "Trek" branding in some territories. (Image credit: Paramount) "I wanted to make it accessible to people who don't go to 'Star Trek' movies," Nimoy said in "The Fifty-Year Mission" by Edward Gross and Mark A. Altman. "I wanted to make it a movie-movie. It starts out like a 'Star Trek' movie and then makes a left turn. It is intentionally very different." "The Voyage Home" effectively closes the trilogy that began four years earlier with "The Wrath of Khan". The story picks up three months after Spock's regenerated body is reunited with his katra (spirit), though nobody ever explains why Kirk and the rest of the crew are all still wearing exactly the same clothes. Following the self-destruction of Enterprise over the Genesis Planet, the gang are heading back to Earth to face the music for a lengthy rap sheet that includes grand theft starship and insubordination on an epic scale. But as they voyage home (geddit?) in a reconditioned Klingon Bird-of-Prey nicknamed the Bounty — complete with a cloaking device that will come in very handy when hiding in Golden Gate Park — they learn that an alien probe of unknown origin (one of the coolest "Star Trek" spaceships ) is tearing Earth apart looking for humpback whales. With the species extinct since the 21st century, the crew travel back in time via one of the most surreal sequences in "Star Trek" history — Morphing CG heads? What the hell was Nimoy thinking? — in the hope of finding the whales that might just be able to ask politely if the probe might leave us alone. (Image credit: Paramount) Screenwriters Steve Meerson and Peter Krikes were assigned to the project early on (working with Nimoy and producer Harve Bennett on the story), and their treatments included a future Earth under threat from a plague and a discarded subplot about Lt. Saavik being pregnant with Spock's child as a result of the pon farr mating ritual. There were also discussions about the Bird-of-Prey decloaking above the Super Bowl, and — most bizarrely of all — a guest-starring role for Eddie Murphy as an astrophysicist who wants to believe in aliens. Murphy was both a Trekkie and one of the biggest stars on the planet at the time but ultimately decided to make notorious stinker "The Golden Child" instead. "In retrospect, I think I might have been better off doing 'Star Trek IV'," he said later. Paramount had also gotten cold feet about putting the star of the highly lucrative "Beverly Hills Cop" in its highest-profile franchise. "Paramount said, 'We're not going to put out [our] two most valuable assets in one movie – so start over, folks!'" said Nicholas Meyer (h/t The Telegraph ), hired to retool the script after Murphy's departure. "That's why I was called at the last minute." (Image credit: Paramount) Meyer was already "Star Trek" royalty, having brought the movie series to life as director and uncredited writer of "The Wrath of Khan". Indeed, he's arguably the reason the "odd numbers bad/even numbers good" theory of "Trek" films persisted for so long, having later gone on to co-write and direct "Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country". He shared scripting duties with Bennett, with the producer writing the 23rd-century-set bookends of the film, and Meyer handling everything in present-day California. Weirdly, Meyer had prior experience bringing a time traveler to contemporary San Francisco in his 1979 HG Wells/Jack the Ripper adventure "Time After Time". With the three previous "Star Trek" movies largely studio-based, "The Voyage Home" marked a rare chance for cast and crew to head out on location. The Monterey Bay Aquarium filled in for the Cetacean Institute (slightly implausible home of humpbacks George and Gracie), while the USS Ranger — moored in San Diego and no stranger to Hollywood after "Top Gun" — guest-starred as a nuclear "wessel". (Image credit: Paramount) Kirk and co. also headed out onto the streets of San Francisco. Nimoy had toyed with giving them '80s-appropriate disguises, but changed his mind when he realized nobody would bat an eyelid at their 23rd-century civilian attire. Aside from some second unit work photographing humpbacks off the coast of Hawaii, the whales themselves were mostly animatronics created by Industrial Light & Magic. "One of the reasons we think that ['The Voyage Home'] really didn't win visual-effects awards is people didn't really understand how good [the whales were]," said executive producer Ralph Winter. "ILM did such a good job on those whales that they went on tour for a year or more around the world to museums because the expertise, the art, and science of what they had done was very good." Meyer, meanwhile, fully embraced the opportunity to write a fish-out-of-water comedy, with this seasoned crew of Starfleet veterans struggling to get their heads around the eccentricities of late 20th-century America. (Image credit: Paramount) Kirk and Spock experiment extensively with "colorful metaphors" — "double dumbass on you!" — while Kirk gets out of paying for dinner by using the convenient excuse that money isn't a thing in the future. Scotty (James Doohan) attempts to talk to a mid-'80s Apple Macintosh via a mouse before he risks screwing with the timeline by 'inventing' transparent aluminum decades early. And in the film's most famous moment, Spock delivers a Vulcan neck pinch to a punk playing his music very loudly on a public bus, winning extensive applause from his fellow passengers in the process. The nuisance rocker was played by Nimoy's assistant, Kirk Thatcher, who co-wrote the "I Hate You" song that plays on that era-authentic ghetto blaster. He later returned to the role in "Star Trek: Picard", though this time he responded more apologetically to Seven of Nine's request to turn it down. Kirk is undoubtedly the center of the movie, pulling the strings and getting his first romantic interest since the Original Series — whale expert Dr Gillian Taylor (Catherine Hicks), who eventually accompanies the Enterprisers back to the fut

item.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
item.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. From L-R: Oluwatomi Otuyemi, Senior PR Account Manager, M.Inc PR; Tamunotonye Waka

From L-R: Oluwatomi Otuyemi, Senior PR Account Manager, M.Inc PR; Tamunotonye Wakama PR and Communications Associate, M.Inc PR and Ayodele Johnson, Content Executive, M.Inc PR at the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Collaboration as a Driver of Economic Opportunity A stronger credit ecosystem requires collaboration among financial institutions, fintech companies, regulators, investors, businesses and development organisations. Each has a role to play in improving access to reliable information, developing relevant financial solutions and building confidence in the credit system. Emphasising the importance of collective action, Dr. Jameelah Sharrieff-Ayedun , Managing Director/CEO, CreditRegistry, noted that “No single institution can reimagine Africa’s credit economy alone,” highlighting the need for lenders, regulators, policymakers and innovators to work together in advancing the sector. Afreximbank’s position as the Expo’s founding sponsor also reflects the connection between financial infrastructure, trade and enterprise development, particularly as African economies seek to expand opportunities for businesses across the continent. The discussions at ACE 2026 underscored that expanding access to credit across Africa will require more than the availability of capital. Reliable credit information, financial literacy, responsible innovation and collaboration among financial institutions, businesses, policymakers and technology providers will all be critical to building a more inclusive and trusted credit ecosystem. Commenting on the significance of the Expo, Mirabel Emma Aleladia , CEO and Lead Strategist, M.Inc PR, said, “ Africa’s evolving credit economy requires sustained engagement among the organisations, institutions and innovators shaping the financial services landscape. The partnership reflects the agency’s commitment to staying informed about developments across business and financial services, and understanding the issues shaping the organisations and audiences it serves. Through platforms such as ACE, M.Inc continues to broaden its industry perspective and remain connected to conversations influencing Africa’s evolving business landscape. item.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
item.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®

item.title: The MacBook Neo is receiving a rare $100 discount for Black Friday
item.description: This thing is poised to eat their lunch. | Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge If you’re looking for a new laptop or a gift for the student in your life, you can save $100 on the MacBook Neo at several retailers, in both storage sizes and all four colors. The 256GB model is currently discounted to $599.99 at Amazon and Costco , while the 512GB model with Touch ID is available for $699.99 via the same retailers ( Amazon / Costco ). None of the retailers currently list an end date for the discount, which is the biggest price drop we’ve seen since Apple raised the laptop’s MSRP by $100 in July in response to the ongoing RAM crisis . MacBook Neo Where to Buy: $799 $699.99 at Amazon (512GB, Touch ID) $699 $599.99 at Amazon (256GB) $699 $599.99 at Costco (256GB) Apple’s budget-friendly MacBook leverages the A18 Pro processor, a chip originally found in the iPhone 16 Pro, to keep costs down. Both the 256GB and 512GB models feature 8GB of memory, and my colleague Antonio G. Di Benedetto was impressed by the vivid 13-inch screen and speakers, the latter of which are better than those in many cheap (and even midrange) Windows laptops. The Neo isn’t super performant, especially in terms of storage speed and total memory, but it’s great for everyday tasks, casual use, and students. Read our Apple MacBook Neo review . Update, November 26th: Adjusted pricing and availability to reflect the additional discount that’s now available at both Amazon and Costco.

item.title: Android app developers will soon have to share their address publicly
item.description: Independent Android app developers are worried about their privacy after Google announced that from next year many of them will be required to share a phone number and address publicly. The policy change is intended to meet European Union regulations under the Digital Services Act , but Google says contact details will be made public worldwide. Developers have until February 1st 2027 to declare whether or not they're a "trader" under UK and European law. Broadly speaking, Google says the definition applies if you earn revenue from your apps, especially if that revenue is regular or at high volume. item.title: Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look
item.description: null Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . Stargazers in the U.S. could get an incredible view of Venus in the predawn hours of the coming week, as the planet climbs into the southeastern sky ahead of the rising sun, with Mercury clinging close to the horizon below. Celestron Nexstar 4SE (Image credit: Celestron) This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you quickly find a steady view of the moon. For a closer look at craters and the terminator, make sure to grab a 9mm or 12mm eyepiece and get stronger magnification. _ Celestron Nexstar 4SE review The bright star Spica will glow less than five degrees away from Venus before dawn on Nov. 27 — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length against the night sky. Spica is a double system of two stars that orbit one another once every four days. Its stars are separated by just approximately 11 million miles (less than 18 million kilometers), making them far too close to split visually with even the most powerful amateur equipment. However, the system still makes for a dazzling target, appearing as a magnificent blue-white star when viewed through the eyepiece of a 4-inch telescope. Venus will appear close to Spica in the southeastern sky. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) Check that the sun is safely below the horizon before turning your telescope on Venus to observe a crescent of light playing across the planet's dense atmosphere. Over the coming weeks and months, Venus will appear increasingly illuminated as it moves farther away from Earth in its orbit, while its apparent size through a telescope will gradually decrease. Want to get a closer look at the planets of the solar system and the stars beyond? Then be sure to check out our roundups of the best telescopes and smart telescopes for observing the night sky. Editor's Note: If you would like to share your astrophotography with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . Stargazers in the U.S. could get an incredible view of Venus in the predawn hours of the coming week, as the planet climbs into the southeastern sky ahead of the rising sun, with Mercury clinging close to the horizon below. Celestron Nexstar 4SE (Image credit: Celestron) This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you quickly find a steady view of the moon. For a closer look at craters and the terminator, make sure to grab a 9mm or 12mm eyepiece and get stronger magnification. _ Celestron Nexstar 4SE review The bright star Spica will glow less than five degrees away from Venus before dawn on Nov. 27 — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length against the night sky. Spica is a double system of two stars that orbit one another once every four days. Its stars are separated by just approximately 11 million miles (less than 18 million kilometers), making them far too close to split visually with even the most powerful amateur equipment. However, the system still makes for a dazzling target, appearing as a magnificent blue-white star when viewed through the eyepiece of a 4-inch telescope. Venus will appear close to Spica in the southeastern sky. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) Check that the sun is safely below the horizon before turning your telescope on Venus to observe a crescent of light playing across the planet's dense atmosphere. Over the coming weeks and months, Venus will appear increasingly illuminated as it moves farther away from Earth in its orbit, while its apparent size through a telescope will gradually decrease. Want to get a closer look at the planets of the solar system and the stars beyond? Then be sure to check out our roundups of the best telescopes and smart telescopes for observing the night sky. Editor's Note: If you would like to share your astrophotography with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
item.description: null On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. (Image credit: collectSPACE/Robert Z. Pearlman ) Why it mattered It may be hard to imagine now, but 15 years ago, the idea of a nuclear-powered rover on Mars was just a concept. When the Curiosity rover launched in 2011, it made that idea a reality the car-size probe (using a plutonium-based radioisotope thermoelectric generator that converts heat from radioactive decay into power) as it headed to the Red Planet. Curiosity was the largest rover ever launched to Mars, following up on the success of the tiny Sojourner rover in 1997 and the larger twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity in 2004. Its sky crane landing system was novel at the time, and fully automated. Once it began its descent in August 2012, NASA could only wait through "seven minutes of terror" to see how it turned out. It ended being a huge success. NASA's Curiosity rover on Mars. (Image credit: NASA) After its smooth landing, Curiosity lived up to its original name: the Mars Science Laboratory. Within weeks, Curiosity fulfilled its primary mission. It found evidence of ancient running water on Mars . It later found organic molecules on Mars as well. Curiosity's primary mission was expected to last just about one Martian year (687 Earth days, or about two Earth years), as the rover explored its Gale Crater landing site. But NASA has extended the mission as the rover continues to operate in good health. In fact, Curiosity has survived long enough to welcome its successor to Mars, the Perseverance rover , which landed in February 2021 on a mission to collect the first samples for later retrieval. Perseverance used the same basic 2-ton design, plutonium power system and sky crane landing system to reach Mars. And today, a ground-based twin of the Curiosity rover, called Promise , is being outfitted for an upcoming mission to the moon. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Detty December Finds Its Crown: Green Indie Artistry 2026
item.description: There is a burst of energy and undeniable excitement that comes over a room when the crowd realises it has power. It happened at BallR Lagos in December 2024, when Green Indie and Hennessy staged the first Indie Star Search finale. The lights dropped, the names were read, and the verdict was something the audience helped write. On Thursday, 17 December 2026, that idea returns bigger. Green Indie Artistry opens at 5:00 PM at Baywater Park, Lekki Phase 1, Lagos. The headliners are 9ice, Fido, and JAYBERRY . Four DJs keep the floor moving between sets. And at the center of the night sits the Indie Star Search, where four finalists perform for the people who will decide who wins. It is less a concert than a referendum with a dance floor. The Premise: Judged by the Room Most competitions are decided behind closed doors. Green Indie flips that. Four finalists perform live, and everyone holding a pass votes on the sets. That audience vote carries its weight in the result. The format has a sharp edge. The people who paid to be in the room become accountable for what happens in it. If the winner is an artist you championed from the front, you helped put them there. The competition has history. The inaugural Indie Star, Young Incredible, won in 2024 with “Lagos to Abuja” and walked off under a storm of confetti. The four finalists for 2026 will be revealed on 6 December. The Headliners The live bill is built on contrast, and that is deliberate. 9ice legendary entertainer, bringing decades of Lagos street credibility into a room full of emerging talent. This is a statement about continuity: the old guard is standing next to the new one. Fido is a performance you don’t want to miss, because you know Joy is coming! For a night that asks the crowd to care who wins, a distinctly local identity is a useful anchor. JAYBERRY brings vibrant energy with heartfelt lyrics. That pairing is harder than it sounds. Energy without substance is cho cho cho; substance without energy is a let down. Access is tiered, and the structure is worth understanding before you buy. All tickets available here . VS: General admission: ₦20,000 (about $16 on an international card). VSOP table, seats 4 XO table, seats 7 The tiers are named for the drinks poured on the night, which suits a Hennessy-backed event. The tables are clearly built for groups who want a base for the night, not just a spot at the rail. Why It Matters Beyond One Night Green Indie describes itself as Africa’s first Direct-to-Fan music platform, selling music directly to listeners rather than routing it through labels. Indie Star Search is the most visible expression of that philosophy: it hands part of the discovery decision to the audience. Whether or not you buy the platform’s broader claims, the event tests an idea. In a creative economy where algorithms often decide what gets heard, a room that votes in real time offers a different signal. It is messier, louder, and more human. It is also a hybrid worth watching: a

Whether or not you buy the platform’s broader claims, the event tests an idea. In a creative economy where algorithms often decide what gets heard, a room that votes in real time offers a different signal. It is messier, louder, and more human. It is also a hybrid worth watching: an independent platform sitting alongside a premium luxury brand and a tiered VIP economy. That is one version of how independent music may get funded and showcased across the continent. Before You Go Buy early. Tables move faster for groups. Watch 6 December.
