item.title: NASA sends planes to monitor US Army's lead detonation. 'Irresponsible' to compare it to Chernobyl, agency chief says
item.description: null NASA has sent three different research aircraft and is using a satellite-based instrument to support the U.S. Army's detonation of degraded explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, the agency announced yesterday (Nov. 24). After a week-long delay caused by public concern over the event creating clouds of lead and toxic materials, today (Nov. 25) around 10 a.m. EDT (1400 GMT) the U.S. Army has planned to execute a controlled detonation of five tons of aging explosives at the ammunition plant. The detonation follows concerns that cooling winter temperatures or attempts to chemically neutralize the materials could lead to an unexpected, uncontrolled explosion. "In challenging circumstances such as this, you want the nation's best on the field. That is precisely why you call on NASA , putting our airborne and space-based sensors and some of the brightest scientific minds in the country to work," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in an online statement . To support this detonation, NASA deployed three research aircraft : a P-3 Orion, a Gulfstream III from NASA's Langley Research Center and a B200 from NASA Ames. The agency is also monitoring the situation using its TEMPO (Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution) instrument which is mounted and orbiting Earth on a commercial satellite. "Working alongside our partners across the federal government, NASA is utilizing its advanced scientific instruments and expertise to collect environmental and atmospheric data to inform the broader federal response," NASA stated . The environmental monitoring using TEMPO is especially important as the materials to be detonated include lead azide and other toxic components that are causing not just environmental worries, but significant local concern over possible health repercussions. This concern is severe enough that, following detonation, officials are encouraging local residents to stay indoors with the doors and windows closed for 24-28 hours. In fact, the CDC has activated an emergency response "to provide accurate public health communication and technical assistance," the CDC stated online . They have also offered additional guidance for locals to try and mitigate as much exposure to toxic materials like lead dust as possible. In the map below, which comes from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers using satellite data, the highlighted area shows where surface deposits of lead is expected to exceed the maximum allowable amounts on surfaces per the Environmental Protection Agency. In this map in the area surrounding the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, the highlighted area shows where surface deposits of lead is expected to exceed the maximum allowable amounts on surfaces per the Environmental Protection Agency. The blue represents lead expected to exceed maximum allowable amounts on windows where green is on floors. In the map below, which comes from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers using satellite data, the highlighted area shows where surface deposits of lead is expected to exceed the maximum allowable amounts on surfaces per the Environmental Protection Agency. In this map in the area surrounding the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, the highlighted area shows where surface deposits of lead is expected to exceed the maximum allowable amounts on surfaces per the Environmental Protection Agency. item.title: Eye of the Sahara
item.description: NASA/Luke Delaney The Richat Structure, also known as the “Eye of the Sahara,” is seen from the International Space Station as it orbited above on Nov. 14, 2026. It is an eroded geological dome about 100 million years old created by igneous activity and uplift in the nation of Mauritania. In this type of geologic structure, rocks exposed in the center of the “bullseye” are older than rocks forming the outer rings. This structure measures 45 kilometers (28 miles) across and is made up of igneous and sedimentary rocks. Image credit: NASA/Luke Delaney

item.title: “Senegal and Morocco Are Brotherly Nations”: Sadio Mané Speaks After CAS Restores AFCON Title
item.description: Senegal captain Sadio Mané and his teammates gather around the Africa Cup of Nations trophy on the pitch in Rabat. Yesterday, after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) overturned a previous Confederation of African Football (CAF) decision on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, and reinstated Senegal as the champions of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON), the 34-year-old Senegal captain Sadio Mané took to Instagram to celebrate the news. Alongside photos of himself and his teammates lifting the trophy, Mané thanked Senegalese supporters at home and in the diaspora, praised his squad for their sacrifices, and extended a thoughtful message of respect to Morocco. If you’re just catching up on how the Teranga Lions arrived at this moment, the journey since the final in Rabat on 18 January 2026 has been anything but ordinary. During a tense stoppage-time spell—after Senegal had a goal disallowed and hosts Morocco were awarded a late penalty—Senegal’s coach Pape Thiaw pulled his players off the pitch, delaying the match for 14 minutes. It was Mané—widely celebrated as one of Africa’s finest footballers of his generation after trophy-laden spells with Liverpool and Bayern Munich before joining Al-Nassr—who stepped in to persuade his teammates to return and finish the game. Senegal went on to win 1–0 in extra time thanks to a Pape Gueye goal. Senegal captain Sadio Mané raises the AFCON trophy on the podium alongside Édouard Mendy and the Teranga Lions squad. In March, however, CAF’s Appeal Board overturned that result and awarded Morocco a 3–0 forfeit victory over the temporary walk-off. The Senegalese Football Federation appealed to CAS in Lausanne, and on Tuesday,sport’s highest court ruled unanimously in Senegal’s favour—confirming that Congolese referee Jean-Jacques Ndala acted within his authority when resuming the match, and restoring Senegal’s second AFCON title. Read Mané’s full statement below: The decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport reinstating Senegal as champions of Africa fills us with joy. First, I want to thank the entire Senegalese people, both at home and in the diaspora. You supported us from the first match right through to this decision. Your trust gave us strength during the most difficult moments. Thank you to my teammates. I know the effort and sacrifices each of you made to win this second star. I am proud to have experienced this journey alongside you. My thanks also go to the entire technical staff and everyone who supported the Lions. I would also like to send a message of respect and encouragement to the Moroccan people and the Moroccan players. They had a great campaign and should be proud of what they achieved. I wish them all the best going forward. Senegal and Morocco are two brotherly nations. May the passion for football continue to bring us closer together. Congratulations to all Senegalese people. This victory belongs to you too. While the Royal Moroccan Football Federation has indicated it plans to challenge

Read Mané’s full statement below: The decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport reinstating Senegal as champions of Africa fills us with joy. First, I want to thank the entire Senegalese people, both at home and in the diaspora. You supported us from the first match right through to this decision. Your trust gave us strength during the most difficult moments. Thank you to my teammates. I know the effort and sacrifices each of you made to win this second star. I am proud to have experienced this journey alongside you. My thanks also go to the entire technical staff and everyone who supported the Lions. I would also like to send a message of respect and encouragement to the Moroccan people and the Moroccan players. They had a great campaign and should be proud of what they achieved. I wish them all the best going forward. Senegal and Morocco are two brotherly nations. May the passion for football continue to bring us closer together. Congratulations to all Senegalese people. This victory belongs to you too. While the Royal Moroccan Football Federation has indicated it plans to challenge the decision further, CAF has confirmed it respects the CAS ruling. Senegal captain Sadio Mané raises the Africa Cup of Nations trophy while lifted by teammates after the final in Rabat. *** Photo Credit: Sadio Mané/Instagram The post “Senegal and Morocco Are Brotherly Nations”: Sadio Mané Speaks After CAS Restores AFCON Title appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Lead azide detonation sends clouds over Iowa as questions of health risks swirl
item.description: In a powerful explosion that launched gray-white clouds over southeastern Iowa, the Army detonated 68 barrels containing 9,700 pounds (4.4 tons) of degraded lead azide on Wednesday at about 9 am CT, preventing a spontaneous unmitigated explosion of the crystallized, highly unstable compound. The detonation occurred at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa, a town of fewer than 400 people. Residents within a 5-mile area of the facility were advised to evacuate, while people farther out were told to shelter in place, close windows and doors tightly, turn off fans, and set indoor air systems to recirculate. Local Iowa outlet KWQC caught the plume from the two earth-covered containers, which were detonated simultaneously. A KWQZ journalist, at a reportedly safe distance from the blast, said on the live broadcast that he could see and then feel the shockwave roll through the crop field in which he was standing. He put a mask on for the rest of the broadcast. Read full article Comments

item.title: NASA's nuclear-powered Mars delivery service takes shape
item.description: NASA has settled key design choices for its planned nuclear-fission-powered spacecraft, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, following a mission review in October. Targeting launch in late 2028, SR-1 would be the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit. It is designed to demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion and deliver a capsule carrying three helicopters to Mars. There have been some changes since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman showed off the concept [PDF] at the agency's Ignition event in March. Improved shielding and spacecraft design will allow a shorter boom between the reactor and the spacecraft's main body, protecting its electronics and the SkyFall payload. The shorter boom will, according to NASA, "reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design." The revised design also includes larger X-band antenna dishes to transmit data to Earth. Decisions are still pending on how many radiator panels the vehicle needs, the output power levels of the nuclear power module, and how long the reactor will operate. Currently, the mission calls for the spacecraft to start its reactor once it has left Earth orbit and gradually ramp up power. After a period during which performance data will be sent back to Earth, the reactor will be shut down until after the SkyFall capsule, containing a trio of Mars Ingenuity-class helicopters, is delivered to Martian orbit. Solar arrays will power the spacecraft during its cruise to Mars. The fission reactor will then be reactivated to let engineers collect more data on its performance in deep space. NASA also awarded a $39.3 million contract to Johns Hopkins University's Applied Physics Laboratory to develop the heat rejection system for the nuclear power module. "Further maturation of the spacecraft plans will focus on reducing risk, simplifying the design, and staying on schedule," the agency said. The latter part regarding the schedule is certainly a challenge . Meeting the late-2028 launch target leaves roughly two years to finish designing, building, and testing the spacecraft. ESA is also targeting late 2028 for its long-delayed Rosalind Franklin rover. Missing the intended Mars departure opportunity could push SR-1 into a later launch window, although NASA has not specified a fallback schedule. ®

item.title: New York bans AI toys, including those using internet to talk to children
item.description: The state attorney general says she would ‘not hesitate to enforce’ the five-year ban signed by Governor Kathy Hochul The New York governor, Kathy Hochul , signed legislation on Wednesday that places a five-year ban on the manufacture and sale of toys powered by AI chatbots, including talking stuffed animals, dolls and robots that use the internet to hold conversations with children. The recently re-elected governor, who has also placed a one-year moratorium AI datacenter construction in the state , said that parents shopping for children’s toys “should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk”. Continue reading...

item.title: Konga Yakata: Bigger Black Friday Deals, Free Delivery & a Chance to Win an SUV
item.description: With Black Friday arriving on Friday, November 27, Konga is urging shoppers to take advantage of the remaining days of its annual Yakata shopping festival, which ends on November 30. The e-commerce giant is promising exciting deals, significant price reductions, a chance to win a brand-new SUV and free delivery for eligible shoppers in Lagos. Konga Yakata has continued to attract shoppers with discounts across technology, electronics, home appliances, personal care and everyday essentials. However, Black Friday is expected to be one of the biggest highlights of this year’s campaign, with customers encouraged to shop early and take advantage of the offers while stocks last. Speaking on the Black Friday campaign, Irfan Vayani, Senior Vice President at Konga Group, said: “Konga Yakata Black Friday is more than just a sales event; it is our way of giving back to Nigerians who have made Konga their trusted shopping partner. This year, we are going bigger and better. From unbeatable discounts across all categories to the chance to win a brand-new SUV simply by shopping on the Konga app, our goal is to make this Yakata season one of joy, value and transformation. We want to touch lives in real, tangible ways.” Adding more value to the shopping experience, Konga has introduced free delivery for the remainder of Yakata. The offer is available exclusively to shoppers in Lagos who purchase products carrying the KongaNow tag. Eligible customers can therefore enjoy discounted prices while saving on delivery costs, making their Black Friday shopping even more rewarding. Shoppers also stand a chance to win a brand-new SUV through Konga’s Win A Car campaign. Customers who make purchases through the Konga app automatically qualify for the random draw, regardless of the amount spent. There is no minimum purchase requirement, giving every eligible app shopper an opportunity to participate. The festival also features attractive offers from leading brands, including Samsung, LG, Anker, Midea, Starlink, ASUS, Zinox, Guinness and others. Their participation has expanded the range of deals available, giving customers more opportunities to shop across different product categories. Beyond the website and app, Konga has extended the Yakata experience to Instagram and Facebook through interactive live shopping shows. These sessions allow shoppers to discover featured products, enjoy special live deals and engage with the campaign in real time. With the November 30 deadline fast approaching, shoppers have just a few days left to take advantage of the offers. Although some customers have called for an extension, no extension has been announced. The remaining days present an opportunity to secure great deals, enjoy free delivery on eligible Lagos orders and participate in the Win A Car campaign. This Black Friday, shoppers can make their purchases count by visiting the Konga website or app and taking advantage of Yakata before the festival closes on November 30. With the sale

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Early in the second half of Tuesday night’s National League South match between Torquay United and Chesham, play was briefly suspended due to an ear-splitting din emitted over the Plainmoor public address system. “The game has stopped because the Torquay Tannoy system is making a loud noise that won’t stop,” posted Chesham on their Social Media Disgrace account. “I’m not kidding.” A sort of aural cross between an ocean liner’s foghorn and a party conference speech delivered by a senior member of the Reform party, it eventually stopped and play resumed with Torquay running out 2-1 winners. In this constantly changing world of global disruptions, uncertainties and risks, with social, political and economic disaffection seemingly on the rise everywhere, it’s genuinely heartening to know that some things never change . ‘Plus ça change, plus c’est la même chose’, as the late, great French writer Jean-Baptiste Alphonse Karr famously said, something that I’m sure Big Dunc is well aware of” – Noble Francis. May I be the 1,092nd correspondent to demand a review of the Letter o’ the Day award for Monday – and it be awarded to Declan Hackett for his letter foretelling the rescinding of the red card given to Lenny Yoro on Sunday? Given the precedent of awarding/revoking/re-awarding of the Afcon 2025 edition this would be entirely justified” – Peter Martin. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: The unexpected joy hiding in Grand Theft Auto VI’s chaos? A little routine
item.description: Rockstar’s latest blockbuster makes the everyday business of shopping, working out and taking care of a pet snake as compelling as its shootouts and car chases I knew I’d need many skills during the opening hours of Grand Theft Auto VI, but effective time management was not one of them. From playing the previous five titles in the series (and their many spin-offs), I understood I’d have to master Rockstar’s idiosyncratic approach to car handling. True enough, the vehicles do drive like airbeds tied on top of supermarket trolleys. I also knew I’d need to get to grips with the somewhat tricky aiming and shooting if I was to commit any sort of respectable crime spree. But for the first few hours of playing this staggeringly large and bewildering game, what concerned me most was lead character Jason’s personal routine. Each day, he needs to get up, choose an outfit, complete a workout, feed his pet snake Dolores, and perhaps do some DIY, so that when his girlfriend Lucia gets out of jail she’ll fall for him again – rather than fall through his apartment’s rotten staircase. Meanwhile, his drug-smuggling boss phones every five minutes with new parcels for Jason to pick up or drop off, and his pals Cal and Donnie get into all sorts of cocaine-related hijinks they expect Jason to extricate them from. There are also predatory neighbours to do favours for, and groceries to buy. I’ve seen so many people on social media posting about how they took several days off work to play this game, only to find themselves busier and more productive than ever. On his radio show last week, James O’Brien derided himself for completing, in Jason’s apartment, a simple DIY task that he’s put off for months in his own home. I know where he’s coming from. Continue reading...

item.title: Satellites watch volcanic eruptions add new beaches on Iwo Jima | Space photo of the day for Nov. 25, 2026
item.description: null Iwo Jima on Oct. 26, 2026 on the left and the same location on Nov. 11, 2026 shows the impact of a volcanic eruption. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey ) Iwo Jima looks remarkably different from space after a volcanic eruption created new land extending the Japanese island's beaches. What is it? On Oct. 27, Japan's Meteorological Agency detected an underwater volcanic eruption off the shores of Iwo Jima. Soon after this initial detection of the "submarine" volcano, satellites orbiting our planet started taking a look, observing to see what havoc this eruption might wreak. When you compare the satellite images above captured by the Landsat 9 satellite's Operational Land Imager (OLI), you can see the stark differences between the island on October 26 before the eruption and weeks later on November 11. The island was also observed by NASA's NISAR spacecraft as well as the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors. Together, this imagery gave researchers a more complete picture of how the eruption continued and the effects it left behind. And amazingly, with satellite imagery experts have been able to show that the eruption has actually added more land to the island's beaches. Why is it incredible? On Nov. 16, Japan's Coast Guard confirmed in a statement that about 125 acres (50 hectares) of new land is now connected to the island's southeast beach following the recent volcanic eruption. This is not the first time that a volcano has created new land. Lava and ash from a volcanic eruption can solidify and accumulate, adding land material around the volcano or to a nearby coast if it is located offshore or underwater, as we saw in this case. But these new landforms aren't always permanent fixtures. This new addition to the island's beach could easily and quickly be washed away by the waves, which happened on Iwo Jima just a few years ago in 2023 . And experts expect the same thing to happen with this new land. "I imagine we'll see this new land wash away within a few months," Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center who has previously studied landforms created by volcanic eruptions, said in a statement . "But we'll have to wait and see."

Credits: NASA, ESA, and S. Terry (University of Maryland); Image Processing: G. Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) An expanse of stars gleams in a rainbow of colors in these NASA Hubble Space Telescope images of the Milky Way. The images focus on an area of sky toward the galactic bulge, a densely packed, spherical region of stars that surrounds the center of a galaxy’s disk. These Hubble observations are part of a survey that will help researchers better interpret upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope observations as they seek to characterize the stars and search for exoplanets in this busy region of our galaxy. Astronomers study the Milky Way’s galactic bulge because it holds nearly a quarter of the galaxy’s stellar mass, and its proximity allows them to examine the region in greater detail. Although we can see the glow from these crowded spheres of stars in other galaxies, they are too jam-packed and far away to resolve individual stars. By studying the Milky Way’s galactic bulge, researchers hope to find new planets and better understand how galaxies form, evolve, and interact over billions of years. Because researchers wish to compare Hubble’s observations to future Roman observations, Hubble looked at the region in wavelengths that overlap with Roman’s areas of sensitivity, the red end of the visible spectrum and near-infrared wavelengths. Hubble’s high resolution allows its instruments to collect data on the brightness, ages, composition, and motion of stars over time. With this knowledge, astronomers can search for potential exoplanets, determine the location of black holes or dark matter, and better understand our galaxy’s environment and evolution. A crowded starfield appears interrupted by a dark patch of sky in this NASA Hubble Space Telescope image. A closer look at this darker region reveals many faint stars filling the area. The image is part of a Hubble survey of the galactic bulge. It will help researchers interpret future Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope data of the same region. NASA, ESA, and S. Terry (University of Maryland); Image Processing: G. Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) A key component of Roman’s future observations is the search for exoplanets by capturing microlensing events , a type of gravitational lensing that occurs when light from a more distant object is magnified and distorted by the mass of a closer object along the line of sight. The way light from the distant star is distorted and magnified can reveal clues to the nature of the foreground star and any planets it may have. Hubble’s observations will help characterize stars in the region before they undergo a lensing event. Months or years in the future, when Roman captures a microlensing event, researchers can compare Hubble data to Roman data of the event, making it easer to interpret. These microlensing events are on a much smaller scale, that of stars and planets, than larger gravitational lenses that occur around galaxies and galaxy clusters . NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope’s high resolution reveals individual stars in an area near our galaxy’s center swarming with stars. The image is part of a Hubble survey of the galactic bulge that will help researchers interpret future Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope data of the same region. NASA, ESA, and S. Terry (University of Maryland); Image Processing: G. Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) Over Hubble’s lifetime, it has observed our galaxy’s central bulge many times. These legacy surveys include the WFC3 Galactic Bulge Treasury Program that used Hubble’s Wide Field Camera 3 to study the brightness, precise positions, and motions of stars in this congested part of our galaxy. It also includes the Sagittarius Window Eclipsing Extrasolar Planet Search (SWEEPS) that used Hubble’s Advanced Camera for Surveys to look at 180,000 stars in the bulge of our galaxy. These new observations come from an observing program (# 17776 : S. Terry) designed to aid Roman in its search for exoplanets, black holes, neutron stars, and more. The data also adds to Hubble’s continuing legacy of high-precision observations of stars in the galactic bulge. Hubble Science Highlights Hubble’s most notable scientific discoveries reflect the broad range of research and the breakthroughs it has achieved. Hubble vs. Roman NASA’s Hubble and Roman space telescopes will work together to broaden our perspective of the universe. Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will settle essential questions in the areas of dark energy, exoplanets, and astrophysics.

item.title: Infinix Nigeria Unveils Black Friday Grand Finale Featuring Stan Nze and Smart 20 Series Giveaway
item.description: Infinix Nigeria is set to bring its 2026 Black Friday campaign to a close with a grand finale on Friday, November 27, featuring an exclusive Instagram Live session with Nollywood actor Stan Nze and an opportunity for selected participants to win the Infinix SMART 20 device. The session will mark the highlight of the campaign’s final day, giving customers another opportunity to engage with the brand while enjoying the last round of Black Friday offers. As part of the November 27 Black Friday celebrations, Infinix will host Stan Nze on its official Instagram Live, where participants can interact with the actor and take part in activities during the broadcast. Selected participants will stand a chance to win exciting gifts by participating in the live sessions across Infinix’s Instagram, Facebook and TikTok accounts. Viewers will also receive exclusive discount codes worth ₦10,000 to shop for the SMART 20 Series on the 3C HUB e-commerce platform. The SMART 20 is designed to support everyday use with a combination of performance, display quality and practical features. It comes with a 6.78-inch display with a refresh rate of up to 120Hz for smoother scrolling and viewing, a 5,200mAh battery designed to keep users connected for longer, and a MediaTek Helio G81 Ultimate processor to support everyday tasks and entertainment. Its 7.7mm slim profile, IP64 dust and splash resistance, and UltraLink technology, which enables offline communication with compatible devices over distances of up to 1km, add to its appeal. Together, these features make the device a practical option for users looking for a smartphone that balances functionality, durability and design. With the grand finale approaching, customers have one final opportunity to take part in the campaign’s activities. Follow Infinix Nigeria on Instagram and join the live session with Stan Nze on Friday, November 27. Participants should remain engaged throughout the broadcast and follow the instructions shared during the session for a chance to be selected as winners. Follow Infinix Nigeria on Instagram for updates on the grand finale and details of the live session. item.title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
item.description: While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment Off! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull, Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity ( though his suspension was overturned on appeal) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford. This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24. Continue reading...

item.title: Microsoft fixes Office dialog that had nothing to say and wouldn't go away
item.description: Microsoft has released a fix for a baffling bug that threw a blank window over Office applications and brought work to a standstill. The problem appeared when users launched an affected Office app, which could display an empty dialog box with no text and no buttons. Because the dialog offered no way to close it, some users were locked out of their work entirely, unable to continue until the issue was resolved. The good news is that there's an update to fix the problem – version 2611, build 16.0.20625.20142. The bad news is that you might not be able to launch the applications to perform the update because of that blank dialog window. Microsoft instructs affected users to save their work, close all Office applications, and open Command Prompt as administrator. They can then force the update with: "%programfiles%\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\ClickToRun\officec2rclient.exe" /update user updatetoversion=16.0.20625.20142 The glitch affects a swathe of Microsoft 365 products – Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access, and OneNote. Users reported the problem on Microsoft's forums , where volunteer moderator Stefan Blom noted that "this seems to be a common error at the moment" and suggested users try an Office repair or the more thorough Online Repair. Online Repair reinstalls Office, however, some users reported activation and sign-in problems alongside the blank windows, which may hint at the cause. Microsoft has yet to elucidate. Other users found that rolling back Office resolved the issue, while several reported that signing in with another application, such as Edge, fixed things. For administrators preparing fleets of devices, a dialog that blocks first use creates another deployment headache. One user with E3 licensing reported: "We can't just hand off a staged machine without getting call[s] that our new users can't get Office to work because of the blank licensing window." Microsoft has shared a fix for the problem, but has not stated which versions of its productivity applications were affected, nor has it explained what went wrong. The fix is welcome. An explanation of how Office ended up blocking users with a window containing nothing at all would be welcome too. ®

item.title: Meet Jessi Kalambayi: Miss Universe DRC Who Made the Top 12 at Miss Universe 2026
item.description: Miss Universe Congo Jessi Kalambayi wearing her national crown and sash in a gold beaded evening gown. Photo Credit: Jessi Kalambayi/Instagram The 75th Miss Universe competition has come to a close in San Juan, Puerto Rico, and Jessi Kalambayi gave the Democratic Republic of the Congo a night to remember. Out of 116 contestants from around the world—and 17 representing Africa —the 28-year-old beauty queen became the sole African delegate to reach the Top 12 at Tuesday night’s live finale, representing her country as Miss Universe Congo at the Coliseo de Puerto Rico José Miguel Agrelot. That is a major result for the Central African nation, and there is quite a story behind the woman who made it happen. Born Jessi Longwe Kalambayi in Kinshasa and raised between South Africa and the United States, Jessi arrived at Miss Universe with an impressive background beyond pageantry. She holds a bachelor’s degree in Psychology with a minor in Africana Studies from Metropolitan State University of Denver, as well as a master’s degree in International Studies, specialising in Migration, from the University of Denver. Her professional experience includes working as a programme manager supporting refugee resettlement. She has also used her platform to speak about embracing natural African hair textures, from afros to braids, as part of celebrating Congolese identity. Miss Universe Congo Jessi Kalambayi honours the Democratic Republic of the Congo national football team for her Miss Universe 2026 national costume. Photo Credit: Jessi Kalambayi/Instagram And this was hardly her first time navigating a major pageant stage. Before winning the Miss Universe DRC 2026 crown in July, succeeding Dorcas Dienda, Jessi had already made her mark in the United States. In 2024, she won Miss Colorado USA and went on to place in the Top 10 at Miss USA. That experience came in handy in San Juan, where she moved through the preliminary rounds and closed-door interviews with the nine-member selection committee to secure a place in the initial Top 30. Miss Universe Congo Jessi Kalambayi on stage during the swimsuit round of the Miss Universe 2026 Preliminary Competition. Photo Credit: Jessi Kalambayi/Instagram Finale night brought another big moment. Alongside fellow African Top 30 semifinalists from Ethiopia, Guinea, Tanzania and Uganda, Jessi made it through the swimsuit round and advanced into the Top 12 alongside contestants from Puerto Rico, Venezuela, the Philippines, the United States and France—standing as Africa’s lone representative in that round. Miss Universe Congo Jessi Kalambayi during the Top 12 evening gown round at the 75th Miss Universe finale in San Juan, Puerto Rico. Photo Credit: Jessi Kalambayi/Instagram Her Miss Universe journey came to an end just before the announcement of the Top 5, while Puerto Rico’s Jennifer Barreto went on to claim the crown. Still, Jessi’s run marked an important showing for the Democratic Republic of the Congo and closed out the 75th

item.title: Amazon to start selling cars in the UK next year
item.description: US retail giant links up with Hyundai in attempt to crack £200bn British market Amazon is planning to sell cars in the UK from early next year, in a move that threatens to disrupt the vehicle retail market. The Amazon Autos service will be launched in “early 2027”, starting with cars from the Korean manufacturer Hyundai. It will be the first time the US tech company has sold cars outside its home country. Continue reading...

item.title: A familiar Iranian hacking group has found a new way to cause chaos
item.description: One night in October, hackers staged one of the most unusual cyber attacks in history : cranking up the temperature in refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France and destroying millions of euros of food. Hackers have targeted commercial fridges and freezers before, but never at this scale and never in the heart of Europe. The brazen attack left cyber professionals unsure as to who might have executed such a madcap operation. But French intelligence agencies found traces of Farsi and other clues in the digital trail pointing to an elite hacking unit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The unit allegedly behind the hack, Shahid Kaveh, was already well known to Western intelligence agencies. Named after Mahmoud Kaveh, an Iranian commander who died during the 1980s Iran-Iraq war, it is one of several hacking units overseen by the Revolutionary Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command. Read full article Comments

item.title: JetBrains finds agents may cheat with open source
item.description: JetBrains has revamped a benchmark for evaluating large language models after suspecting too many agents gamed their tasks the first time round. The company labelled this agentic practice "reward hacking" in a post summarizing the results of its revised evaluation. Like its predecessor , Kotlin Benchmark 2.0 is a collection of tasks that evaluates how well AI coding agents work with the Kotlin programming language , in order to help Kotlin programmers decide which agent-model configurations to use. The tasks include fixing tricky problems in Kotlin code across different domains, and making corrections to multiple files. Dirty data The revised benchmar k now includes 30 Kotlin multi-file code problems that have not been exposed to the public in any way before. The revised test all but guarantees that the agents have not encountered this set of problems, or potential solutions, before. Another 70 tasks are based on code that resides in public repositories. The test also blocked all network access for the open source tasks, except for what was needed to communicate with the model itself. This minimized the possibility that the agent could look for an existing answer already posted, perhaps through a patch or pull request. A 30-minute limit was set for each task. Overall, the agents were significantly less accurate when solving problems on codebases they had never encountered. Top resolution rates dropped rather suspiciously from 86.2 percent on tasks based on open source repositories to 60 percent on those based on closed source repositories. Although the agents lacked network access, JetBrains boffins theorized that they might have benefited from encountering and internalizing these open source repositories during training. Only the private repositories were completely new to them. Also curious was how a different set of models excelled at the closed source problems, compared to those models that usually did better on the open source tasks. Leaderboard Shakeup When restricted to closed source tasks, two dark horse models rose to the top: Gemini 3.8 Flash, via Antigravity CLI, topped the list with a 60 percent success rate, closely followed by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (running on OpenCode) at 58.9 percent. Of the two, the open weight DeepSeek was far cheaper (at $0.08 per task) than the closed weight Gemini ($1.74 per task), however. In contrast, Opus 5.5 completed only 53.3 percent of the tasks at $1.21 per task, and Fable 5.1 completed only 44.4 percent of the tasks, at a luxurious $3.27 per task. Claude Code harnessed both of these models. Claude’s lackluster completion rates on closed source tasks are somewhat sus given how both of these Anthropic models scored significantly higher on tasks using open source materials. In fact Claude ran the table when it came to open source: Fable 5.1 topped the charts with 86.2 percent accuracy, closely followed by Opus 5.5 at 84.8 percent accuracy. item.dc:creator: Joab Jackson
item.content:encoded: JetBrains has revamped a benchmark for evaluating large language models after suspecting too many agents gamed their tasks the first time round. The company labelled this agentic practice "reward hacking" in a post summarizing the results of its revised evaluation. Like its predecessor , Kotlin Benchmark 2.0 is a collection of tasks that evaluates how well AI coding agents work with the Kotlin programming language , in order to help Kotlin programmers decide which agent-model configurations to use. The tasks include fixing tricky problems in Kotlin code across different domains, and making corrections to multiple files. Dirty data The revised benchmar k now includes 30 Kotlin multi-file code problems that have not been exposed to the public in any way before. The revised test all but guarantees that the agents have not encountered this set of problems, or potential solutions, before. Another 70 tasks are based on code that resides in public repositories. The test also blocked all network access for the open source tasks, except for what was needed to communicate with the model itself. This minimized the possibility that the agent could look for an existing answer already posted, perhaps through a patch or pull request. A 30-minute limit was set for each task. Overall, the agents were significantly less accurate when solving problems on codebases they had never encountered. Top resolution rates dropped rather suspiciously from 86.2 percent on tasks based on open source repositories to 60 percent on those based on closed source repositories. Although the agents lacked network access, JetBrains boffins theorized that they might have benefited from encountering and internalizing these open source repositories during training. Only the private repositories were completely new to them. Also curious was how a different set of models excelled at the closed source problems, compared to those models that usually did better on the open source tasks. Leaderboard Shakeup When restricted to closed source tasks, two dark horse models rose to the top: Gemini 3.8 Flash, via Antigravity CLI, topped the list with a 60 percent success rate, closely followed by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (running on OpenCode) at 58.9 percent. Of the two, the open weight DeepSeek was far cheaper (at $0.08 per task) than the closed weight Gemini ($1.74 per task), however. In contrast, Opus 5.5 completed only 53.3 percent of the tasks at $1.21 per task, and Fable 5.1 completed only 44.4 percent of the tasks, at a luxurious $3.27 per task. Claude Code harnessed both of these models. Claude’s lackluster completion rates on closed source tasks are somewhat sus given how both of these Anthropic models scored significantly higher on tasks using open source materials. In fact Claude ran the table when it came to open source: Fable 5.1 topped the charts with 86.2 percent accuracy, closely followed by Opus 5.5 at 84.8 percent accuracy. (Kotlin users will pay dearly for the extra sliver of Anthropic accuracy: The average cost of Fable completing a Kotlin cleanup task runs $2.38, while Opus could do the job for $0.68.) Gaming the boss One possible interpretation of these disparate numbers is that models are drawing from their own knowledge bases instead of reasoning from scratch. Whether this is cheating or the models simply working as intended might be more a matter of philosophical debate. Mark Hinkle, founder of the AIE Network consultancy, suspects the issue of integrity may go deeper. "Private code doesn't stop reward hacking, it changes the shortcut," he wrote to The Register on LinkedIn. "On public code the agent goes and finds the answer somebody has already published. On private code there's no answer to find, so it satisfies whatever is checking it. I treat these things like entry-level employees, and a sharp new hire figures out fast what the boss actually looks at." JetBrains did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but concluded in its post that more investigation is needed. It promises that its people will pore over the open source results to see if any have been contaminated by the LLMs' own memory. It also plans to run its own static analysis tool, Qodana , against the results to check for errors. Sireesha Pulipati , a staff data engineer and AI observer, suggested, also by LinkedIn, that JetBrains may have needed more specificity in its agent instructions. "Out of the box [an agent] tends to reach for generic patterns. But when we give it instructions and skills that tell it where to look for our patterns and context, it follows them. A well-controlled harness, with those standards built in, is what makes the agent useful," Pulipati wrote. So good on JetBrains for providing Kotlin users some information about working with AI, but, as always, AI benchmarks should be approached with extreme side-eye. ®

item.title: Pepsi Agba Baller Promo: Everything You Need to Know About Winning Big with ₦800 Million Cash Up for Grabs
item.description: ₦800 million in cash prizes. A winner every minute. Four millionaires every day and one ₦10 million weekly jackpot winner every Sunday, announced live by 8 pm on Pepsi ‘s Instagram page, @pepsi_naija. Seven-Up Bottling Company’s (SBC) Pepsi Agba Baller Promo is giving consumers across selected regions the opportunity to win cash rewards simply by purchasing participating products and entering their unique codes. Running from November 2, 2026, to January 3, 2027, the promotion is open to eligible consumers in nine participating regions: Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Kwara, Osun, Ekiti, Kogi, Niger and Ondo. If you have been wondering how to participate, which products qualify or what happens when you win, here’s everything you need to know about the Pepsi Agba Baller Promo. What Is the Pepsi Agba Baller Promo? The Pepsi Agba Baller Promo is a consumer rewards initiative by Seven-Up Bottling Company, featuring Pepsi and other participating Seven-Up Bottling Company products with a yellow cover. item.title: Novel Experiments Expand the Hunt for ‘Ultralight’ Dark Matter
item.description: For the most part, we are blind to the universe. Almost a century ago — in 1933, to be exact — Fritz Zwicky’s studies of distant galaxies led him to suggest that “dark matter is present in very much greater density than luminous matter.” Observations by the astronomer Vera Rubin would later substantiate the case for the intangible, leading her to write in 1980 that “the conclusion is inescapable… Source

item.title: Watch live: Europe unveils 1st close-up views of asteroid Dimorphos after NASA's DART impact
item.description: null After a two-year journey, the Hera spacecraft is arriving at the Didymos double asteroid system, and its first images are being released to the public today (Nov. 25). The European Space Agency's (ESA's ) Hera probe launched atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 7, 2024 . Its destination is the Didymos-Dimorphos asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos , a " rubble pile" asteroid , and its smaller moonlet Dimorphos. NASA slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in 2022 in the historic DART test , which confirmed that such an impact can alter the trajectory of an asteroid. Hera arrives at Didymos today, and ESA is sharing the first close-up images from the mission in a free online livestream. ESA's livestream starts at 1:45 p.m. ET (1845 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 25) . Watch it live here, courtesy of the European Space Agency. At Dimorphos, Hera will inspect the wreckage caused by DART (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), humanity's first test of planetary defense. The test was designed to see if the orbit of a threatening asteroid could be altered, taking it off a potential crash course with Earth. A simulation of the impact of DART on Didymos (Image credit: S.D. Raducan) The DART mission succeeded, shortening Dimorphos' orbit by just over 30 minutes, showing that kinetic impacts can indeed alter the trajectories of asteroids. Hera will now show up to the crash scene and study the impact crater left by DART and inspect any changes the collision caused. Scientists are thrilled by the prospects. A series of images captured by the DART spacecraft as it sped to impact the asteroid Dimorphos on Sept. 26, 2022. (Image credit: NASA/JHUAPL) "ESA's Hera mission has arrived to learn the answers we need to know," the mission's principal investigator Patrick Michel said in an ESA statement . "How did the impact change Dimorphos? What is the mass of the asteroid and which of its properties explain its response to DART impact? "Hera is carrying out a thorough investigation ever of a deflected asteroid, packed with scientific firsts, to give us a complete and unbiased picture of humankind's first planetary defense test." A view of Didymos from ESA's Hera spacecraft. (Image credit: ESA) ESA has already shared some of the remarkable images Hera has captured en route to Didymos, including a breathtaking image of both asteroids as Dimorphos cast its shadow on its larger companion in a deep-space double-asteroid solar eclipse . Hera even stopped by Mars on its way to the asteroids, snapping pictures of its moon Deimos . The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos. (Image credit: ESA) Hera will remain at the Didymos-Dimorphos system for months, deploying cubesats that will study the asteroids with visible and infrared light cameras and radar instruments. (Image credit: NASA/JHUAPL) "ESA's Hera mission has arrived to learn the answers we need to know," the mission's principal investigator Patrick Michel said in an ESA statement . "How did the impact change Dimorphos? What is the mass of the asteroid and which of its properties explain its response to DART impact? "Hera is carrying out a thorough investigation ever of a deflected asteroid, packed with scientific firsts, to give us a complete and unbiased picture of humankind's first planetary defense test." A view of Didymos from ESA's Hera spacecraft. (Image credit: ESA) ESA has already shared some of the remarkable images Hera has captured en route to Didymos, including a breathtaking image of both asteroids as Dimorphos cast its shadow on its larger companion in a deep-space double-asteroid solar eclipse . item.title: Debian wakes up wearing Windows XP's actual skin
item.description: Win4Wine is one of the more remarkable and creative hacks we've read about in recent years. It runs Windows XP's genuine Explorer shell through patched Wine on Debian 13, with a custom window manager integrating Linux applications into the desktop. As its GitHub repository explains: "The taskbar, Start menu, desktop and folder windows are XP's real ones, and Linux applications get XP's frames and taskbar buttons." This impressive, possibly demented project has English installation instructions and a README, although its design documents are in Japanese. We found Mozilla's built-in translation handled those pretty well. Its developer goes by miKuta0407 on GitHub, their homepage , and X . Also note, you're going to need some Windows installation media for the full experience. The README says: "No Microsoft files are included. Only the files that are needed are extracted locally from your own ISO." It supports Windows XP Professional SP3 installation images in 32-bit Japanese or English editions, with an experimental option for Windows 7 SP1 x64. Without either Windows image, it can download and use ReactOS's free software shell instead, for what it terms "a Windows 2000-like classic look." In our view, that sounds much better anyway. Before any former Windows users cry hurray and reach for an optical drive, this is not some ready-to-run project. The top of the README warns: "This is a personal, experimental project, not a finished product for daily use." The developer has tested it only on a fresh Debian 13 installation and recommends a VM or spare machine, rather than an existing working desktop, which sounds like an excellent precaution to us. Also, before you ask, yes, it was vibe-coded with Claude. We found ourselves reminded of another crazy-but-is-it project that we wrote about back in January: What if Linux ran Windows... and meant it? Meet Loss32 . The Loss32 proposal was even more extreme. It suggested replacing essentially the entire Linux userland, so it would be a Linux kernel running Wine with a Windows desktop and Windows apps. However, Mikuta-san was way ahead of us – lower down, the README mentions and even links to Loss32. Saying that, since it launched at the end of 2025, the bottom of the Loss32 web page shows a couple of updates, reporting on delays in getting it working. That, to be honest, did not shock us, but we still admire the let's-do-this spirit. The developer also seems to have got slightly distracted by a previous project, touchHLE: high-level emulator for early iOS apps . Loss32, in turn, reminded us of Neptune OS, an attempt to give seL4 a Windows personality transplant . We wrote about that back in 2022, and work on it has continued: the project page shows updates in recent months. The team has also pushed out preview releases in 2022, 2024, 2025, and most recently in September. This OS face transplant also reminded us of our article, Classic 7 is Windows 10 LTSC cosplaying as Windows 7 . Some people really miss the

item.title: Astronomers discover the most distant and ancient supermassive black hole-powered quasar in the universe
item.description: null The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun. The supermassive black hole is seen as it was just 630 million years after the Big Bang. 40 million years further back in time than the previous record holder for the most ancient quasar. The discovery further deepens the mystery of how supermassive black holes grew so massive so soon into the history of the universe. That's because previously, scientists had theorized it should take 1 billion years of feeding and merging for black holes to reach supermassive status of millions or billions of times as massive as the sun. Quasars occur when supermassive black holes are surrounded by vast amounts of gas and dust on which they feed. The immense gravitational influence of the black hole causes this material, in the form of an accretion disk, to glow brightly and to blast out bright jets of plasma. That means quasars at the heart of galaxies in regions called active galactic nuclei (AGNs) like this one can often be brighter than the combined light of every star in the entire surrounding galaxy, but only briefly. The newly discovered quasar, designated J1504+6252 and nicknamed Dún Aonghasa, is in this brief phase of its existence. It was discovered among millions of objects in 18 months of data from Euclid. Euclid's initial observation of Dún Aonghasa was followed up by an array of ground-based and space-based telescopes, including the W.M. Keck Observatory, the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory, the Hubble Space Telescope , and ultimately the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). It was the JWST that determined the mass of this supermassive black hole. What is interesting about Dún Aonghasa is that it is unlike other supermassive black holes seen at a similar period of the early universe. That's because this black hole is feeding relatively slowly. That means if it engaged in rapid feeding to reach its massive size, that period of gorging on gas and dust has either ended or it has paused. The red dot at the center of this Euclid image is Dún Aonghasa (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, Wolf et al. 2026) That is something that further complicates our picture of supermassive black hole growth. By staring back 13.1 billion years in time to see Dún Aonghasa, Euclid is also observing a crucial time in cosmic history when the first stars and galaxies were taking shape, and the clearing of cosmic gas was ending the dark ages of our universe by allowing light to travel freely. Euclid's primary mission is improving our understanding of dark energy , the mysterious force accelerating the expansion of the universe, and dark matter , the most mysterious "stuff" in the cosmos. Collectively, these aspects of the universe account for around 95% of its matter-energy budget and have come to be collectively referred to as the dark universe. Hence Euclid's nickname

The team's research was published on Tuesday (Nov. 24) in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.

item.title: Senegal regaining Afcon title is the right end to fiasco but issues do not stop there | Osasu Obayiuwana
item.description: After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governance A journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history. As the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee member Samir Sobha told the Guardian, the decision of the organisation’s appeals board in March to overturn Senegal’s victory and award the title to Morocco, prompting a legal charade ended by the court of arbitration for sport’s verdict on Tuesday , was a “big joke” that brought Caf and the Afcon into needless disrepute. Continue reading...

item.title: Microsoft 365 Backup stretches recovery window to ten years
item.description: Recovery windows of up to ten years are now available in Microsoft 365 Backup for OneDrive and SharePoint, up from a previous maximum of two. The change took effect on October 31, though Exchange remains capped at two years. Administrators can select recovery windows of three months, six months, or any whole number of years from one to ten. Microsoft's list price is $0.15 per GiB per month of protected content. Extended windows can increase costs by keeping deleted data billable for longer. Switching to a longer recovery window will also not make backups for that period magically available. So no nostalgic trips back to 2016. Wider recovery windows may appeal to organizations that need access to older data, but backups are not a substitute for compliance retention and archiving. Recovery after a breach or ransomware attack is also critical, particularly getting back to a healthy state before any malware seeped into files. Microsoft says backups are physically redundant and geographically replicated while respecting the tenant's data residency requirements. Full OneDrive account and SharePoint site restores offer recovery points every ten minutes for the most recent two weeks, then weekly points through the configured window, up to ten years. Individual file and folder recovery is limited to recovery points from the most recent 14 days, regardless of the configured window. Restore remains free, which is handy since regular testing is a vital part of any disaster recovery plan. The arrival of a ten-year recovery window is good for enterprises that need it and have deep enough pockets. However, it is important to keep in mind that being able to configure a longer recovery window doesn't constitute a disaster recovery plan in itself and may be overkill in many instances. Microsoft notes: "The existing one-year default recovery window remains unchanged. Longer recovery windows must be configured on the applicable backup policies." The company also recommends that users "review your organization's SharePoint and OneDrive backup requirements to determine whether longer recovery windows are needed." A decade of recovery history could be valuable. It also means a decade of data to account for when setting budgets, access controls, and retention policies. ®

Recovery after a breach or ransomware attack is also critical, particularly getting back to a healthy state before any malware seeped into files. Microsoft says backups are physically redundant and geographically replicated while respecting the tenant's data residency requirements. Full OneDrive account and SharePoint site restores offer recovery points every ten minutes for the most recent two weeks, then weekly points through the configured window, up to ten years. Individual file and folder recovery is limited to recovery points from the most recent 14 days, regardless of the configured window. Restore remains free, which is handy since regular testing is a vital part of any disaster recovery plan. The arrival of a ten-year recovery window is good for enterprises that need it and have deep enough pockets. However, it is important to keep in mind that being able to configure a longer recovery window doesn't constitute a disaster recovery plan in itself and may be overkill in many instances. Microsoft notes: "The existing one-year default recovery window remains unchanged. Longer recovery windows must be configured on the applicable backup policies." The company also recommends that users "review your organization's SharePoint and OneDrive backup requirements to determine whether longer recovery windows are needed." A decade of recovery history could be valuable. It also means a decade of data to account for when setting budgets, access controls, and retention policies. ®

item.title: ‘It threw me off my bowling a bit’: Isobel Goodwin living dream after England callup
item.description: London City striker, who was playing tenpin bowling when Wiegman called, says her journey has not been easy Not many phone calls are important enough to justify Isobel Goodwin missing her turn in a game of tenpin bowling. The England head coach ringing to tell her of a first senior international call-up qualified as an exception for the overjoyed London City Lionesses striker. After scoring with a pin-point finish at the Emirates this month under the gaze of Sarina Wiegman, Goodwin had been hotly tipped to be given a chance with the Lionesses and she is now eager to impress as the squad prepare to face Ukraine in their World Cup qualifying playoff. Continue reading...

item.title: Amazon to flog motors in Britain, but Prime won't deliver
item.description: Amazon is channeling its inner car salesman as it prepares to flog motors on the UK arm of its online tat bazaar. Amazon Autos will launch in Britain in early 2027, its first expansion outside the US, where it debuted in December 2024. Customers can browse and reserve cars online before completing the purchase with a dealer. Hoping it will be "a nice little earner," Amazon will let punters view real-time dealer inventory, prices, get an instant trade-in valuation, and connect with a local dealer to reserve a car, "all on Amazon." In the US, the service now covers more than 150 cities and offers vehicles from 35 brands. Hyundai is the first announced UK carmaker partner, while dealer group Vertu Motors will list used vehicles. More brands and dealers are due to be confirmed before launch. Hyundai's launch range will include electric, hybrid, and petrol models. "Buying a car is one of the biggest purchases people make, and we think it should feel as simple and transparent as shopping for anything on Amazon," said Matt Nuffort, director of Amazon Autos International. Of course, buying a car isn't quite like adding an air fryer or a memory stick to your basket. How does financing and checkout work for UK buyers? Customers will complete the purchase and paperwork at their chosen dealership. Amazon is not offering financing itself, but buyers can explore financing options via the site, adjusting terms like deposit and duration to see how monthly payments change. Credit applications must be completed with the dealer. In the US, buyers can submit a credit application through the platform, review terms and conditions, then sign electronic contracts online. They typically pay a deposit and visit the dealership to complete the remaining paperwork and pick up the vehicle. Buyers shouldn't expect their new car to arrive in an enormous cardboard box with a smiley logo on it, or to be lowered onto their driveway by a giant Amazon delivery drone. But given that one of the online retailer's flying delivery robots crashed into someone's garage after making a drop-off near Detroit last week, perhaps that's for the best. ®

item.title: Cardi B Wears Nigerian Designers Weiz Dhurm Franklyn & Sevon Dejana for Billboard Canada Cover
item.description: Cardi B in Nigerian Designers Sevon Dejana and Weiz Dhurm Franklyn for Billboard Canada Cardi B ‘s latest fashion moment comes with a lovely Nigerian connection, and we have two designers to celebrate! The rapper is the newest cover star of Billboard Canada, following her recognition as the inaugural Global Woman of the Year at the 2026 Billboard Canada Women in Music ceremony in Toronto on 24 November 2026. For the accompanying editorial, her longtime creative collaborator Kollin Carter worked with photographer AB+DM Studio to put together a series of looks, including two gorgeous creations from Nigerian fashion houses Weiz Dhurm Franklyn and Sevon Dejana. And BNers, both designers brought something very different to the spread. First up is a sculptural blue mermaid gown by Abelia Anaba Franklyn , the creative mind behind Weiz Dhurm Franklyn. The design comes from the brand’s Spring/Summer 2027 Ready-to-Wear collection, The Remembering (Ncheta), which draws inspiration from the artistry of ancient Igbo-Ukwu bronze works. Its fitted silhouette is covered in painterly blue textures across the bodice and hips, while an exaggerated organza ruffle frames the neckline and reappears at the hem. The layered, feather-like finish gives the gown an almost sculptural quality, making it a particularly interesting interpretation of the collection’s inspiration. Cardi B wears a sculptural blue mermaid gown from Nigerian fashion house Weiz Dhurm Franklyn’s Spring/Summer 2027 Ready-to-Wear collection, The Remembering (Ncheta), for her Billboard Canada editorial. Photo Credit: Weiz Dhurm Franklyn/Instagram Then comes Sevon Dejana, with a two-piece couture creation from the label’s Out of Body Haute Couture Spring/Summer 2027 collection. Cardi wears a structured, high-neck jacket with long sleeves and a matching skirt, both covered in intricate gold, red and wine-coloured crystals. Three-dimensional crimson floral details add another layer to the design, while a towering floral headpiece completes the look. Set against a lush botanical backdrop, the entire styling leans into the collection’s dramatic, otherworldly direction. Cardi B wears a crystal-embroidered structured jacket and skirt from Nigerian designer Sevon Dejana’s Out of Body Haute Couture Spring/Summer 2027 collection for Billboard Canada. Photo Credit: Sevon Dejana/Instagram Of course, there’s more to Cardi’s Billboard Canada cover story than the fashion. The Grammy-winning rapper also gets candid about life as a mother of four , working through self-doubt and making history with her sold-out Little Miss Drama arena tour across North America. Looking back on a year that has included the release of her chart-topping second album, Am I the Drama? , and new business ventures, she tells the magazine that the past twelve months have reminded her of who she is. The post Cardi B Wears Nigerian Designers Weiz Dhurm Franklyn & Sevon Dejana for Billboard Canada Cover appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Af

item.title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
item.description: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics. LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online. The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI. Read full article Comments

item.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
item.description: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early. The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered. Continue reading...

item.title: November's full moon dazzles skywatchers with a stunning Beaver Moon supermoon (photos)
item.description: null The November full moon rose to put on a spectacular natural light show on Nov. 24 and we've got the photos to prove it! Read on to see our favorite shots of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world. Each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names , often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising. The November moon is often known as the Beaver Moon, a name associated with the time of year when beavers prepare for winter and when trappers historically set beaver traps before waterways froze. November's full moon served as the opening salvo in a series of four dazzling supermoons , which turn full around the time that the natural satellite passes closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit. That added proximity can make it appear noticeably brighter and larger than the smallest full moon of the year, setting the stage for an incredible photo shoot as the lunar disk climbed high into the autumn sky. Best photos of the November 2026 full Beaver Moon Our first shot of the moon was captured by photographer Pongmanat Tasiri as the moon rose over the roof of the Wat Phra That Doi Suthep Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, as a stunning array of craters and lunar seas scar the Beaver Moon's surface. The Beaver Moon takes flight into the night sky. (Image credit: Photo by Pongmanat Tasiri/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) Meanwhile, Gary Hershorn snapped a gorgeous shot of the full yellow moon rising over the Chrysler Building in New York, with the Empire State Building and myriad other skyscrapers dominating the skyline. The Beaver Moon rises over the New York skyline. (Image credit: Photo by Gary Hershorn/Getty Images) Hershorn also managed to line up a colorful shot of the lunar disk glowing between the concrete canyon of New York's iconic 42nd Street just before moonset on the morning of Nov. 24, mere hours before the moon turned full. The moon shines between a concrete canyon in New York. (Image credit: Photo by Gary Hershorn/Getty Images) NASA astronaut Anil Menon snapped a series of stunning photos from the International Space Station on Nov. 24, November full moon slipped out of view below Earth's horizon, while being gradually deformed by the warping effect of our planet's atmosphere. "Moonset today from space station - no edits to these photos from 400mm lens," Menon wrote in a post on X . A composite image of 4 full moon photos captured by NASA astronaut Anil Menon from aboard the International Space Station. (Image credit: NASA/Anil Menon, created by Anthony Wood in Canva) Heading back down to Earth Salih Zeki Fazlioglu took a colorful photo of the Beaver moon illuminating a thin veil of clouds above Istanbul, Turkiye, as reflected sunlight competed with the artificial glow of the city below for the viewer's attention. Moonrise over Isatanbul. (Image credit: Photo by Salih Zeki Fazlioglu/Anadolu via Getty Images) This shot of the lunar disk looming over the Old P

item.content:encoded: null The November full moon rose to put on a spectacular natural light show on Nov. 24 and we've got the photos to prove it! Read on to see our favorite shots of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world. Each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names , often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising. The November moon is often known as the Beaver Moon, a name associated with the time of year when beavers prepare for winter and when trappers historically set beaver traps before waterways froze.
